title: Dynamic Governance of Multi-LLM Agent Systems for Collaborative Conversational Outcomes
summary: This research explores dynamic governance mechanisms for multi-LLM agent systems to achieve collaborative conversational outcomes, especially when agents have opposing objectives.

title: A Forced-Structure Reduction and Verifiable Bounds for Conway's 99-Graph
summary: This paper details a systematic and reproducible approach by an autonomous AI research agent to investigate Conway's 99-graph problem, contributing verifiable bounds and reductions.

title: Detecting a Route Flip Is Easier Than Knowing Whether to Fix It: Causal Route-Mediated Damage in Quantized Mixture-of-Experts
summary: This research investigates causal route-mediated damage in quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, demonstrating how numerical disturbances can affect expert routing.

title: Poor Man's Agentic Modeling: Simulating Large LLM-Agent Societies on a Laptop
summary: This paper presents a method for 'poor man's agentic modeling,' enabling the simulation of large societies of LLM agents efficiently on a laptop for macroscopic observations.

title: AutoWorldModel-Bench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Automated World-Model Research
summary: This paper introduces AutoWorldModel-Bench, a new state-centric benchmark designed for automated world-model research and testing AI coding agents as autonomous researchers.

title: From Monolithic to Modular: Segment-level Automatic Prompt Optimization
summary: This research introduces Segment-level Automatic Prompt Optimization (SAPO), a modular method that decomposes prompts to apply targeted improvements, aiming to overcome limitations of monolithic prompt rewriting.

title: LLMs in Process Diagram Engineering: From Optimal PFDs to Validated P&IDs
summary: This paper explores the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate and optimize process diagram engineering, from creating optimal Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs) to validated Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs).

title: Harnessing agent memory to build lifelong AI partners for materials scientists
summary: This research focuses on harnessing agent memory to create lifelong AI partners for materials scientists, facilitating the accumulation and transfer of research experience and knowledge.

title: Identity from the Outside: A Conceptual Framework and Research Program for AI Personality Clones
summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework and research program for AI personality clones, prompting a re-examination of personal identity from an external perspective.

title: Cutting AI Datacenter Energy with Reinforcement Learning: Measured Power Control of LLM Training from One GPU to the Fleet
summary: This research demonstrates how reinforcement learning can be used to control power on GPUs, significantly cutting energy consumption in AI datacenters during LLM training.

title: Forecasting Side Effects of Activation Steering
summary: This research investigates how 'activation steering' modifies language models, highlighting the challenge of unintended side effects and the need for safe deployment.

title: LinearKV: One Cached State Suffices for Position-Independent Caching in Hybrid LLMs
summary: This paper introduces LinearKV, a new method for position-independent caching to accelerate LLM serving by optimizing KV cache management in full-attention models.

title: InfraBench: Evaluating Infrastructure Agents Across Layers, Lifecycle, and Risk
summary: InfraBench is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating AI infrastructure agents, assessing their ability to automate complex infrastructure management tasks across various layers and risks.

title: CORA-Diff: Confidence-Oriented Residual Acceptance for Efficient Diffusion Language Model Inference
summary: CORA-Diff proposes a method to improve the efficiency of Diffusion Language Model inference by addressing fixed denoising horizons and optimizing blockwise decoding processes.

title: Geometry-aware Incremental Neural Operator for Long-Horizon PDE prediction
summary: This paper presents a geometry-aware incremental neural operator for long-horizon prediction of partial differential equations, addressing issues like error accumulation and spectral inconsistency.

title: Towards Query-Agnostic RAG Evaluation via Query Coverage and Claim Verifiability
summary: This research proposes new evaluation methods, including query coverage and claim verifiability, to improve the consistent and fine-grained assessment of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.

title: VQ-bench: A Composable Vector Quantization Framework
summary: VQ-bench is presented as a unified framework for developing and benchmarking vector quantization algorithms, which are crucial for AI infrastructure efficiency.

title: RecSys Factory: Bounding LLM Agent Autonomy to Decision Points in the Industrial Recommender Lifecycle
summary: This paper discusses the autonomy-determinism-efficiency trilemma when deploying LLM agents in industrial recommender systems and focuses on bounding their autonomy to decision points.

title: The Off-Support Barrier: Why Semantic Safety Constraints Are Not Learning-Problem Invariants, and What Follows for Prior Design, Containment, and Verification
summary: This paper argues that semantic safety constraints in AI are 'off-support objects,' impacting prior design, containment, and verification in the field of AI safety.

title: BEST-KAG: Enhancing Question Answering of Building Engineering Standards with Multimodal Knowledge Graph Modeling and Large Language Model
summary: BEST-KAG enhances question answering for building engineering standards using multimodal knowledge graph modeling and large language models for multi-clause reasoning and multimodal knowledge.

title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
summary: AI Tutor, a reinforcement learning-based model, is introduced to enhance engagement and long-term learning effectiveness in online education.

title: Towards the Harness of Embodied Agents
summary: This paper explores the 'harness' paradigm for embodied agents operating in the physical world, introducing Thea as an agentic loop infrastructure for such systems.

title: Conformity Mitigations in Large Language Models Lie on a Single Resistance-Receptivity Frontier
summary: This research investigates conformity mitigations in large language models, analyzing how peer opinion influences model outputs in collaborative settings.

title: EvoGraph-Mem: Failure-Aware Editable Graph Memory for Long-Term Language Agents
summary: EvoGraph-Mem is introduced as a failure-aware editable graph memory system designed to provide long-term memory for language agents and address memory degradation.

title: AgonAlpha: Autonomous Alpha Discovery via Prompt Economy and Scalable Agentic Search
summary: AgonAlpha is an architecture for autonomous research systems that discovers trading factors through prompt economy and scalable agentic search, including budget allocation and evidence verification.

title: Local verification cannot detect non-transportability: a cohomological theory of context preservation in agentic reasoning
summary: This paper presents a cohomological theory arguing that local verification is insufficient to detect non-transportability in agentic reasoning, raising concerns about context preservation and safeguards.

title: Symbolic Machine Learning for Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium Prediction in Cx-N2 Binary Mixtures
summary: This research explores the use of symbolic machine learning for accurate prediction of vapor-liquid equilibrium in hydrocarbon-nitrogen binary mixtures, offering interpretability lacking in deep learning models.

title: Glance, Scrutinize, and Think: Advancing Video Anomaly Detection from Training-Free to Agentic Reasoning
summary: This work advances video anomaly detection by proposing agentic reasoning to improve semantic understanding, moving beyond the limitations of traditional DNN and LLM-based methods.

title: Apodex Discovery: Reality Benchmarks and Environments for Evaluating and Building Discoverative Artificial Intelligence
summary: Apodex Discovery calls for 'reality benchmarks and environments' to effectively evaluate and develop 'Discoverative Artificial Intelligence,' drawing parallels with the Apollo mission's success.

title: Can Frontier LLMs Match Natively Multimodal Embeddings? A Comparison on Hard-Negative Text-to-Image Retrieval
summary: This paper compares frontier LLMs with natively multimodal embeddings on hard-negative text-to-image retrieval tasks, referencing Google's Gemini Embedding 2, to evaluate their respective capabilities.

title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces
summary: This paper proposes an "Inverse Theory of Mind" modeling approach for content recommendation systems, particularly for dynamic and generative user interfaces and extended reality. It addresses the challenge of understanding user preferences from observed actions.

title: From Numbers to Judgment: Specialist LLM Agents and Reinforcement Learning for European Listed Real Estate
summary: This research investigates the use of specialist LLM agents and reinforcement learning for financial analysis of European listed real estate. It introduces Larix, which maps an analysis framework to eight lens-aligned specialist agents.

title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs
summary: This paper evaluates the "self-consistency via majority vote" technique for small LLMs on the GPQA Diamond benchmark for science questions. It finds that this method surprisingly reduces per-problem accuracy for a majority of hard science problems.

title: Social Chain of Thought: A Multi-Agent Architecture Grounded in Medical Differential Diagnosis Methodology
summary: This research proposes "Social Chain of Thought," a multi-agent architecture grounded in medical differential diagnosis methodology. It applies LLM-based agentic systems to medical diagnostic reasoning, a high-impact healthcare use case.

title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces MobileJudgeBench, a new benchmark for systematically evaluating the reliability of LLM-as-judge methods in mobile agent evaluation. It addresses the increasing reliance on LLM-based judges for assessing task completion.

title: A Modular Agentic Framework for Synthetically Constrained Multi-Objective Hit-to-Lead Optimization
summary: This paper presents SABLE (Synthetically-accessible Agentic Bayesian Ligand Exploration), an open-source modular agentic framework for hit-to-lead optimization in drug discovery. The framework iteratively designs hit analogs considering various constraints.

title: From Prompting to Behavioral Alignment: Personalized LLM Judges for Recommendation Evaluation
summary: This research explores using personalized LLM judges as an evaluation method for recommendation systems. It proposes LLMs as an alternative to traditional feature pipelines for predicting user engagement from raw text logs.

title: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates the localization of safety alignment within large language models, identifying that refusal behavior is encoded in specific MLP layers and mid-network blocks. It sheds light on the internal mechanisms of AI safety.

title: EnterpriseRAG: Benchmarking LLM Instruction Adherence and Robustness under Non-Ideal Enterprise Retrieval
summary: This paper introduces EnterpriseRAG, a new benchmark designed to measure LLM instruction adherence and robustness under non-ideal enterprise retrieval conditions. It highlights a significant "orchestration gap" in current RAG deployments.

title: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications
summary: This paper introduces CoAdapt-GUI, a test-time adaptation framework for improving the generalization of mobile GUI agents to unseen applications. It focuses on joint workflow context and policy adaptation for agents.

title: Learning from Online User Feedback for Shopping Agents
summary: This research explores methods for improving large language model-based shopping agents by learning from online user feedback generated on e-commerce platforms. It contrasts with existing approaches that rely on offline training signals.

title: Foresight Without Seeing: Latent Futures for World Action Models
summary: This paper introduces "Latent Futures for World Action Models (WAMs)" which couple future visual prediction with robot action generation. These models enable robotic policies to simulate and understand how the physical world evolves during interaction.

title: MBA: Multimodal Benchmark and Agents for Real-World Business Ideation
summary: This paper introduces MBA-Bench, the first multimodal benchmark designed for evaluating agentic systems in real-world business ideation contexts. It addresses the limitation of existing text-only approaches for LLM-powered agents.

title: Making AI-Generated Feedback Matter: From Provision to Student Enactment
summary: This research explores how to make AI-generated feedback more effective for student learning, focusing on both providing high-quality feedback at scale and supporting students to act on it. It applies generative AI to educational feedback processes.

title: CLAIM: Leading Open-domain Active Clarification of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Measurement
summary: This paper introduces "CLAIM," a method for open-domain active clarification in large language models using uncertainty measurement. It enables LLMs to ask clarifying questions for ambiguous user queries, improving response quality in human-computer interaction.

title: XBridge: Entity-Grounded Latent Bridge for Heterogeneous LLM Communication
summary: This paper introduces XBridge, an entity-grounded latent bridge for communication within heterogeneous multi-agent LLM systems. It aims to improve inter-agent communication by preserving internal representations, allowing different model families to interact more effectively.

title: AgenticTwin: An Agentic LLM Framework Integrated with Digital Twin for Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper introduces AgenticTwin, an agentic LLM framework integrated with digital twin technology for anomaly detection in cyber-physical systems. It aims to simplify the interpretation of complex sensor data for operators.

title: FrontierFinance: A Challenging Benchmark for Measuring Frontier Intelligence of Finance Agents
summary: This paper introduces FrontierFinance, a challenging new benchmark designed to measure the frontier intelligence of AI finance agents. It aims to capture the full complexity of investment research workflows, moving beyond simple financial data extraction.

title: HUGIN: Enhancing Vision-Language Planning for Autonomous Logistics Sorting
summary: This paper introduces HUGIN, a system designed to enhance vision-language planning for autonomous logistics sorting systems. It applies embodied AI and joint multi-scene understanding to industrial automation tasks requiring complex planning.

title: Making Your LLMs More Objective: Stabilizing LLM Safety Behavior Across Traits with Trait-Invariant Safety Tuning
summary: This research proposes "Trait-Invariant Safety Tuning" to stabilize large language model safety behavior, ensuring consistent refusal of unsafe requests across different traits. It addresses the issue of varying safety decisions for the same request.

title: HyperANFIS: Enhancing Rule Representation and Interpretability in Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Systems via Hyperbolic Geometry
summary: This paper introduces HyperANFIS, an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system that uses hyperbolic geometry to enhance rule representation and interpretability.

title: FarSky: Task-Aware Latent-Space Coupling for Generative Intra-Hour Solar Forecasting
summary: This research presents FarSky, a deep learning approach utilizing task-aware latent-space coupling for generative intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting.

title: Why AI Detection Fails for Academic Integrity
summary: This study quantifies the failure of commercial AI detectors in distinguishing AI editing from full LLM drafts, leading to potential academic misconduct misidentification.

title: Federated Learning for Distributed CNC Tool Wear Prediction
summary: This research explores the application of federated learning for distributed tool wear prediction in CNC machining environments to improve accuracy and reliability.

title: Contextual Quality-Diversity Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control in Tropical Commercial Buildings
summary: This paper proposes CQD-ERL, a contextual quality-diversity evolutionary reinforcement-learning controller for supervisory HVAC system control in tropical commercial buildings.

title: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Complete Financial Statements with Forma
summary: This research introduces a method for long-horizon financial statement forecasting, demonstrating specialist training superiority and releasing the ProForma-20Q benchmark.

title: Weightless Fine-Tuning: Personalizing LLMs via Logit-Space Transport
summary: This paper proposes Weightless Fine-Tuning (WFT), a new method for personalizing LLMs by adapting them to target distributions without prohibitive costs of traditional SFT.

title: Dynamics Models for Offline Hyperparameter Selection in Real-World RL
summary: This research addresses hyperparameter selection in real-world reinforcement learning by proposing calibration models trained on offline data to approximate environment dynamics.

title: Market-Information-Aware Gated-LoRA of Foundation Models for Transferable Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting
summary: This paper presents a method utilizing market-information-aware Gated-LoRA with foundation models to achieve transferable day-ahead electricity price forecasting.

title: Lifecycle-Optimal Tokenization: Vocabulary Size as a Deployment-Regime-Dependent Infrastructure Parameter
summary: This research demonstrates that the optimal tokenizer vocabulary size for Large Language Models is dynamic, depending on the serving regime rather than being a fixed design choice.

title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR
summary: This research introduces PAIR, a method for adaptive rollout allocation in Reinforcement Learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), to optimize compute resources for reasoning trajectories.

title: Unmasking Toxic Mimicry in Medical Offline Reinforcement Learning for ICU Sepsis Management via Counterfactual Clinical Audits
summary: This paper identifies "Toxic Mimicry," a failure mode in medical offline reinforcement learning for ICU sepsis management, and proposes counterfactual clinical audits to detect it.

title: Diffusion-Based Data-Driven Assortment Optimization
summary: This research applies diffusion models, a type of generative AI, to develop a data-driven approach for assortment optimization in revenue management.

title: Click2Poly: A VLM for vector mapping buildings and walls
summary: This introduces Click2Poly, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) specifically designed for accurate vector mapping of buildings and walls for geospatial applications.

title: AutoGrable: What Is a Good Graph for a Table?
summary: This research investigates methods for automatically generating optimal graph structures from tabular data, enabling effective application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).

title: XGBoost "is all you need": the case of forecasting transmitted heat energy in District Heating Systems
summary: This paper conducts a comparative study between XGBoost and LSTM for forecasting transmitted heat energy in District Heating Systems, identifying scenarios where conventional ML excels.

title: Dual-Primal Graph VAEs for Noisy Label Aggregation
summary: This paper introduces Dual-Primal Graph VAEs as a neural network-based method for accurately inferring ground-truth from noisy crowdsourced labels.

title: Convergence Guarantees of Gradient Descent for Neural Networks via Generalized Lipschitz Smoothness
summary: This theoretical paper establishes convergence guarantees for gradient descent in general feedforward neural networks, assuming only Lipschitz properties of activation functions.

title: Defending against Model Extraction for GNNs with Model Reprogramming
summary: This research proposes Model Reprogramming as a defense mechanism to protect Graph Neural Networks from Model Extraction attacks in Machine-Learning-as-a-Service environments.

title: RelShap: Relationally Consistent Shapley Explanations
summary: This paper introduces RelShap, a method for generating relationally consistent Shapley explanations for machine learning models that handle relational data by preserving structural constraints. It addresses the issue of feature independence assumptions in traditional Shapley value attributions.

title: Let it Cook: Learning to Wait in Sequential Decision Making
summary: This research proposes "Let it Cook," a method for sequential decision-making where an agent learns to strategically wait, allowing the environment to evolve without constant intervention. This approach is applied to tasks where continuous action is not always necessary.

title: Robust Ambiguity Detection (RAD) From Model- and Feature-Space Consistency
summary: This paper introduces Robust Ambiguity Detection (RAD), a method for evaluating the robustness of machine learning models by assessing their predictive consistency under permissible variations in model or feature space. It aims to identify when model predictions remain unchanged despite minor perturbations.

title: When Offline Evaluation Misleads: A Diagnostic Protocol for Reward and Policy Selection in Delayed-Feedback Contextual Bandits
summary: This research proposes a diagnostic protocol to address issues arising from offline evaluation and proxy rewards in delayed-feedback contextual bandit systems, particularly for tasks like personalizing marketing messages. It aims to improve reward and policy selection in such scenarios.

title: Sparse and robust geometric twin support vector machine via asymmetric RoBoSS loss function
summary: This paper introduces a sparse and robust geometric twin support vector machine that utilizes an asymmetric RoBoSS loss function. The new method is designed to handle redundant features, label noise, and feature noise in training data more effectively than standard SVMs.

title: RECAST: A Machine-Learning Framework for Correction and Super-Resolution of Coarse-Grid PDE Solvers
summary: This paper introduces RECAST, a machine learning framework for recurrent error correction and super-resolution of coarse-grid PDE solvers. It aims to improve the accuracy and spatial fidelity of solutions from computationally efficient coarse-grid simulations.

title: A Local Sinkhorn Framework for Conditional Distribution Reconstruction of Multidimensional Random Fields
summary: This paper proposes a local Sinkhorn divergence framework for the conditional distribution reconstruction of multidimensional random fields. The approach uses debiased Sinkhorn divergence to create a differentiable and computationally efficient local distribution matching objective.

title: FM-LLM: A frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for adapting LLMs to time series forecasting
summary: This paper introduces FM-LLM, a frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework designed to adapt Large Language Models for time series forecasting. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods by leveraging spectral dynamics rather than relying heavily on textual prompts.

title: Transferable Above-Ground Biomass (AGB) Estimation Model from Multi-Sensor Data with Sparse Field Calibration
summary: This research develops a transferable model for estimating above-ground biomass (AGB) using multi-sensor data with sparse field calibration. This AI application aims to provide spatially continuous quantification of forest AGB for carbon accounting.

title: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models
summary: This paper introduces continuous-latent predictive modeling with semantic alignment for developing EEG-language foundation models. The method aims to enhance generalizable neural decoding across subjects and datasets, addressing challenges in existing pretraining paradigms.

title: Is Per-Agent Policy Composition Safe? Rethinking Successor-Feature Transfer in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research investigates the safety of per-agent policy composition in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, rethinking successor-feature transfer. It addresses the challenge of dynamically changing objectives in deployed RL systems without expensive retraining.

title: Low-Interaction-Rank Learning: Unifying Multiplicative Dual-Encoder Heads
summary: This paper proposes "Low-Interaction-Rank Learning" as a unifying framework for multiplicative dual-encoder networks, which compute real-valued outputs for input pairs. This architecture is relevant across various domains like operator learning and retrieval.

title: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
summary: This paper introduces "Rubric Dropout," a method designed to mitigate reward hacking in reinforcement learning scenarios where Large Language Models act as judges using rubrics for reward. It addresses limitations of fixed rubric-based proxies for quality.

title: GCPO: Diagnosing and Constraining Subspace Geometry in Rollout RL for LLMs
summary: This paper introduces GCPO, a method for diagnosing and constraining subspace geometry in rollout reinforcement learning for Large Language Models. It aims to address training instabilities, cross-task capability degradation, and response-length inflation in LLM post-training.

title: Drift and Dependence: Layer-wise Information-Theoretic Bounds for Replay-Based Continual Learning
summary: This research analyzes the generalization behavior of replay-based continual learning by proposing layer-wise information-theoretic bounds that account for drift and dependence. It provides a deeper understanding of how these systems mitigate catastrophic forgetting.

title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection
summary: This paper introduces LEMUR, a latent entropy-aware multimodal unlearning method that uses visual-anchored reasoning redirection to address privacy vulnerabilities in large multimodal reasoning models. It focuses on mitigating privacy risks introduced by RL post-training.

title: REOPD: Reliability-Adaptive Reward Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper introduces REOPD, a reliability-adaptive reward extrapolation method designed for on-policy distillation. It aims to improve student model training by dynamically adjusting reward amplification beyond the single global coefficient used in existing methods.

title: Consolidator: Learning Persistent Routed Memory Across Context Boundaries
summary: This research introduces "Consolidator," a mechanism for learning persistent routed memory across context boundaries within a Phasor Memory Network. It focuses on ensuring that retained state influences subsequent memory access, not just its persistence.

title: Robust and Efficient Noisy-Label Time-Series Classification via Dynamic Time Warping Based Granular Ball Computing
summary: This paper proposes DTW-based Granular Ball Computing (DTW-GBC) for robust and efficient time-series classification that is resilient to noisy labels. It aims to improve upon traditional Dynamic Time Warping-based nearest-neighbor classifiers.

title: Chain-of-Thought Shows the Path to a Tree: Realizing Branching Complexity
summary: This research explores how Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in Large Language Models can realize branching complexity, lifting the expressive ceiling of bounded-depth Transformers. It provides characterizations tying CoT steps to circuit complexity classes.

title: Epiplexity Guided Data Selection and Generation for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
summary: This research proposes Epiplexity Guided Data Selection and Generation as a method to improve the out-of-distribution generalization capabilities of modern AI systems. The focus is on selecting data that contains more structural information to facilitate better transfer across tasks.

title: MOON: Multi-Objective OrthoNormalized Updates for Multitask Learning
summary: This paper introduces MOON (Multi-Objective OrthoNormalized Updates), a novel method for multi-objective optimization in multitask learning. It aims to mitigate task conflicts by manipulating gradients under Euclidean geometry, improving how model parameters are updated.

title: TradingMoE: Routing the Right Experts in Evolving Markets
summary: TradingMoE is an LLM-based system designed for financial analysis and trading in evolving markets, utilizing a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. It focuses on routing the right experts to address the varying predictive capabilities required for different assets and market conditions.

title: High-Order Liquid Evidence Encoding for Gradual GNSS Spoofing Detection in Autonomous Driving
summary: This research proposes a High-Order Liquid Evidence Encoding method for detecting gradual GNSS spoofing attacks, which are crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. It aims to identify subtle manipulation of vehicle position estimates.

title: Orientation, not magnitude: the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models
summary: This paper investigates the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models, arguing that orientation rather than magnitude is key. It aims to diagnose why model merging by task arithmetic works and where it fails.

title: Backtrader-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Algorithmic Trading with Self-Generated MCQs
summary: Backtrader-Bench is a new framework designed to benchmark LLM coding agents in algorithmic trading using self-generated multiple-choice questions. It aims to overcome limitations of static benchmarks and numerical backtests.

title: Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets
summary: This research explores retrofitting recurrent depth into a specific pretrained language model, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, to study its effects on installation, extrapolation, transfer, and retention. It aims to enhance the model's capabilities without increasing its size significantly.

title: TRACE Bench: Task-driven Roleplay Agentic Checklist Evaluation
summary: TRACE Bench is a new task-driven agentic checklist evaluation framework designed for roleplay assessment. It aims to reveal which role requirements were tested, failed, and provide dialogue evidence to support the judgment.

title: Lost in Compaction: Evaluating Side-Constraint Loss under Context Compaction
summary: This research investigates the impact of context compaction on user-issued "Session Constraints" in LLM systems, which occurs when the context window is under pressure. It evaluates how these constraints are lost or maintained during context summarization.

title: Diffuse to Compress: Leveraging Diffusion LMs for Lossless Compression
summary: This paper introduces a method called "Diffuse to Compress" that leverages Diffusion Language Models for lossless text compression. The research is motivated by the growing need for efficient storage of digital textual data.

title: Gloss-Free Representation Learning for Cross-Dataset Sign Spotting
summary: This research explores gloss-free representation learning for cross-dataset sign spotting in sign language, aiming to overcome the limitations of resource-constrained languages. It uses broadcast news to pair continuous signing with spoken-language transcripts.

title: Better, Faster, Stronger: Programmatic Skill Learning Best Reduces Agent Cost
summary: This research investigates how programmatic skill learning can cost-effectively enhance LLM agent capabilities and adapt them to novel domains. It focuses on reducing agent operational costs through skill acquisition.

title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution
summary: This paper proposes a method for creating self-evolving embodied agents through "Skill-Harness Evolution." It focuses on adapting agents by refining their surrounding components like skills, context, action interfaces, and execution harness, rather than just model weights.

title: ODE-Based Transformer Decoders for Iterative Sign Language Translation
summary: This paper proposes a parameter-efficient alternative for sign language translation using ODE-Based Transformer Decoders. This method aims to improve the expressiveness of Transformer architectures without increasing model size or computational cost.

title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
summary: This research investigates the persistence of "unlearned" knowledge in large language models by forecasting the recovery of latent traces of information. It aims to understand if residual signals of unlearned data remain detectable.

title: Is Convergence Inevitable? Tracing Output Homogeneity Back to Base Models
summary: This paper investigates the origins of output homogeneity in language model content, arguing that the lack of diversity likely stems from the pretraining phase. It traces this phenomenon back through the model's development pipeline.

title: DonorRank: Donor Language Selection for Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Speech Recognition
summary: DonorRank is a novel method for selecting donor languages to improve low-resource cross-lingual automatic speech recognition (ASR). It addresses challenges arising from linguistic variation and evolving speech patterns in under-resourced communities.

title: Principal Trait Analysis: Towards Deriving "Skills" in Human-AI Collaboration
summary: This research introduces Principal Trait Analysis to derive "skills" and understand effective prompting traits for Large Language Model-powered agents in human-AI collaboration. It aims to identify key attributes contributing to task success in such partnerships.

title: Group Alignment-Induced Sycophancy: A Two-Sided Evaluation of Steerable Pluralistic Alignment
summary: This paper evaluates "group alignment-induced sycophancy" in language models, a phenomenon where models over-agree with users regardless of objective truth. It explores approaches to "steerable pluralistic alignment" to mitigate this ethical issue.

title: CT-$\Delta$Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal 3D Medical Imaging Difference Reporting with Vision-Language Models
summary: CT-ΔBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language Models for longitudinal 3D medical imaging difference reporting. It aims to assess how well models can describe disease evolution from serial CT scans.

title: Beyond Single-Turn Confidence: Trajectory-Adapted Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces trajectory-adapted uncertainty quantification methods for LLM agents, focusing on interactive scenarios where agents can ask clarifying questions and use tools. It addresses how uncertainty is measured across an agent's multi-step actions.

title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs
summary: This work proposes Self-Fix Step-DPO (SFS-DPO), a reinforcement learning framework designed to improve LLMs' ability to self-correct by enabling step-level self-verification and correction of their own mistakes.

title: Learning to Persuade Exposes How Easily LLMs Abandon Correct Beliefs
summary: This research investigates how large language models (LLMs) are susceptible to persuasion, demonstrating how easily they can abandon correct beliefs. It highlights concerns about LLMs' resistance to harmful persuasion in collaborative and advisory roles.

title: Easper: An Accessible ASR Pipeline for Language Documentation
summary: Easper is an open-source, no-code workflow designed to make multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) accessible for field linguists. It addresses the bottleneck of audio transcription in language documentation by providing an iterative solution.

title: Who Would You Vote For? Auditing Political Alignment in LLMs: An Italian Case-Study
summary: This paper examines the political alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically using an Italian case study, as users increasingly rely on them for political information. It highlights concerns about the political preferences expressed by these systems and their potential influence.

title: Semantic Lenia: Emergence of Homeostatic Solitons within the Semantic Space of Large Language Models
summary: This work introduces Semantic Lenia, an artificial life framework that re-conceptualizes LLM inference as a continuous dynamical system within the macroscopic logit space. It uses a non-linear homeostatic feedback loop to dynamically balance semantic information.

title: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing
summary: This paper introduces Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing, a method for composable unstructured knowledge editing in LLMs. It aims to update specific knowledge within an LLM to prevent it from becoming outdated, without requiring full model retraining.

title: The Wording Effect: Quantifying Two-Way Drift in LLM Benchmark Performance
summary: This research quantifies the "Wording Effect," demonstrating that rephrasing benchmark problems, even while maintaining meaning, can routinely alter an LLM's answer. It highlights how benchmark scores can be sensitive to the exact phrasing of questions.

title: When the API Speaks the Wrong Language: Revisiting Post-Training for Multilingual Tool Use
summary: This paper addresses the degradation of LLMs' API calling reliability in multilingual settings, specifically focusing on "Argument Language Mismatch" where tools are selected correctly but arguments are generated in inconsistent languages. It revisits post-training methods to improve multilingual tool use.

title: Locating and Controlling Implicit Personalization in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates implicit personalization in LLMs, where outputs shift based on unstated demographic cues. It aims to locate and control this behavior by connecting behavioral changes to the model's internal activations, addressing bias and fairness concerns.

title: Ripple-Pivot Search: Active Parallel Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Ripple-Pivot Search, an active parallel decoding method for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs). This technique aims to significantly speed up inference compared to autoregressive models by optimizing parallel decoding schedules.

title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
summary: LabelFusion-TS proposes fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and financial time series data for monetary-policy stance classification in financial text. It investigates the utility of financial time series as an additional input for classifying central bank communications.

title: AWARe: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting via Activation-Weighted Adaptive REtention
summary: AWARe is a proposed method aimed at mitigating catastrophic forgetting in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during fine-tuning on downstream tasks. It uses Activation-Weighted Adaptive Retention to prevent the degradation of previously acquired knowledge.

title: Causal Structure is Inducible but Functionally Decoupled: The Routing/Readout Boundary of a Typed Mechanism Library
summary: This paper investigates how transformer models organize causal knowledge, reporting a decoupling between slot-by-type structure that organizes routing and the functional readout. It explores the internal computational mechanisms of language models when answering interventional questions.

title: Language-Conditional Dequantization: Recovering What Quantization Steals from Non-English Languages
summary: This work proposes Language-Conditional Dequantization (LCD), a post-hoc method to recover multilingual capabilities lost during aggressive quantization of LLMs. It addresses the disproportionate perplexity degradation observed in non-English languages compared to English.

title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces GRPO, a method for generating actionable financial advice from business records, outperforming commercial LLMs in CATE evaluation. It emphasizes integrating numerical reasoning, domain knowledge, and sound judgment while avoiding harmful recommendations.

title: TELLME: Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment
summary: This study proposes TELLME (Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment), a new method to improve continual pre-training (CPT) for domain adaptation in LLMs. It aims to address challenges associated with acquiring large datasets and high computational costs in CPT.

title: Located but Not Releasable: Silent Gate Inversion and Bounded Linear Release
summary: This research investigates how language models represent task-relevant latent structure that they often fail to use, exploring whether this internal knowledge can be converted into observable behavior. It proposes a pipeline to detect, localize, and release such latent information.

title: Total Recall at What Cost? Benchmarking the Serving Cost of Agentic Memory Systems
summary: This paper benchmarks the serving cost of agentic memory systems, comparing solutions like Mem0, Hindsight, and Mastra Observational Memory. It analyzes the economic implications of using these systems for long-running conversational agents to manage context.

title: LazyTrain: Limited-resource Allocation toward Zero-waste Yield Optimization in Large Language Model Training
summary: LazyTrain addresses the challenge of training large language models on limited hardware by optimizing resource allocation for GPU compute, host memory, and data transfer. It proposes a solution for zero-waste yield optimization in LLM training scheduling.

title: LODESTAR: Trustworthy Entropy Is Navigated, Not Merely Measured -- Reinforced Polarizer Keeps a Frozen LLM from Being Confidently Misled by the Wrong Evidence
summary: This research proposes using predictive-distribution entropy as a selection rule in retrieval-augmented question answering (RAG) to improve trustworthiness. It shows that keeping candidate answers with the lowest answer-token entropy lifts mean answer F1 scores across five QA benchmarks.

title: Accuracy and Order Sensitivity Diverge Under Label-Free Strategies
summary: This paper investigates how multiple-choice benchmarks, widely used for evaluating large language models, can conflate model knowledge with sensitivity to option order, making them unreliable. It tests strategies to prevent models from seeing option labels to address this issue.

title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of SLMs: Pre-trained vs. Compressed
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking the trustworthiness of Small Language Models (SLMs), which are emerging as efficient alternatives to LLMs. It compares approaches for building SLMs, either by training compact models from scratch or by compressing larger ones.

title: Asymptotic Risk Calibration for Selective Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces an asymptotic risk calibration method for selective question answering to address the issue of large language models generating fluent but incorrect answers. It focuses on improving uncertainty quantification for reliable question answering.

title: Poly-Dialectal Neural Machine Translation System for Bangla Regional Dialects
summary: This research proposes a poly-dialectal neural machine translation system designed to handle the significant regional dialectal variations in Bangla, a challenge for natural language processing. The system aims to address divergences from Standard Colloquial Bangla across its diverse variants.

title: Structuring the Space of Perspectives
summary: This paper explores the concept of "perspectives" in natural language processing (NLP), which examines how different writers or speakers report the same event based on their experiences and beliefs. It discusses how various NLP areas, from text analysis to algorithm optimization, engage with these perspectives.

title: QV-PIC: Query-Aware Visual Position-Independent Caching for Efficient RAG Serving
summary: This paper introduces QV-PIC, a query-aware visual position-independent caching method to enhance the efficiency of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) serving. It aims to mitigate redundant computations caused by RAG repeatedly prefilling identical text chunks across queries.

title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges
summary: This research introduces SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), a new method that enhances RAG by incorporating SQL and query-time dynamic hyperedges for LLMs. It aims to improve handling of structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning, addressing limitations in mainstream dense-retrieval RAG implementations.

title: A corpus-specific clinical RAG system matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on HealthBench
summary: This study evaluates VITA, a corpus-specific clinical Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, demonstrating that it matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on the HealthBench medical benchmark. The research highlights the effectiveness of specialized RAG systems in healthcare applications.

title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
summary: This paper presents the first systematic study of massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved hybrid linear attention large language models (LLMs). It uncovers two architecture-aligned morphologies: pre-attention spikes and inter-spike plateaus.

title: Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge
summary: This research identifies an "Information Abundance Paradox," showing that training large language models with increasingly long contexts can paradoxically undermine their parametric knowledge. It challenges the assumption that longer contexts universally improve model performance.

title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
summary: This paper demonstrates that relying on a single large language model to simulate user behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning for human-AI interaction systematically fails to generalize. The failure is attributed to "simulator collapse," where the simulator LLM becomes mode-collapsed.

title: A Cascaded Unsupervised-Supervised NLP Pipeline for Detecting Accusatory Language in Public Procurement
summary: This research proposes a cascaded unsupervised-supervised natural language processing (NLP) pipeline designed to detect accusatory language in public procurement documents. The system aims to leverage stakeholder comments and government data for improved oversight.

title: Structural Silence: When AI Infrastructure Fails Speakers of Underrepresented Languages
summary: This paper examines how existing AI infrastructure, including training corpora and evaluation benchmarks, structurally fails speakers of underrepresented languages, exacerbating access gaps in AI tools for education and language support. It highlights issues of bias and fairness in AI development.

title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing
summary: This research reproduces and stress-tests two methods aimed at improving large language model (LLM) reasoning reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation (RPC) and Logic-Representation Editing (LCF). The methods are evaluated across various domains and models like Qwen3-8B.

title: GeoUniPR: A Geometry-Consistent Unified Framework for Cross-Modal Place Recognition
summary: This paper introduces GeoUniPR, a geometry-consistent unified framework for cross-modal place recognition (CMPR) that identifies locations across heterogeneous sensing modalities like vision and LiDAR. It aims to bridge the modality gap more efficiently than existing complex alignment methods.

title: CLEAR: Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling for Long-Tailed Classification
summary: This research proposes CLEAR (Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling) to address the reliability challenges of long-tailed classification where models trained on imbalanced data perform unevenly across classes. The method aims to improve reliability across frequent and underrepresented classes.

title: Self-Evolving Code-with-Image Reasoning
summary: This paper explores "Self-Evolving Code-with-Image Reasoning," a paradigm where multimodal models utilize tools for visual tasks, moving beyond simple perception to reasoning over visual evidence. It addresses the central challenge of integrating tool use with multimodal reasoning.

title: Clinical Feasibility of Low-Magnification Fluorescence Imaging for Breast Cancer Margin Detection Using Texture Analysis and Deep Learning
summary: This study investigates the clinical feasibility of using low-magnification fluorescence imaging with texture analysis and deep learning for breast cancer margin detection. It applies AI to analyze MUSE images of surgical breast tissue for improved cancer diagnosis.

title: Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding for Clinical Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This research proposes Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding (DD-CMD) for clinical text-guided medical image segmentation, specifically for pulmonary infection. It integrates both spatial alignment and frequency content to improve segmentation accuracy based on clinical text input.

title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts
summary: This research paper presents a method for estimating human gaze targets from images in-the-wild without requiring explicit inputs like head bounding boxes or human pose.

title: COGENT: Counterfactual Gaussian Explanations for Volumetric Medical Images
summary: This paper introduces COGENT, a method for generating counterfactual Gaussian explanations to improve the explainability of deep learning models in volumetric medical imaging.

title: VLMs Win a Systematic Evaluation of Underwater Image Reconstruction
summary: This paper describes a systematic evaluation pipeline for underwater image reconstruction, designed to assess the accuracy and consistency of reconstruction methods.

title: TangPoetryBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark and Rubric-Conditioned Evaluator for Poetry-to-Image Generation
summary: This introduces TangPoetryBench, a multi-dimensional benchmark and rubric-conditioned evaluator for measuring the quality of poetry-to-image generation models.

title: Multi-Agent Target-Existence Verification and Learned Mask Geometry Refinement: Winning Report of the MeViS-Text Track at the 8th LSVOS Challenge 2026
summary: This paper details the first-place solution for the MeViS-Text track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge, focusing on referring video object segmentation guided by written motion expressions.

title: Gaussian Meta-Space Augmentation for Stacking Ensembles in Multimodal IPMN Risk Stratification
summary: This research presents Gaussian Meta-Space Augmentation for stacking ensembles, a method aimed at improving multimodal risk stratification for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) in pancreatic cancer.

title: Test-Time Hallucination Control in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper investigates object hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) and proposes methods for test-time control to improve their reliability.

title: Generative Semantic Segmentation via an Observable Semantic-Image Interface and Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment
summary: This research proposes a method for generative semantic segmentation using an observable semantic-image interface and hierarchical generator evidence alignment to address issues like color drift.

title: Through Van Gogh's Eyes: Global Style Transfer with Diffusion Mod
summary: This paper introduces a "Global Style Transfer with Diffusion Mod" method for artistic image synthesis, aiming to capture an artist's overall style more effectively.

title: From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection
summary: This research proposes a method for physics-grounded reflection simulation and diffusion-based video dereflection to improve video quality by removing reflections.

title: Repurposing RGB-based Foundation Model for Depth Estimation on Thermal Images Using Hierarchical Supervision
summary: This research explores repurposing RGB-based foundation models for depth estimation on thermal images using hierarchical supervision, beneficial for robotic applications in adverse conditions.

title: Hand Visibility Detector: Per-Keypoint Visibility Estimation for Hands
summary: This paper presents a Hand Visibility Detector designed for per-keypoint visibility estimation in hands, crucial for assessing the reliability of Hand Pose Estimation results under occlusion.

title: A Hybrid Framework of Vision Transformer and Gated Recurrent Unit for Detection of Mosquito Diseases
summary: This research proposes a hybrid framework combining Vision Transformers and Gated Recurrent Units for detecting mosquito diseases by analyzing mosquito locomotion behavior.

title: Topology-Aware Query Selection for Surgical Instrument Instance Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces Topology-Aware Query Selection, a method to improve surgical instrument instance segmentation by refining predictions to ensure correct object identity and count.

title: KANResDiff: Learning Local Residual Diffusion via Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Ambiguous Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This research proposes KANResDiff, a method that learns local residual diffusion via a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for ambiguous medical image segmentation, aiming to provide diverse and plausible hypotheses.

title: Generative Video Compression Based on Hierarchical Referencing
summary: This paper explores generative video compression based on hierarchical referencing, leveraging diffusion models to improve perceptual quality by efficiently encoding latent frames.

title: CAM-Guided Saliency Cutout and Image-Based Malware Classification
summary: This research proposes using CAM-Guided Saliency Cutout as a data augmentation technique to improve image-based malware classification.

title: Robustness of AI-Art Detectors under Generator Shift
summary: This research examines the robustness of AI-art detectors when facing generator shifts, addressing concerns about their effectiveness against rapidly advancing text-to-image models.

title: Hybrid-LUT: Channel-Aware Hybrid Lookup Table and Filtering for Efficient Image Denoising
summary: This paper introduces Hybrid-LUT, a channel-aware hybrid lookup table and filtering method designed for efficient image denoising, reducing on-chip SRAM consumption.

title: Motion-as-Prompt: Enhancing Motion Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via Motion-Guided Cross-Frame Visual Prompting
summary: This research proposes "Motion-as-Prompt," a method to enhance motion reasoning in multimodal large language models through motion-guided cross-frame visual prompting.

title: Zero-OVCD: Bridging Training-Free Foundation Models and Pseudo-Label Learning for Open-Vocabulary Change Detection
summary: This paper introduces Zero-OVCD, a method that combines training-free foundation models and pseudo-label learning to improve open-vocabulary change detection in remote sensing images by addressing issues like inaccurate masks and ambiguous semantic assignments.

title: Learning from Multimodal Pseudo-Labels for Robust Open-Vocabulary Instance and Panoptic Segmentation
summary: This work proposes learning from multimodal pseudo-labels to enhance the robustness of open-vocabulary instance segmentation and open-set panoptic segmentation, aiming to recognize both known and unseen object categories more effectively.

title: EGM-Det: Entropy-Guided Multimodal Adaptive Fusion for UAV RGB-IR Object Detection
summary: EGM-Det is an entropy-guided multimodal adaptive fusion framework designed to improve object detection in UAV imagery by jointly using RGB and infrared data and dynamically addressing spatially varying modality reliability.

title: Boundary-Enhanced Segmentation of Pig Point Clouds in Commercial Housing Environments
summary: This research focuses on boundary-enhanced segmentation of pig point clouds in commercial housing environments to improve accuracy by addressing blurred target boundaries, local adhesion, and background mis-segmentation.

title: STAR: A Spatial-Topology Aware Routing Framework for Generalizable 3D Scene Understanding
summary: STAR is a spatial-topology aware routing framework designed to construct generalizable 3D scene understanding models by effectively managing topological discrepancies across different sensor modalities within a Mixture-of-Experts architecture.

title: Advancing MLLM-based UAV Image Understanding and Reasoning: A Benchmark and a Training-Free Multi-Agent System
summary: This work advances MLLM-based UAV image understanding and reasoning by presenting both a new benchmark to evaluate such systems and a training-free multi-agent system designed to address challenges like extreme scale variation and arbitrary camera orientations.

title: JieZi: A Large-Scale Expert-Audited Dataset and Benchmark for Ancient Chinese Character Exegesis
summary: JieZi is introduced as a large-scale, expert-audited dataset and benchmark specifically designed for the scholarly exegesis of ancient Chinese characters, addressing the current lack of structured resources for computational approaches in this field.

title: LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
summary: LiveAnimate is a new system for stable, long-form streaming human animation in real-time, enabling interactive applications like live streaming and virtual avatars by synthesizing video from a single reference image and a driving pose stream.

title: Making Every Step Count: Spatio-Temporal Information Allocation for Imaging Inverse Problems
summary: This research proposes a method for spatio-temporal information allocation to enhance the performance of flow-based generative models in solving imaging inverse problems, focusing on improving the design of individual updates for better coherent semantics and fine-grained structure.

title: Dual Modality Prompted Diffusion Priors for Zero Shot Hyperspectral Pansharpening
summary: This work introduces a method utilizing dual modality prompted diffusion priors to achieve zero-shot hyperspectral pansharpening, aiming to reconstruct high-resolution hyperspectral images while preserving both spatial details and spectral fidelity.

title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
summary: UniSwap is a new method for streaming audio-visual identity swapping in talking videos, designed to coordinate the transfer of appearance and voice while maintaining the source motion, scene, linguistic content, and audio-video timing.

title: Automated binary classification of hazelnut X-ray images: A deep-learning benchmark for quality assessment
summary: This research introduces a deep-learning benchmark for the automated binary classification of hazelnut X-ray images, addressing challenges such as subtle radiographic differences and class imbalance to improve quality assessment.

title: ProBAG: Prototype-Guided Boundary-Aware Graph Diffusion for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
summary: ProBAG introduces a prototype-guided boundary-aware graph diffusion method for weakly supervised histopathology segmentation, aiming to improve localization accuracy in tissue interfaces where CAM-based methods are often unreliable.

title: Achieving Near-Zero-Overhead Multi-Model Hierarchical Classification in Real-Time Detection Pipelines
summary: This work focuses on achieving near-zero-overhead multi-model hierarchical classification within real-time detection pipelines, particularly for edge-deployed vision systems in applications like target recognition and autonomous vehicles.

title: VOLA: Improving Open-World Driving by VLM-Based Semantic Attribute Prediction
summary: VOLA improves open-world driving by using VLM-based semantic attribute prediction to help autonomous vehicles understand and react appropriately to novel or unexpected objects, shifting scene perception beyond mere object naming.

title: PolarSym: Polar Geometry-aware Attention for CAD Floorplan Parsing
summary: PolarSym introduces a polar geometry-aware attention framework to enhance CAD floorplan parsing, aiming to improve the automatic extraction of architectural elements from 2D engineering drawings.

title: CoDiR: Confidence-Guided Diffusion Refinement for Semi-Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
summary: CoDiR is a confidence-guided diffusion refinement framework developed for semi-supervised histopathology segmentation, addressing challenges of scarce annotations and unreliable pseudo-labels by combining diffusion with a Mean Teacher model.

title: Can Vision Models Read the Radar Display? On the Feasibility of Radar Imagery for Air Traffic Complexity Estimation
summary: This research explores the feasibility of using radar imagery as input for computer vision models to estimate air traffic complexity, aiming to mimic how air traffic controllers perceive traffic via their radar displays.

title: TD-VAD: Breaking Visual Dependence in Video Anomaly Detection with Text-Driven Learning
summary: TD-VAD proposes a novel approach to video anomaly detection by breaking visual dependence through text-driven learning, thereby addressing the challenges of obtaining sufficient annotated anomaly data for training.

title: GeoBridge: Decoupled Semantic Conditioning for Generative Image Geolocalization
summary: GeoBridge is introduced as a method for generative image geolocalization, utilizing decoupled semantic conditioning with multimodal large language models to improve reasoning and decoding of geographic cues into coordinates.

title: BoltNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Convolutional Network for On-Device Plant Species Identification
summary: Introduces BoltNet, an ultra-lightweight convolutional network designed for on-device plant species identification from citizen-science imagery, balancing capacity with memory, latency, and power constraints for field use.

title: LookBack: Where and How to Score LVLM Responses via Visual Reference Usage
summary: Introduces LookBack, a method for scoring Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) responses by analyzing their visual reference usage to identify and mitigate image-based hallucinations.

title: Warping Earth Observations for better ice labeling in the Marginal Marginal Ice Zone
summary: Explores methods for warping multimodal satellite imagery to improve ice labeling in dynamic environments like the Antarctic marginal ice zone, addressing challenges in combining heterogeneous sensor data for Earth Observation.

title: Do You See What You Draw? A Semantic Closed-Loop Framework for Holistic Evaluation of Unified Multimodal Models
summary: Proposes a semantic closed-loop framework for the holistic evaluation of unified multimodal models, addressing the critical challenge of assessing Large Vision-Language Models that integrate both visual generation and understanding.

title: HarmoniDPO: Video-guided Audio Generation via Preference-Optimized Diffusion
summary: Introduces HarmoniDPO, a method for video-guided audio generation that utilizes preference-optimized diffusion to achieve precise temporal synchronization and high perceptual quality, addressing challenges in the video-to-audio relationship.

title: Dual Anchors, Do It Better: Hierarchical Group Merging for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
summary: Proposes a method using hierarchical group merging with dual anchors to improve zero-shot anomaly detection, particularly for industrial and medical applications where domain shifts are prevalent.

title: Adaptation of Generalist Robot Policies with Minimal Data
summary: Explores methods for adapting generalist robot policies with minimal data, aiming for robots to improve through autonomous interaction rather than relying on extensive task-specific human data collection.

title: Top-down Traffic Scenario Generation via Joint Initial-Goal Diffusion and Trajectory Infilling
summary: Presents a method for top-down traffic scenario generation using joint initial-goal diffusion and trajectory infilling, crucial for developing and testing autonomous vehicles in robust simulators.

title: From Self-Normal-Positioning to Omni-Directional Tracking: Real-Time Surface Modeling Enabled Probe Tilt Control for Robotic Ultrasound Imaging
summary: Introduces real-time surface modeling for probe tilt control in robotic ultrasound imaging, moving beyond self-normal positioning to enable omni-directional tracking and improve image acquisition consistency.

title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Investigates locomotion variability and user experience in human-robot interaction with smart wheelchairs, examining how model-based assistance strategies can better accommodate inherent human movement variability.

title: Herding End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guards
summary: Proposes using neuro-symbolic safety guards to improve end-to-end autonomous driving agents, addressing their tendency to violate basic traffic rules by integrating physical conditions for safe decision-making.

title: Keep the Future, Drop the Rollout: RIFT for World Action Models
summary: Introduces RIFT, a method for World Action Models (WAMs) that optimizes robot action generation by conditioning on future representations rather than iterative video rollout, aiming to reduce deployment latency across various tasks.

title: RoadWeaver: Large-Scale Lane-Level HD Map Generation from Scratch for Autonomous Driving Simulation
summary: Presenting RoadWeaver, a system for large-scale lane-level HD map generation from scratch, providing diverse and scalable maps crucial for autonomous driving simulation and long-horizon evaluation.

title: Video2Track: From Real-World Interaction Videos to Steerable Adversarial Closed-Track Testing for Automated Driving Systems
summary: Introduces Video2Track, a system that transforms real-world interaction videos into steerable adversarial closed-track testing scenarios for the rigorous verification and validation of automated driving systems (ADS).

title: IoT-Enabled Autonomous Maritime Navigation in Smart Ports: A Curriculum-Guided Shared Policy Learning Framework
summary: Investigates a curriculum-guided shared policy learning framework for IoT-enabled autonomous maritime navigation in smart ports, addressing the challenge of reliable onboard intelligence for safe and scalable operations.

title: StellaVLA: In-Context Structured Demonstration for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Introduces StellaVLA, a method utilizing in-context structured demonstration to enhance the generalizability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, improving their performance in out-of-distribution scenarios for object manipulation.

title: G0.5: One Autoregressive Stream for Robot Reasoning and Action
summary: Introduces G0.5, a pretrained autoregressive Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that uses a single transformer decoder for robot reasoning and action, unifying the VLM's role as a decision-maker rather than just a context encoder.

title: Policy-Induced Hand Priors in Humanoid Dual-Arm Manipulation: Diagnosing and Mitigating Initial-Pose Dependence
summary: Investigates policy-induced hand priors in VLA-based humanoid dual-arm manipulation, diagnosing and mitigating initial-pose dependence to ensure robust operation across varying robot configurations.

title: Enhancing Visual Domain Robustness in Behaviour Cloning via Saliency-Guided Augmentation
summary: Proposes enhancing visual domain robustness in vision-based behavior cloning through saliency-guided augmentation, addressing the limitations of conventional image augmentations in handling significant visual domain shifts.

title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
summary: Introduces D3D-GEN, a robot-aware domain-grounded interactive 3D world generation system designed to create realistic simulation environments for training and validating embodied AI in social robotics navigation.

title: Learning Loco-Manipulation From SMPC Demonstrations With Sparse Offline-to-Online RL
summary: This paper presents a method for learning loco-manipulation for robot autonomy by integrating locomotion and manipulation skills, using sparse offline-to-online Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Sample-based Model Predictive Control (SMPC) demonstrations.

title: HandEdit: A Unified Benchmark for Egocentric Human-to-Robot Dexterous Hand Image Editing
summary: This introduces HandEdit, a benchmark for egocentric human-to-robot dexterous hand image editing, aimed at overcoming data collection costs for robotic manipulation by leveraging human hand videos despite appearance discrepancies.
