title: Position: Reasoning is a Learnable Rule-Based Process
summary: This position paper argues that autonomous reasoning in AI, a topic of significant scientific and economic interest, is best understood as a learnable rule-based process, moving from symbolic AI to deep probabilistic generative models.

title: Diagnostic Foundation for Evaluating LLMs' Research Integrity as Co-Scientists
summary: This paper introduces IntegrityBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the research integrity of large language models when acting as co-scientists, assessing their ability in misconduct classification and ethical reasoning.

title: Position: The Alignment Community is Unintentionally Building a Censor's Toolkit
summary: This position paper argues that current AI alignment methods, intended to prevent harmful outputs, are dual-use technologies that could be misused for censorship and manipulation.

title: Agreement Is Not Alignment: Divergent Moral Grounds in Human and LLM Ethical Judgments
summary: This paper posits that agreement between human and LLM ethical judgments does not equate to alignment, as their underlying moral reasoning principles may diverge.

title: Multi-Agent Scheduling with LLM-Assisted Contract Net Negotiation for Stream Processing in Mobile Edge Computing
summary: This paper proposes MAS-DecStream, a system for multi-agent scheduling using LLM-assisted contract net negotiation to manage stream processing in mobile edge computing environments.

title: Position: We Need Practical AI Alignment Methods to Mirror Human Reasoning
summary: This position paper argues for the development of practical AI alignment methods that enable AI systems to mirror human reasoning, particularly for accurate and cognitively-aligned decision-making in high-stakes scenarios.

title: Don't Want Your LLM to Recommend Nuclear Strike? Try Asking It in Japanese
summary: This research investigates how the language of a prompt can influence the safety alignment of large language models, demonstrating that safety controls evaluated only in English may be bypassed in other languages in high-stakes scenarios.

title: Dual-Flow Transformers: Decoupling the Primary Prefill Path from Additional Decode Computation
summary: This paper introduces Dual-Flow Transformers, an architecture designed to decouple the prompt prefill path from decode computation in LLMs, aiming to optimize inference cost and efficiency.

title: Learning to Adapt Cross-Domain Preferences via Meta-LoRA for LLM Personalization
summary: This paper introduces Meta-LoRA, a new method that uses meta-learning to adapt large language models to cross-domain user preferences for enhanced personalization with limited data.

title: Research Assistant: AstraZeneca's Agentic System for R&D
summary: AstraZeneca has developed "Research Assistant," an internal LLM-based agentic system designed to help scientists and clinicians explore biomedical questions by integrating data from various sources.

title: Large Language Models Can Follow Instructions, But Not Many at Once: Phase Transitions in Compositional Constraint Satisfaction
summary: This research explores the limitations of large language models in simultaneously adhering to multiple explicit constraints, observing phase transitions when numerous compositional constraints are applied.

title: MindMemOS: A Portable and Self-Evolving Memory Operating Layer for AI Agents
summary: This paper introduces MindMemOS, a portable and self-evolving memory operating layer designed for AI agents to enhance their ability to accumulate experience and adapt over long-term interactions.

title: Governed Persistent Memory: Source-Bound State Semantics and Fail-Closed Release for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Introduces Governed Persistent Memory (GPM), an auditable bitemporal state-transition model designed to manage long-term agent memory, addressing issues like contradictory or stale records. It aims to improve reliability and auditability of information stored for long-horizon AI agents.

title: $\varepsilon$-MemEvo: Adaptive Cross-Task Memory Transfer for LLM Program Evolution
summary: Introduces ε-MemEvo, a framework enabling adaptive cross-task memory transfer for LLM program evolution systems like FunSearch, preventing the discarding of search experience after task completion. This improves knowledge retention and reuse across different programming tasks.

title: CAS: A Causal Attribution Score for Local and Global Explainable Artificial Intelligence
summary: Introduces the Causal Attribution Score (CAS), a compact architecture for causal explanation in AI, designed to attribute intervention effects on real-world outcomes. This method aims to improve explainability in AI systems beyond just predictive explanations.

title: Trie Automata for Constrained Decoding over Large Finite Sets
summary: Proposes using Trie Automata as a method for constrained decoding in large language models, specifically to enable generating structured outputs that conform to predefined finite sets of valid strings. This offers an alternative to general-purpose grammar compilation for such tasks.

title: Reasoning Jury: Multi-Model Consensus for Evaluating Reasoning Traces
summary: Introduces the "Reasoning Jury," a multi-model consensus approach for evaluating the quality of long reasoning traces generated by LLMs. This aims to improve data curation, training signals for reinforcement learning, and understanding of model reasoning behaviors.

title: Auditable agentic AI for evidence-grounded thyroid ultrasound diagnosis and reporting
summary: Presents ThyroidXAgent, a clinician-interactive agentic AI system designed for evidence-grounded thyroid ultrasound diagnosis and reporting. This system coordinates lesion localization, measurement, risk stratification, and reporting, with a focus on auditable processes.

title: DiG-bench: Discovery in Games
summary: Introduces DiG-bench, a new AI benchmark designed to evaluate AI's capacity for discovery and forming novel generalizations through experimentation in controlled environments. It addresses a gap in current AI benchmarks regarding the measurement of scientific discovery abilities.

title: Dead text or binding clause? Measuring and restoring constraint influence in black-box LLM dialogues
summary: Investigates "behavioral relapse" or "revocation inertia" in black-box LLM dialogues, where models fail to reliably act upon withdrawn user constraints. The paper measures this phenomenon and suggests methods to restore constraint influence.

title: @skills: Attention is all you have
summary: Discusses the limitations of the current installation-based model for delivering AI agent skills, where numerous skills compete for limited "trigger slots" in the system prompt. This highlights a challenge for the scalability and usability of agent capabilities.

title: Jagged Judges: Epistemic Stability Under Silence, Pressure, and Persistence
summary: Introduces the "Wiggle score" to evaluate the epistemic stability of LLM judges under various conditions like re-prompting or pushback. It assesses whether these judges, central to model evaluation, are stable beyond mere accuracy on golden data.

title: SteerBench-Work: A Benchmark for Agent Steering at Action Boundaries
summary: Introduces SteerBench-Work, an incident-anchored and bidirectional benchmark designed to evaluate agent steering capabilities at action boundaries. It focuses on the pre-commit decision for LLM agents using tools, allowing for human or policy review.

title: Designing AI Pipelines for Decision-Ready ITSM Intelligence
summary: Presents a sociotechnical AI pipeline designed and evaluated using design science research principles, aimed at transforming large volumes of heterogeneous IT service management (ITSM) ticket data into actionable intelligence for stakeholders.

title: On the Expressive Power of Transformers
summary: Investigates the expressive power of multi-layer transformers, a critical component of large language models, aiming to precisely calibrate their capabilities as language recognizers. This study delves into the fundamental theoretical properties of this architecture.

title: Lines and Ladders: A Context-Aware Multi-Agent Framework for Large-Scale Retail Price Taxonomy
summary: Introduces "Lines and Ladders," a context-aware multi-agent framework designed to maintain price consistency and manage price taxonomy for large-scale retail catalogs. It addresses the challenge of managing millions of items to ensure consistent pricing across variants.

title: Privacy-Preserving RAG by Concealing Sensitive Information from External LLMs
summary: Proposes a method for privacy-preserving Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by focusing on concealing sensitive information from external Large Language Models (LLMs). This addresses a critical privacy concern often overlooked in RAG systems.

title: The Role of Natural Language Understanding in Multimodal Video-Based Dengue Diagnosis
summary: Explores the role of Natural Language Understanding in multimodal video-based dengue diagnosis, focusing on detecting infection-related behavioral changes in mosquitoes from video data despite environmental challenges.

title: Beyond the Best Guess: Improving LLM Solution Coverage with Evolution Strategies
summary: Proposes using evolution strategies to improve the solution coverage of Large Language Models in discovery domains like math and science. This goes beyond a single "best guess" to enhance the models' ability to generate diverse and effective solutions.

title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence
summary: Introduces a Spatial Memory Agent that leverages experience-grounded procedure memory to enhance spatial intelligence in embodied agents, robotic planning, and multimodal assistants. It aims to improve spatial reasoning abilities in VLM agents.

title: Correct Is Not Governed: Provenance Integrity in Agentic Workflows
summary: Defines "governed execution" and "provenance integrity" within agentic workflows, emphasizing that correct actions must also rely on valid authority and supported claims, rather than just achieving a correct outcome. This addresses system integrity for agents.

title: PROVE-RT: Generating Mechanized Theorem Prover Scripts for Real-Time Systems using LLMs
summary: Introduces PROVE-RT, a method for generating mechanized theorem prover scripts for real-time systems using Large Language Models, aiming to provide a more rigorous and scalable alternative to traditional pen-and-paper proofs for schedulability analysis.

title: ARAC: Benchmarking Auto-Research's Alignment and Completeness on End-to-End Researchs
summary: Introduces ARAC-Bench, a new benchmark to evaluate the alignment, logical coherence, and evolutionary completeness of Auto-Research systems with human research behavior.

title: Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents
summary: Explores how self-improving LLM agents can develop unsafe policies from successful trajectories, leading to "skill misevolution" as successful but unsafe behaviors become reusable.

title: AI and Consumer Rights in India Working Paper
summary: This working paper examines whether India's Consumer Protection Act, 2019, adequately addresses liability for harm caused by defective AI products and services.

title: Agent Behavioral Contracts II: Certifying Compositional Reliability Without Assuming Independence
summary: Investigates compositional reliability bounds for multi-agent systems, challenging the common assumption of conditional independence between component reliabilities.

title: Polish Medical Visual Question Answering: Vision-Language Models Underutilize Visual Evidence
summary: Presents a new Polish-language medical VQA benchmark, built from Polish Board Certification Examination questions, to evaluate Vision-Language Models.

title: FlashDrive: Flash Vision-Language-Action Inference for Autonomous Driving
summary: Proposes FlashDrive to improve the efficiency of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference for autonomous driving by addressing its computational bottlenecks for real-time control.

title: OGR-MARL: Option-Guided Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous USV Cooperative Pursuit in Constrained Port Waterways
summary: Introduces OGR-MARL, an option-guided residual multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, for heterogeneous unmanned surface vehicles to cooperatively pursue targets in constrained port waterways.

title: Foundations of MT-PDCL: Measure-Theoretic Probabilistic Definite Clause Logic
summary: Introduces Measure-Theoretic Probabilistic Definite Clause Logic (MT-PDCL), a new framework addressing limitations of standard probabilistic logic programming for exact inference in finite domains.

title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
summary: Explores optimizing cache reuse policies to reduce inference overhead in diffusion models, identifying current policies' mismatch with global efficiency.

title: DMDIntel: Interpreting Large Language Models via Dynamic Mode Decomposition
summary: Introduces DMDIntel, a method using Dynamic Mode Decomposition to interpret Large Language Models' predictions by decomposing hidden states into prominent patterns for input attribution.

title: VALG: An Agentic System for ML Theory Research
summary: Presents VALG, an agentic system designed to assist with machine learning theory research by formulating problems and proving theorems in mathematical setups.

title: Explanatory Engagement Under Rare Anomalous Failure: Asymptotic Rarity in Model Behavior (or: The Asymptotic AI)
summary: Examines how Large Language Models' explanatory engagement changes when facing rare anomalous failures in a workflow with a low, controllable failure rate.

title: Behavioral Reprogramming of Open-Weights Models: Cognitive Plasticity and Alignment Bounds
summary: Investigates the cognitive plasticity of open-weight LLMs and their susceptibility to rigorous behavioral reprogramming, aiming to induce different alignments.

title: EEG-PRIME: Prototype-Aligned Representation Learning with Multi-Level Conditioning for EEG Decoding
summary: Proposes EEG-PRIME, a two-stage EEG foundation model that uses prototype-aligned representation learning and multi-level conditioning for robust cross-dataset multi-task EEG decoding.

title: SPADE: Speculative Decoding for Precise and Low Cost Distributed Edge Cloud Inference
summary: Introduces SPADE, a speculative decoding method designed to enable precise and low-cost distributed edge-cloud inference for Large Language Models.

title: SkillEvo: Self-Renewing Evolution Gradients from Multi-Turn Interaction Feedback
summary: Presents SkillEvo, a method for agents to generate "self-renewing evolution gradients" from multi-turn interaction feedback, enabling continuous skill improvement.

title: Numeracy in Large Language Models: Fundamental Limitations and Paths to Improvement
summary: A survey examining the fundamental limitations of Large Language Models in numerical understanding and elementary mathematical tasks, and suggesting paths for improvement.

title: LoKiFormer: Locality-aware Attention with Decoupled Knowledge Memory for Efficient Large Language Model Pretraining
summary: Introduces LoKiFormer, an architecture that uses locality-aware attention and decoupled knowledge memory to improve the efficiency of Large Language Model pretraining.

title: MARCH: Scaling Recurrent Memory with Content-Routed State Anchors
summary: Proposes MARCH, a method to scale recurrent memory by using content-routed state anchors, addressing the quadratic computation and linear cache growth of token-level memory.

title: Multi-AUV Ad-hoc network-based Target Tracking: A Value Gradient Guidance Multi-Agent Diffusion Reinforcement Learning Approach
summary: Presents a Multi-Agent Diffusion Reinforcement Learning approach using value gradient guidance for multi-AUV ad-hoc network-based target tracking in constrained underwater environments.

title: Unifying Generative Models with Path Integrals
summary: This paper formulates a unified theoretical framework for generative modeling using path integrals, where various generative models arise from different evaluation principles. It describes the Martin-Siggia-Rose-Janssen-de~Dominicis form to separate free from interacting probability flow.

title: Dual Spatial-Temporal Attribution: Architecture-Aligned Post-Hoc Explainability for Recurrent Graph Anomaly Detection
summary: This research addresses the opacity of deep learning detectors for anomalies in dynamic graphs by proposing a dual spatial-temporal attribution method for post-hoc explainability. The goal is to provide reasons for flagged anomalies, which is crucial for deployment in regulated information systems.

title: Geometric and Behavioral Stratification in Transformer Residual Streams
summary: This paper investigates the internal workings of trained transformer models, focusing on "privileged bases" within residual streams. It explores the prediction and unembedding directions to understand how these coordinate axes influence model behavior.

title: Learning Under Treatment-Induced Label Indeterminacy with Expert Annotations of Counterfactual Outcomes: A Case Study in Neurological Prognostication
summary: This study addresses the challenge of label indeterminacy in clinical prediction models, particularly when treatment decisions make outcomes unobservable, using a case study in neurological prognostication. It proposes using expert annotations of counterfactual outcomes for learning in such scenarios.

title: When Can You Trust Offline Evaluation of Equal-Cost Top-k Allocation? A Controlled, Reproducible Benchmark and Practitioner's Guide
summary: This paper introduces a controlled and reproducible benchmark to evaluate the trustworthiness of offline evaluation for equal-cost top-k allocation. It provides a practitioner's guide for off-policy evaluation of deterministic top-k policies from logged data.

title: Exploring Oversmoothing with Householder Matrices
summary: This research explores the phenomenon of oversmoothing in deep graph neural networks (GNNs), where node representations collapse with increasing network depth. It proposes using Householder matrices to study and address this issue.

title: GENADA: efficient generative time series adversarial attack framework
summary: This paper introduces GENADA, an efficient generative time series adversarial attack framework, to expose the vulnerability of deep learning models used in time series analysis. It demonstrates how small input perturbations can severely degrade predictive performance.

title: Scaling Automatic Research Agents via World Models
summary: This research explores scaling automatic research (AutoResearch) agents using world models, leveraging the capabilities of modern large language models (LLMs) to independently implement solutions and learn from the execution outcomes in empirical research.

title: Prof-K: Probabilistic One-Pass Filtering for Efficient Top-k Selection
summary: This paper introduces Prof-K, a probabilistic one-pass filtering method designed for efficient top-k selection, a fundamental computational primitive. It aims to address the inefficiency of existing approaches for large data sizes in various machine learning workloads.

title: Represent, Then Generate: Multimodal-Conditioned Time-Series Generation under Irregular Missingness
summary: This research proposes a method for multimodal-conditioned time-series generation to synthesize absent physiological signals from co-recorded data, addressing irregular missingness in clinical monitoring. The approach aims to provide a remedy when informative signals are unavailable.

title: Predicting When Random Low-Dimensional Reparameterizations Train Neural Networks
summary: This paper investigates the conditions under which neural networks can be effectively trained or fine-tuned using random low-dimensional reparameterization. It explores the necessary size of the latent search space to reach a low-loss region.

title: Structure-preserving uncertainty quantification for GENERIC dynamics
summary: This research focuses on developing methods for structure-preserving uncertainty quantification (UQ) for machine learning models that embed physical structures directly into their architectures. It addresses limitations where standard UQ methods may violate encoded admissibility conditions.

title: CAKE: Compiler-Agent Co-Design for Frontier Kernel Evolution
summary: This paper introduces CAKE (Compiler-Agent Co-Design) for the evolution of GPU kernels, addressing the challenge of reproducing expert kernels by integrating GPU kernel agents with compiler design. It aims to overcome limitations where agents treat the compiler as a black box.

title: Interpretable Causal Discovery via Causal-Effect Constraints
summary: This research proposes a method for interpretable causal discovery by using causal-effect constraints to uncover underlying causal relationships from data. The goal is to not only predict causal edges but also to explain observed or hypothesized phenomena.

title: Training Under Challenge: Executable Certificates and Challenge-Closed Optimality for Neural Networks
summary: This paper introduces "Training Under Challenge," an executable-certificate framework designed to provide deeper insights into the training process and optimality of neural networks. It aims to reveal whether a network has reached a global optimum or is limited in other ways, beyond what a flat training curve indicates.

title: Finding the Needle in a Haystack: Test-Time Analog Circuit Representation Adaptation for Bayesian Optimization
summary: This research proposes a test-time analog circuit representation adaptation method for Bayesian optimization (BO) to efficiently search for analog circuit topologies. It addresses the mismatch caused by fixed circuit embeddings after encoder training.

title: The Impact of Temporal Context Length and Encoding Strategies on Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning
summary: This research investigates the impact of temporal context length and encoding strategies on self-supervised electrocardiogram (ECG) representation learning. It explores how these choices affect information needed for rhythm inference and longitudinal consistency in real-world recordings.

title: A Contract-Grade Verifier for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels, and a Native Blackwell Backward for the Gated-Linear-Recurrence Family
summary: This paper presents a "Contract-Grade Verifier" for GPU kernels generated by Large Language Models, aiming to ensure higher correctness beyond simple random input tests. It also introduces a native Blackwell Backward for the Gated-Linear-Recurrence family.

title: Federated Compositional Muon Optimizer for Matrix-Wise Models
summary: This paper proposes a Federated Compositional Muon Optimizer designed to improve the performance of Muon, a recently developed optimizer, for matrix-wise models in AI, particularly for hierarchical structured problems.

title: Perturbation-based Regional Interpretability through Subtraction Mapping (PRISM): naming-error dissociations in language models and post-stroke aphasia
summary: This research introduces PRISM (Perturbation-based Regional Interpretability through Subtraction Mapping), a new method for mechanistic interpretability of large language models. It adapts subtraction analysis from human neuroimaging to test for specialized internal components in language models.

title: MAG: MAnifold Guided Semi-Supervised Multi-modal In-Context Learning
summary: This paper introduces MAG, a manifold-guided semi-supervised multi-modal in-context learning method to improve task adaptation for multi-modal large language models using both labeled and unlabeled data. It addresses the sensitivity of few-shot ICL to demonstration quality.

title: A Cloud-Edge System for Multimodal Clinical Screening in Resource-Constrained Rural Settings
summary: This research proposes a cloud-edge system for multimodal clinical screening, designed to make medical AI diagnostic capabilities accessible in resource-constrained rural settings with limited bandwidth and compute.

title: Decentralized Multi-Player Q-Learning in Episodic Markov Decision Processes with Information Asymmetry
summary: This study investigates decentralized multi-player reinforcement learning using Q-learning in episodic Markov Decision Processes, specifically examining how different forms of information asymmetry impact the learning process.

title: Beyond Outcome Rewards: Step-Level Self-Distilled Policy Optimization for Deep Search Agents
summary: This paper introduces a step-level self-distilled policy optimization method to improve deep search agents by providing more granular rewards, addressing the sparse outcome reward problem in traditional reinforcement learning.

title: CoMedBench: A Multi-Source Benchmark of Synthetic Medical Data Fidelity and Downstream Utility
summary: CoMedBench is a multi-source benchmark designed to evaluate the fidelity and utility of synthetic medical data for developing reliable healthcare machine learning systems while addressing privacy concerns.

title: HiRoute: Hierarchical Routed Prompt Tuning for Safety Alignment of Large Language Models
summary: HiRoute introduces a hierarchical routed prompt tuning method to improve the safety alignment of Large Language Models, making them more robust against harmful requests and jailbreak attacks.

title: A Compositional Theory of Curvature in Probabilistic Circuits
summary: This paper develops a compositional theory of curvature for Probabilistic Circuits, which are generative models that support exact inference, focusing on their loss-surface curvature.

title: Robust data-driven discovery of fractional differential equations via weak formulations and Pareto-based subset selection
summary: This research proposes a robust data-driven method, called Weak-Pareto, for discovering fractional differential equations from noisy data by combining weak formulations and Pareto-based subset selection.

title: EGRL: Edge generation-guided relation-aware learning for RNA-protein interaction prediction
summary: This paper introduces EGRL, an edge generation-guided relation-aware learning method using Graph Neural Networks for efficiently predicting RNA-Protein Interactions, which are critical for cellular functions.

title: Revisiting Overestimation Bias Problem of Q-learning: Settling Large Discrete Action Space via Action Intersection
summary: This paper re-examines the overestimation bias problem in Q-learning, particularly in settings with large discrete action spaces, proposing an action intersection method to mitigate the issue.

title: Towards Socially Compliant Navigation in Deep Reinforcement Learning via Proxemics-Based Reward Modeling
summary: This research proposes a proxemics-based reward modeling approach for deep reinforcement learning to enable socially compliant robot navigation in crowded environments.

title: Momentum as Residual-Driven Multiplier Correction for Deep Learning Optimization
summary: This paper introduces an ADMM-Inspired Momentum (AIM) framework to better understand and improve momentum-based optimizers in deep learning by treating momentum as a residual-driven multiplier correction.

title: Multi-perspective Imbalance-Conscious 6G Beamforming Optimization and Performance
summary: This study applies machine learning to optimize 6G-IoT beamforming, comparing supervised and unsupervised approaches and evaluating various feature groups for performance.

title: CardioState-JEPA: Delay-Aware Cross-Modal Learning of a Shared Cardiac Representation
summary: CardioState-JEPA introduces a delay-aware cross-modal learning approach to develop a shared cardiac representation from multi-sensor data (ECG, PPG, PCG), improving upon existing single-modality cardiac foundation models.

title: Understanding Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Vertical Federated Learning: The Gap Between Research and Practice
summary: This paper examines backdoor vulnerabilities within Vertical Federated Learning, analyzing the gap between current research and practical implications for model training and privacy.

title: Comment on "Modeling rapid language learning by distilling Bayesian priors into artificial neural networks"
summary: This paper comments on a previous work, discussing the proposal that Artificial Neural Networks can learn formal languages by distilling Bayesian priors into them via Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning.

title: Learning the Mathematical Property for Designing Low Mutual Coherence Binary Sensing Matrices
summary: This research focuses on using a learning-based technique to discover the mathematical properties required for designing low mutual coherence binary sensing matrices, essential for compressive sensing.

title: Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection for Scalable TabPFN Inference on Large-Scale Tabular Data
summary: This paper introduces Balanced Adaptive Prototype Selection (BAPS), a framework designed to enable scalable inference for pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN) on large-scale tabular datasets.

title: Incremental Evaluation and Training in Relational Deep Learning
summary: This paper proposes methods for incremental evaluation and training in Relational Deep Learning models, which process multi-tabular databases as temporal heterogeneous graphs, to better reflect the continuous nature of real-world data.

title: On the global feature importance for interpretable and trustworthy heat demand forecasting
summary: This paper introduces an ante-hoc Explainable AI methodology to assess global feature importance in Machine Learning models for heat demand forecasting, aiming to enhance their interpretability and trustworthiness in intelligent control systems.

title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: This paper introduces Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a method that enables self-evolving AI agents to learn from experience and internalize it into their policies through a privileged self-teacher.

title: Learning Discrete Decisions for MIPs with Constraint-Aware Diffusion
summary: This paper proposes a novel learning-based approach utilizing constraint-aware diffusion to approximately solve computationally challenging mixed-integer optimization problems.

title: Sampling Luck Masquerades as Allocation Gain: Auditing Test-Time Budget Allocation for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
summary: This research audits the impact of test-time budget allocation strategies for Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) solvers, revealing how sampling variability can masquerade as allocation gains.

title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching
summary: This paper introduces FlowLOB, a new method using flow matching for efficient, controllable, and realistic generation of limit order book (LOB) dynamics for market simulators.

title: LLMs Know the Constraint But Do Not Use It: Activation Bottlenecks in Pragmatic Constraint Reasoning
summary: This paper investigates why Large Language Models (LLMs) often fail to use internally encoded constraints in pragmatic reasoning, formalizing the concept of conditional constraint activation.

title: What Drives LLM Self-Reflection? A Controlled Ablation of Uncertainty Routing in Armed Conflict Forecasting
summary: This research presents a controlled ablation study to understand which components, such as evidence exposure and diagnostic scaffolding, drive improvements in LLM self-reflection for reasoning tasks.

title: Why Do AI Agents Break Rules? How Framing, Context, and Social Signals Shape Compliance
summary: This research demonstrates how specifying penalties can paradoxically cause AI agents to break rules by converting obligations into cost-benefit calculations, investigating the underlying reasons for non-compliance.

title: On Measuring Semantic Preservation in Legal Ontology Learning
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of measuring semantic preservation in legal ontology learning, highlighting limitations in current evaluation methodologies that focus on structural correctness rather than meaning.

title: Comparative Analysis of Multilingual Pre-trained Models for Nepali Automatic Speech Recognition
summary: This study provides a comparative analysis of six multilingual pre-trained models, including Whisper and XLSR-53, for Nepali Automatic Speech Recognition under a single fine-tuning protocol.

title: LoRA-Diffusion: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Low-Rank Trajectory Decomposition
summary: This paper introduces LoRA-Diffusion, a novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that extends low-rank adaptation techniques to diffusion-based language models.

title: AnchorSIPS: A Synthetic Dataset and Evaluation Resource for Evidence-Supported Psychosis-Risk Symptom Measurement
summary: This paper presents AnchorSIPS, a synthetic dataset of 10,000 structured psychosis-risk interviews, designed as an evaluation resource to overcome data-access bottlenecks in AI for mental health assessment.

title: Reliability-Aware Sexism Detection: Combining DPO with Annotator Agreement and Token-Level Confidence Scoring
summary: This research proposes a reliability-aware method for sexism detection, combining DPO with annotator agreement and token-level confidence scoring to address the inherent subjectivity of the task.

title: Thought-Aware KV Cache Compaction for Reasoning via Adaptive Attention Matching
summary: This paper introduces a 'thought-aware KV cache compaction' method that uses adaptive attention matching to address memory bottlenecks caused by lengthy chain-of-thought sequences in reasoning language models.

title: Can Spectral-Clipping Enable Better Learning While Forgetting Less for Low-Rank Adaptation?
summary: This work explores whether spectral-clipping can enhance low-rank adaptation (LoRA) by enabling better learning while reducing catastrophic forgetting in neural network fine-tuning.

title: Vision-Language Models are Fragile Multilingual Associators
summary: This paper introduces M$^2$BIND, a new benchmark to evaluate the stability and fragility of vision-language models' associations when the language of the input context or query changes.

title: Steering the Language Axis: From Linear Decodability to Causal Control
summary: This research investigates the latent dynamics of language selection in Large Language Models, exploring whether language identity can be causally controlled by compact activation mechanisms.

title: HC-RAG: Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Heterogeneous Financial Filings
summary: This paper introduces HC-RAG (Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a system designed for financial question answering that retrieves and synthesizes information from heterogeneous financial filings.

title: StorySpark: Module-wise Evolutionary Search for Story Premise Generation
summary: This paper introduces StorySpark, a new system that employs a module-wise evolutionary search for generating diverse and creative story premises using LLM-based approaches.

title: From Refuse to Richness: Rubric Rewards for Long-Form Hallucination Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research investigates using rubric rewards in reinforcement learning to improve grounding and reduce long-form hallucination in generative models, analyzing the trade-off between refusal and richness.

title: SDAM: Structure-Difference-Aware Memory Evolution for Complex Text-to-SQL
summary: This paper introduces SDAM, a memory evolution framework designed for complex text-to-SQL tasks. It addresses limitations in existing memory designs, such as neglecting historical experience and weak structure analysis, to improve SQL generation.

title: Mimicry without understanding: the origins of decision bias in large language models
summary: This research investigates the origins of decision bias in Large Language Models, demonstrating how social, affective, and cognitive biases can emerge even from unbiased or correctly categorized training data. It explores mechanisms by which LLMs mimic biases without true understanding.

title: Class-Structure Preservation Beats Diversity: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Text Augmentation Methods for Imbalanced Text Classification
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark evaluating text augmentation methods, including LLM-based approaches, for imbalanced text classification in natural language processing. It compares various techniques to determine their effectiveness in preserving class structure.

title: The "Knowledge-Behavior Gap" in Cultural Taboo Safety of Large Language Models
summary: This paper addresses the "Knowledge-Behavior Gap" in cultural taboo safety for Large Language Models, highlighting that current benchmarks primarily assess cultural knowledge or biases rather than LLMs' ability to recognize and respect cultural sensitivities to prevent harm.

title: Are Large Language Models Reliable Reviewers? A Benchmark for Error Detection in Financial Documents
summary: This research proposes a benchmark to assess the reliability of Large Language Models as reviewers for error detection in financial documents. It evaluates LLMs' accuracy in critical financial tasks beyond basic analytics, focusing on their ability to ensure document integrity.

title: Large Language Models Pass the History Exam But Miss the <<History>>: A Polish High School Exit Exam Matura Benchmark
summary: This paper introduces the "Matura Benchmark," evaluating eight leading Large Language Models on their ability to pass Polish high school history exit exams. It specifically assesses interpretative historical reasoning rather than just factual knowledge.

title: Predicting consumer-technology ownership without a diffusion history
summary: This study investigates whether the perceived attributes of consumer technology can predict ownership without historical diffusion data. It utilizes both human survey responses and ratings from frontier language models, including Anthropic Claude Opus, to analyze this predictive capability.

title: New Terms, New Toxicity: Consensus-based Chinese Neologism Toxicity Detection via Search-Augmented LLMs
summary: This paper introduces a method for consensus-based Chinese neologism toxicity detection using search-augmented Large Language Models. It addresses the challenge of identifying evolving toxic expressions in new terms that pose difficulties for traditional moderation systems.

title: Are you Talking Logic to Me? Assessing Language Models Syllogistic Reasoning Capabilities
summary: This research assesses the syllogistic reasoning capabilities of language models, which often struggle with logical tasks. It investigates how different formal Knowledge Representation notations impact models' ability to solve these reasoning challenges.

title: Query Timing Produces Opposite Positional Biases Between LLMs and Humans
summary: This study examines positional biases, such as recency and primacy effects, in Large Language Models compared to humans, specifically investigating how query timing can produce opposite biases. It aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of these evaluation biases in LLMs.

title: Unified Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Complex Graph Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a unified multi-dimensional benchmark designed to evaluate the complex graph reasoning abilities of Large Language Models. It aims to address the limitations of existing benchmarks by providing a more comprehensive testbed for various graph reasoning tasks.

title: DIVE: Unlocking Self-Improvement in Frozen Language Models Through Diversity-Driven Skill Evolution
summary: This research introduces DIVE, a diversity-driven framework enabling "frozen" Large Language Models to achieve self-improvement. DIVE allows LLMs to evolve persistent natural-language skills from task experience and verifier feedback without requiring parameter updates.

title: When Explanations Betray Backdoors: Black-Box Auditing for Language Model Classifiers
summary: This paper investigates black-box auditing for language model classifiers, demonstrating how explanations provided by these models can inadvertently "betray backdoors." It explores methods for detecting such vulnerabilities even with limited information.

title: LLMs Are Not Good Strategists, Yet Memory-Enhanced Agency Boosts Reasoning
summary: This research finds that while Large Language Models struggle with strategic reasoning in long-horizon environments, integrating memory-enhanced agency significantly boosts their reasoning capabilities. This memory integration helps overcome limitations like inconsistent subgoals and strategic drift.

title: Novels generated by language models show compressed formal variation
summary: This study analyzes novels generated by Large Language Models, finding that their output shows compressed formal variation across multiple generations. It investigates the stylistic diversity of AI-generated long-form content, rather than focusing on individual passage detection.

title: Excess Separability: Nuisance-Controlled Residual-Stream Probing for Benchmark Contamination Detection
summary: This paper introduces "Excess Separability," a nuisance-controlled residual-stream probing method for benchmark contamination detection. It offers an alternative approach to diagnosing contamination, addressing limitations of existing methods that often require unavailable training data or foresight.

title: ERSkill: Evolving for Skill-Guided Adaptive Memory Retrieval
summary: This research introduces ERSkill, a framework for evolving skill-guided adaptive memory retrieval in Large Language Model agents. It addresses the static nature of current memory retrieval mechanisms by making them evolvable, thereby improving performance on diverse memory queries.

title: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
summary: This paper introduces PatientAct, a theory-grounded mental health client simulation system utilizing LLMs. It aims to create more realistic simulated clients for training novice counselors and evaluating LLM therapists, addressing limitations of overly cooperative existing simulators.

title: ViTOED: A Dataset for Target-Oriented Emotion Detection on Vietnamese Social Media Texts
summary: This paper introduces ViTOED, a novel dataset for target-oriented emotion detection in Vietnamese social media texts, comprising over 10,000 user comments and 21,000 manually annotated opinion quadruples. This dataset aims to support research in natural language processing for low-resource languages.

title: CRAFT: LLM-Based Iterative Refinement for Temporal Reasoning over Clinical Narratives
summary: This paper introduces CRAFT, an LLM-based iterative refinement framework for temporal reasoning over clinical narratives. CRAFT aims to understand the temporal progression of symptoms from clinical texts, which is crucial for disease monitoring and safety surveillance.

title: FastThaiG2P: Lightning-fast Thai Grapheme-to-phoneme Conversion for Voice Agent Pipelines
summary: FastThaiG2P is a fast Thai grapheme-to-phoneme conversion model designed for text-to-speech pipelines, supporting International Phonetic Alphabet and Kokoro-TTS conventions. It uses a PyThaiNLP-tokenized, extensible dictionary and normalization rules for Central Thai speech.

title: From Atomic Evidence to Logical Composition: Structured Compositional Reasoning over Compound Answer Options
summary: This research introduces a framework to improve large language models' ability to perform structured compositional reasoning over compound answer options involving logical operators like AND, OR, and NEITHER/NOR. It addresses LLM failures when combining atomic judgments correctly.

title: Falsehood and Impossibility Are Different Directions in an AI's Representation of Language
summary: This paper reports an exploratory activation study on the multimodal open-weight model Gemma 3 4B IT, investigating whether AI models internally distinguish between false and impossible linguistic statements.

title: The Embedder's Dilemma: LLMs Are Better, but at What Cost?
summary: This paper provides a controlled, cost-aware comparison of ten large language models and 26 embedding models across 37 tasks, including classification, semantic textual similarity, and clustering. It evaluates whether LLMs are better for text-embedding pipelines and at what cost.

title: When Your Agent Opens the Chat App: Agent-Controlled Search over Raw Chat Logs Rivals Structured Memory
summary: This research investigates whether agent-controlled search over raw chat logs can rival structured memory systems for retrieval quality, questioning how much of the benefit of structured memory comes from the structure itself.

title: BavGround: A Benchmark for Regional Cultural Grounding and Dialect Competence in Bavarian
summary: BavGround is a new benchmark introduced for evaluating large language models' regional cultural grounding and dialect competence in Bavarian, addressing the underrepresentation of regional cultures in LLM evaluation.

title: Prompts in the Wild: A Large Analyzed Collection of Transactional Prompts in Code
summary: This paper presents a large analyzed collection of transactional prompts found in code, arguing that prompts for generative Large Language Models are linguistic objects deserving of investigation.

title: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting
summary: This paper introduces Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting, a method to improve generation quality and accelerate Contrastive Decoding by addressing the proposal-alignment question in speculative decoding.

title: Unifying Depth and Width Pruning for LLMs via Binary Knapsack Optimization
summary: This paper presents SNIPER, a two-stage structured pruning framework that unifies depth and width pruning for large language models using binary knapsack optimization. It aims to improve upon greedy heuristics for model compression.

title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation
summary: LycheeMemory V2 proposes an efficient long-term memory system for LLM agents, utilizing semantic segment-level consolidation to reduce the cost of memory construction compared to eager consolidation methods.

title: HybridRAG-BN: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework with Fine-Tuned Verification for Bangla KBQA
summary: HybridRAG-BN is a new retrieval-augmented framework with fine-tuned verification designed for Knowledge-Base Question Answering (KBQA) in Bangla, aiming to address challenges in low-resource languages.

title: RAGSieve: Self-Referenced Local Contrast for Knowledge-Poison Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: RAGSieve introduces a self-referenced local contrast method for detecting knowledge-poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. It aims to identify maliciously injected documents that promote attacker-chosen claims without relying on external references.

title: CASA: Content-Acoustic Speaking Assessment with Speech Encoder and Large Language Model
summary: CASA is a Content-Acoustic Speaking Assessment system that uses a speech encoder and a large language model to evaluate speaking performance. It provides analysis of how acoustic and content information contribute to predictions in multimodal speech LLMs.

title: LigBench: A Unified and Human-Aligned Benchmark for LLM-based Research Idea Generation
summary: LigBench is introduced as a unified and human-aligned benchmark for evaluating large language model-based research idea generation. It addresses current fragmented evaluation practices for assessing novel research proposals.

title: Better Decomposition, Free Aggregation: A Synthesizer-Folding Framework for Multilingual Multi-Hop Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces a Synthesizer-Folding Framework for Multilingual Multi-Hop Question Answering, designed to improve multilingual retrieval-augmented generation by enabling large language models to access globally distributed external knowledge.

title: Which LLM Is Your Ideal Companion? Evaluating Emotional Companion Capabilities of LLMs Based on Adult Attachment Theory
summary: This research evaluates the emotional companion capabilities of large language models based on Adult Attachment Theory. It assesses their behavior in intimate relationships to understand their suitability for emotional companionship.

title: GEM: A Generative Embedding Model Bridging Reasoning and Retrieval
summary: GEM is a new Generative Embedding Model designed to bridge reasoning and retrieval for large language models, addressing the gap between how users express complex information needs and how conventional retrievers operate.

title: Localize, Then Reason: Visual Latent Structural Reasoning for Molecular Properties and Edits
summary: This research proposes a method for visual latent structural reasoning for molecular properties and edits, improving LLM-based chemical reasoning by combining local chemical perception with property reasoning from molecular images.

title: Self-Referential Induction Increases Response Instability Relative to Unresolvable and Verifiable Questions in Large Language Models
summary: This paper investigates how self-referential induction affects the response instability of large language models compared to unresolvable and verifiable questions, measuring the consistency of reports resembling subjective experience.

title: How Do VLMs Behave When Blind or Misled? Behavioral Evaluation of VLMs on Scientific Figures
summary: This research conducts a behavioral evaluation of vision-language models on scientific figures to understand their reliability when visual evidence is missing or misleading, addressing their behavior under uncertainty.

title: Mixture of Training: Recombining Small-Scale Scaffolded Pretraining Runs into a Larger Language Model
summary: This paper introduces Mixture of Training (MoT), a scaffolded modular pre-training procedure that allows language models to be trained by recombining smaller, independently trained jobs into a larger, coherent model.

title: HIMEC: Directional Change Representation and Fixed-Interface Decoding for Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning
summary: This research presents HIMEC, a method for remote sensing image change captioning that converts bitemporal imagery into sentences describing semantic changes by using directional change representation and fixed-interface decoding.

title: Can Vision-Language Models Assess Proxemic Risk from Egocentric Robot Images?
summary: This study evaluates three open-source vision-language models (InternVL, Qwen-VL, and SmolVLM) on their ability to assess proxemic risk from a robot's egocentric perspective, which is crucial for safe embodied navigation.

title: Surface-to-Skeleton 3D Cephalometry: Estimating Hidden Skeletal Landmarks from CT-Derived External Soft-Tissue Surfaces
summary: This research proposes a method for 3D cephalometry to estimate hidden internal skeletal landmarks from external soft-tissue surfaces derived from CT scans, addressing limitations of existing facial-landmark methods.

title: StrAD: A Streaming Method and Benchmark for Audio Description Generation for Long-form Videos
summary: This work introduces StrAD, a streaming method and a new benchmark for generating audio descriptions for long-form videos, aiming to improve accessibility for blind and low-vision individuals by narrating visual events during natural audio pauses.

title: Attribute-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization for Controllable Fashion Retrieval
summary: This paper proposes Attribute-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization, a new method for controllable fashion retrieval that allows satisfying multiple attributes simultaneously, unlike monolithic embeddings that hinder specific control.

title: PseudoMapLabeler: Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Label Generation for Semi-Supervised Online Mapping
summary: This paper introduces PseudoMapLabeler, a teacher-student semi-supervised learning framework that generates confidence-aware pseudo-labels for online HD map construction, addressing the challenge of scarce labeled training data in diverse environments.

title: From Visual Widgets to UI Code: Efficient Tool-Grounded Generation
summary: This research explores efficient tool-grounded generation to improve screenshot-to-code systems, aiming to reduce hallucination in direct multimodal generation by using structured pipelines with component-wise decomposition and customized representations.

title: EgoCITE: Context-Augmented Indexing and Time-Aware Retrieval for Long-Horizon Egocentric Memory
summary: This paper introduces EgoCITE, a system that uses context-augmented indexing and time-aware retrieval to improve long-horizon egocentric memory, addressing bottlenecks in existing systems that transform continuous first-person video and audio into searchable records.

title: Inference-Time Orthogonal Seeding Enables Geometry-Aligned 3D Organ Segmentation for Slice-Propagation Methods
summary: This research proposes inference-time orthogonal seeding to enable geometry-aligned 3D organ segmentation for slice-propagation methods, aiming to reduce the burden of dense voxel-level annotation in medical imaging.

title: Mr3D-VL: A generalist vision language foundation model for Multiparametric 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging
summary: This paper introduces Mr3D-VL, a generalist vision-language foundation model designed for multiparametric 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging (mpMRI) to improve brain tumor diagnosis and treatment by enabling natural language interaction and interpretability.

title: VOS-Agent: The 1st Place Solution for the 8th LSVOS Challenge (MOSEv2 Track)
summary: This article describes VOS-Agent, the first-place solution for the 8th LSVOS Challenge (MOSEv2 Track), which addresses complex video object segmentation requiring robust target propagation under severe occlusion, disappearance, and reappearance.

title: A Generative Approach for Improving Multi-Label Defect Classification in Photovoltaic Modules
summary: This paper proposes a generative approach to improve multi-label defect classification in electroluminescence images of photovoltaic cells, addressing the learning ambiguity caused by co-occurring defects during model training.

title: Dual-Manifold Geometry Guided Representation Learning: Adaptive Coupling between Kernel and Data Spaces
summary: This paper introduces a dual-manifold perspective for deep representation learning, focusing on the structured geometry embedded in network parameters and proposing an adaptive coupling between kernel and data spaces within convolutional layers.

title: Dual-Stream Cross-Anchor Correction Grounding Long-Form Captions and the Domain Limits of Object-Level Anchors
summary: This research addresses object hallucination in multimodal large language models by proposing a Dual-Stream Cross-Anchor Correction Grounding method for long-form captions, aiming to better tie individual object mentions to visual evidence.

title: Scaling Representation Diversity: Modulated Attention and Reconstructive Regularization for Visual Grounding
summary: This work re-examines Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) from an open-vocabulary grounding perspective, proposing Modulated Attention and Reconstructive Regularization to scale representation diversity and improve cross-dataset generalization.

title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
summary: This paper introduces SCOPE, a method for Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention, aiming to reduce the quadratic self-attention cost in Diffusion Transformers over spatiotemporal tokens.

title: Beyond Correctness: Benchmarking and Aligning Response Behaviors in Hybrid-Thinking MLLMs
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking and aligning response behaviors in hybrid-thinking multimodal large language models (MLLMs), ensuring that different inference modes meet the same user-facing standards beyond mere correctness.

title: Erase but Preserve: Controllable Removal of Copyrighted Animation Characters via Optimized Semantic Anchors
summary: This paper presents a method for controllable removal of copyrighted animation characters from text-to-image diffusion models using optimized semantic anchors, addressing copyright concerns related to unauthorized reproduction.

title: Structured Local Differential Modeling for AI-Generated Image Detection
summary: This paper proposes Structured Local Differential Modeling for AI-Generated Image Detection, a new method to reliably detect AI-generated content by overcoming the dominance of semantically salient components in existing detection methods.

title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: This research introduces LocusGS, a method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that uses spatially grounded tokens and learnable queries to represent and decode 3D scenes more effectively.

title: Semantic Steering for Controllable Generation: Tuning-Free Concept Erasure in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
summary: This paper presents a method for controllable generation in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) to enable tuning-free concept erasure and address safety concerns in text-to-image generation.

title: Heterogeneous Vision-Language Ensemble with Disagreement-Aware Reranking for Text-Based Person Anomaly Retrieval
summary: This work proposes a heterogeneous vision-language ensemble with disagreement-aware reranking to improve text-based person anomaly retrieval from large image galleries using natural language descriptions.

title: SPARED: Reasoning-Based AI-Generated Image Detection via Adversarially Edited Data
summary: This research introduces SPARED, a reasoning-based method for detecting AI-generated images that also justifies its verdicts, addressing limitations of existing detectors regarding provenance shortcuts and explanations.

title: NaviDC-OCR: Navigating Document Parsing Across Digital and Camera-Captured Documents
summary: This paper introduces NaviDC-OCR, an approach that uses Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to navigate document parsing across both digital and camera-captured documents, addressing existing challenges in the field.

title: HounsWorld: A Multimodal World Model for Hidden Patient-State Readout, Reconstruction, and Simulation
summary: HounsWorld is presented as a multimodal world model designed for clinical intelligence, enabling the estimation of a patient's hidden state, reconstruction, and simulation from incomplete medical observations and language.

title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs
summary: This study explores and proposes methods to mitigate relational privacy leakage in document Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly focusing on their unique vulnerabilities in identity document processing.

title: TennisVAR: A Stroke-Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Large Language Model for Tactical Reasoning in Tennis Videos
summary: TennisVAR is introduced as a stroke-evidence-grounded Multimodal Large Language Model developed for tactical reasoning in tennis videos, moving beyond individual stroke perception to explain match progression.

title: A Deep RL based Framework for Targeted White Matter Tractography
summary: This paper proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning-based framework for targeted white matter tractography, aiming to reconstruct the brain's structural pathways more effectively for neuroimaging applications.

title: DiCoR: Decoupled Referent Disambiguation and Contour Recalibration for Efficient Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
summary: DiCoR is presented as a method for efficient referring remote sensing image segmentation, which decouples referent disambiguation and contour recalibration to delineate targets specified by natural language.

title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
summary: This research analyzes PixSDS, explaining why latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) causes noisy pixels in text-to-3D generation due to VAE-induced pixel drift.

title: Structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D Plant Modeling
summary: This paper introduces a novel framework using structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D plant modeling, reconstructing continuous geometric and topological plant evolution from sparse temporal observations.

title: RGB-D Video Generation for Improving Human-to-Robot Object Handover Prediction
summary: This work focuses on RGB-D video generation to improve human-to-robot (H2R) object handover prediction, introducing the Hand2Bot dataset to address data scarcity and the sim-to-real gap in human-robot collaboration.

title: UniTraffic-Agent: Unified Traffic Video Reasoning for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 3 with Two Out-of-Domain Evaluations
summary: UniTraffic-Agent is introduced as a unified traffic video reasoning system for the AI City Challenge, designed to understand and explain traffic events in intelligent transportation.

title: Spatially-Grounded Text-to-Video Generation via Inference-Time Gradient-Free Optimization
summary: This research focuses on achieving spatially-grounded text-to-video generation using Diffusion Transformer models, employing inference-time gradient-free optimization to improve fine-grained spatial controllability.

title: P2Fusion: Prompt-based Progressive Infrared-Visible Image Fusion via Dual-Prior Distillation
summary: P2Fusion proposes a prompt-based progressive infrared-visible image fusion method that uses dual-prior distillation to reconcile information disparity for multimodal perception, addressing limitations of static constraints.

title: Topology-Unified 2D Pose Estimation across Intact, Residual and Prosthetic Limbs
summary: This paper presents a topology-unified 2D pose estimation method that addresses representation bias in benchmarks by enabling accurate pose estimation across individuals with intact, residual, and prosthetic limbs.

title: Learning Unified Video and Image Representation for Video Face Forgery Detection
summary: This research focuses on learning unified video and image representations to improve video face forgery detection, aiming to preserve the security and integrity of facial data against deep generative models.

title: Paths: Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer with Hierarchical Multi-modal Fusion for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification
summary: Paths introduces a prompt-aware spatio-temporal Transformer with hierarchical multi-modal fusion for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification (RE-VReID), improving person tracking across non-overlapping cameras.

title: RbFT-Net: Rectify-Before-Fuse Temporal Radar Anchors for 4D Radar-Camera Depth Completion
summary: This paper introduces RbFT-Net, a network architecture that rectifies and fuses temporal radar anchors for 4D radar-camera depth completion, providing dense metric depth prediction for autonomous systems.

title: Towards Physics-Faithful Generation of Scientific Diagrams
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of current text-to-image models in generating scientifically accurate diagrams, focusing on the need for physical faithfulness over photorealistic quality. It highlights the unreliability of state-of-the-art systems for tasks requiring correct force directions or valid coordinate systems.

title: EgoMonth: A Month-Level Egocentric Video Benchmark for Long-Term Spatiotemporal Memory
summary: EgoMonth is introduced as a new month-level egocentric video benchmark designed to evaluate long-term spatiotemporal memory in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It aims to address the limitations of existing benchmarks that lack inter-clip spatiotemporal continuity in web-sourced videos.

title: QuISE: Defense against Typographic Attacks on VLMs via Query-Irrelevant Semantic Editing
summary: This research introduces QuISE, a defense mechanism against typographic attacks that trick Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by injecting misleading text into images. The method aims to prevent models from relying on adversarial textual cues instead of visual evidence without requiring extensive model modifications or retraining.

title: Predicting Signed Distance Functions for Visual Instance Segmentation
summary: This research proposes a method for visual instance segmentation that predicts Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) to better handle objects with unconstrained shapes. It aims to improve segmentation accuracy for items that are not well described by traditional bounding box approaches, such as long or slender objects.

title: MergeOver: Post-Training Token Merging for Recursive Vision Transformers
summary: MergeOver is presented as a post-training token merging technique designed to reduce the quadratic computational complexity and large parameter counts of Vision Transformers (ViTs). This method aims to enable the deployment of high-performing ViTs on resource-constrained edge hardware.

title: Geometry-Grounded Unified 3D Perception for Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper proposes a geometry-grounded unified 3D perception framework for camera-based autonomous driving, aiming to preserve metric 3D structure across multi-camera streams. It addresses limitations of existing image-based frameworks that often rely on semantic recognition pretraining before introducing 3D geometry.

title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
summary: TRAPSBench is introduced as a new procedurally generated video benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language Models' (VLMs) ability to exhibit epistemic restraint. The research shows that while VLMs can internally recognize when abstention is needed due to occluded or chaotic visual evidence, they often fail to express this.

title: A Controlled Study of Self-Supervised Image and Video Pretraining under Limited Resources
summary: This research presents a controlled study investigating the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining for visual foundation models under limited data and computational resources. The goal is to determine if significant benefits can be achieved with more sustainable pretraining scales, rather than requiring vast data and compute.

title: RoboSynChallenge: Mastering Real-World Dexterity via Generalizing Synthesized Manipulation Skills
summary: RoboSynChallenge is introduced as a competition platform aiming to advance generalizable robotic manipulation by encouraging the transfer of synthesized skills to real-world dexterity. It addresses the limitation of scarce and diverse real-world data in embodied intelligence.

title: Attune: A Self-Annotation Tool for Understanding Robot Operator Attention Profiles
summary: Attune is presented as a self-annotation tool designed to understand and manage human operator attention profiles when supervising multiple robot fleets in complex environments. The tool aims to address challenges in designing multi-robot supervision interfaces by analyzing operator focus.

title: Genetic Fuzzy System-Based Multi-Robot Coordination for Planetary Missions
summary: This paper proposes a decentralized multi-robot system (MRS) coordination approach for collaborative object transportation tasks in unstructured environments. The method utilizes a genetic fuzzy system to minimize total path length and avoid obstacles, particularly for applications like planetary missions.

title: AirForesight: Current-to-Future Spatial Map Imagination with Cross-Space Planning Consistency for UAV-VLN
summary: AirForesight is introduced as a system for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Vision-Language Navigation (UAV-VLN), enabling agents to imagine future spatial maps from current observations. It focuses on achieving cross-space planning consistency, allowing drones to follow language instructions and execute feasible 3D motion in complex outdoor environments.

title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving
summary: BrainWAM is proposed as an approach for autonomous driving that coordinates semantic priors from Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with predictive dynamics for comprehensive planning. It aims to integrate both semantic reasoning and predictive motion, which existing end-to-end driving approaches often address separately.

title: HumanoidVLN: A Physics-Grounded Simulator and Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation Across Diverse Humanoid Embodiments
summary: HumanoidVLN is presented as a physics-grounded simulator and benchmark designed for Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) in humanoid robots. It addresses the unique challenges of bipedal locomotion, varying humanoid morphologies, and locomotion-induced observation distortions that existing benchmarks for wheeled agents do not cover.

title: AMR-Pose: An Active LED Marker-Based Relative Pose Estimation Framework With Probabilistic Switching PnP for Cooperative AUVs
summary: AMR-Pose is introduced as an active LED marker-based framework for reliable relative pose estimation between cooperative Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). It aims to overcome challenges in robust vision-based localization in underwater environments, critical for cooperative ocean exploration and multi-robot coordination.

title: Temporal GRPO: Beyond Trajectory-Level Credit in Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces Temporal GRPO, a method that refines credit assignment in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) reinforcement learning beyond trajectory-level advantages. It aims to improve outcome-driven post-training of VLA policies from sparse task-success feedback.

title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
summary: H2R-Bench is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating human-to-robot manipulation video generation within world models. It addresses the challenge of transferring abundant egocentric human manipulation data to robot learning, which typically suffers from expensive and hard-to-scale robot demonstrations.

title: Semantic Radiance Fields as Simulators for Spatial Reasoning in Real-World Scenes
summary: This research proposes using Semantic Radiance Fields as simulators to train and evaluate spatial reasoning in embodied agents within real-world scenes. The method aims to provide diverse environments that are both geometrically faithful and semantically queryable, overcoming limitations of purely synthetic or reconstructed simulators.

title: Manufacturing Complex Airtight Soft Pneumatic Actuators for Soft Robotics: Process Evaluation and Optimization
summary: This study focuses on evaluating and optimizing manufacturing processes for complex airtight soft pneumatic actuators used in soft robotics. It addresses the challenges of achieving geometric fidelity, compliance, structural integrity, and airtightness simultaneously in fabrication.

title: Predictive Relative-Velocity Steering for Safe Robotic Manipulator Teleoperation in Dynamic Environments
summary: This paper introduces Predictive Relative-Velocity Steering as a method to enhance safe robotic manipulator teleoperation in dynamic environments. It aims to help human operators avoid suddenly appearing obstacles more effectively, especially under challenging conditions like network latency or limited attention.

title: NestDex: Nested Policy Learning with Copilot Assisted Teleoperation for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: This research introduces Nested Policy Learning with Copilot Assisted Teleoperation (NestDex) to improve dexterous manipulation in robots by addressing challenges in collecting consistent, complete-task demonstrations.

title: FIRE-VLA: Failure-Informed Self-Evolution for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper presents FIRE-VLA, a method for failure-informed self-evolution of vision-language-action models to enhance autonomous driving through reinforcement learning and relative policy optimization.

title: ContactGuard: Pre-Contact Execution Monitoring with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models
summary: ContactGuard is introduced as a method for pre-contact execution monitoring in robots, using action-conditioned latent world models to prevent failures in contact-rich manipulation tasks before they occur.

title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
summary: This research explores methods for decoding task progress directly from internal representations within Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, applying mechanistic interpretability to understand their internal workings and monitor runtime.

title: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark
summary: HumanTracker is a proposed benchmark for evaluating humanoid motion tracking that aims to align evaluation metrics more closely with human perception of physical artifacts and stability, improving over traditional kinematic error averages.

title: Excitation-Supervised Closed-Loop Self-Calibration and Target Seeking for an Unknown-Pose Range-Bearing Relay
summary: This work presents a method for a vehicle to self-calibrate and seek a hidden target via an unknown-pose range-bearing relay, making online decisions about relay trustworthiness and necessary actions.

title: Do LLMs Beat Nash? Testing Decentralized Coordination in Self-Play Multi-Agent Games
summary: This research investigates whether large language model agents can achieve decentralized coordination in self-play multi-agent games without direct communication, exploring their ability to reason about counterparts.

title: Genetic Fuzzy System-based Control for Final Approach of Spacecraft Rendezvous and Proximity Operations
summary: This work details a genetic fuzzy system-based controller for spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations, enabling a chaser spacecraft to autonomously approach a target for in-space servicing.

title: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
summary: DreamX-Phi 1.0 is an action-conditioned video world model for robotic manipulation that predicts future observations given an initial frame, language instruction, and a prescribed sequence of end-effector poses and gripper states.

title: Trajectory Prediction via Bayesian Intention Inference under Unknown Goals and Kinematics
summary: This work introduces an adaptive Bayesian algorithm for real-time trajectory prediction, inferring a target's intentions and motion characteristics even when these are unknown and subject to change.

title: SONIC: Supersizing Motion Tracking for Natural Humanoid Whole-Body Control
summary: SONIC investigates scaling motion tracking for natural humanoid whole-body control, aiming to overcome limitations of current neural controllers that are modest in size and target a limited set of behaviors.

title: APEX: Learning Adaptive High-Platform Traversal for Humanoid Robots
summary: APEX proposes a method for humanoid robots to learn adaptive high-platform traversal, moving beyond common deep reinforcement learning solutions that often result in high-impact jumping and struggle with platforms beyond leg length.

title: SpatialVAM:Spatial-Aware Multi-View Video Diffusion as a Data-Efficient Robot Policy
summary: SpatialVAM is a data-efficient robot policy that utilizes spatial-aware multi-view video diffusion to enable robotic manipulation, addressing the need for understanding both 3D spatial structure and temporal evolution.

title: OpenRC: An Open-Source Robotic Colonoscopy Framework for Multimodal Data Acquisition and Autonomy Research
summary: OpenRC is an open-source robotic colonoscopy framework designed for multimodal data acquisition and autonomy research, facilitating reproducible studies of operator control, instrument motion, and visual feedback.

title: JailWAM: Jailbreaking World Action Models in Robot Control
summary: JailWAM explores potential safety risks of World Action Models (WAMs) in robot control, demonstrating how adversaries could exploit their ability to follow high-level instructions and execute physical actions.

title: Trajectory First: A Curriculum for Discovering Diverse Policies
summary: This research paper introduces "Trajectory First," a reinforcement learning curriculum for discovering diverse policies, aiming to make agents more robust and less prone to local optima by training a set of diverse agents in parallel.

title: RadarGen: Automotive Radar Point Cloud Generation from Cameras
summary: This research introduces RadarGen, a diffusion model that synthesizes realistic automotive radar point clouds using multi-view camera imagery, adapting image-latent diffusion for the radar domain.

title: Safe Exploration via Policy Priors
summary: This research paper proposes a method for "safe exploration" in reinforcement learning, allowing agents to learn and adapt online by utilizing suboptimal but conservative policy priors.

title: Training Non-Differentiable Networks via Optimal Transport
summary: This research explores a new method for training non-differentiable networks by optimizing losses that exhibit jumps, where traditional backpropagation methods are ineffective.

title: LOCUS-DT: Localization via Observation-Conditioned Uncertainty Scoring with Digital Twins
summary: This research paper introduces LOCUS-DT, a method for accurate indoor localization using observation-conditioned uncertainty scoring with digital twins, primarily for robotic navigation and search and rescue applications.
