summary: Apple is reportedly collaborating with Alibaba to develop a China-specific AI model, deepening their partnership around Qwen technology.

title: JPMorgan: GLM-5.3 Upgrade and DeepSeek Price Hike Reshape China’s AI Landscape; Raises Target Prices for Zhipu AI and MiniMax - 富途牛牛
summary: JPMorgan reports on the GLM-5.3 upgrade and DeepSeek price hike, which are reshaping China's AI market, and has raised target prices for Zhipu AI and MiniMax.

title: Inducing Reward-Free Judging Rubrics that Reduce Over-Crediting in Agent Evaluation
summary: New research proposes methods for inducing reward-free judging rubrics to reduce over-crediting in the evaluation of language-model agents.

title: Depth-Aware Sensitivity Analysis of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Magnitude-Based Expert Masking
summary: A scientific paper presents a depth-aware sensitivity analysis method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models using magnitude-based expert masking to characterize layer importance.

title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models
summary: This paper explores whether a modular cognitive architecture, similar to the human brain, is an emergent property or a necessary design principle for large language models. It investigates the functional specialization within LLMs for different reasoning types.

title: A Year in LLM Serving: Workload Evolution, Caching and Load-Balancing
summary: This study analyzes a year of large language model (LLM) serving workloads, focusing on critical aspects like caching and load-balancing in cloud environments. It highlights the need for better data to motivate and benchmark serving systems.

title: Agentao: A Governed Local-First Runtime for Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: Agentao is introduced as a governed, local-first runtime designed for tool-using LLM agents, aiming to mitigate risks like over-privileged actions and prompt injection. It supports agents in invoking tools, modifying local state, and using persistent memory.

title: AI Evaluation Should Work With Humans
summary: This position paper argues that current AI evaluation paradigms, focused on superhuman autonomous performance, are misguiding AI development. It advocates for a shift towards evaluating AI performance in collaboration with humans.

title: Stable Miscalibration in Large Language Models: A Practical View of High-Confidence Errors
summary: This research studies "stable miscalibration" in large language models, where confident incorrect answers persist even under minor perturbations. It challenges the view that high-confidence errors solely indicate fragile internal inference.

title: Measuring Cross-Task Behavioral Consistency in Language Model Agents
summary: This paper introduces the Behavioral Consistency Metric (BCM) to measure the cross-task behavioral consistency of language model agents. It argues that agent evaluation needs to go beyond mere outcome metrics like success rate.

title: Cross-Disciplinary Taxonomy and Modeling of Misunderstanding Generation, Amplification, and Detection, from Pragmatics to AI Agents
summary: This paper proposes a cross-disciplinary taxonomy and modeling approach for understanding the generation, amplification, and detection of misunderstandings, particularly in AI-mediated communication channels. It highlights the urgency of solving misunderstanding detection in increasingly automated interactions.

title: Active Perception for Embodied Disambiguation
summary: This research explores "active perception" as a method for robots to resolve target ambiguity in embodied environments when using natural language as a task interface. It addresses ambiguity arising from both user intent and missing physical evidence.

title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences
summary: MobileMem is introduced as a system addressing the need for long-term memory in next-generation AI agents that function as persistent personal assistants. These agents need to learn continuously and leverage user-specific experiences.

title: No Universal Signal Predicts Sample-Level LLM Regression under Version Updates
summary: This paper investigates "sample-level regression" in large language models, where updates can cause previously correct answers to become incorrect for individual samples. It finds no universal signal capable of predicting this regression.

title: Evaluating Agentic Learning Harness Capabilities Without Labels via the Scaling Hypothesis
summary: This paper proposes a method for evaluating "Agentic Continual Learning Harnesses" without relying on labeled benchmarks, using the scaling hypothesis. These systems combine LLMs with retrieval or memory to improve from feedback, particularly in cybersecurity.

title: SemPlan: Benchmarking Structured Semantic Planning for LLM-Based Queries over Enterprise Data
summary: SemPlan is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating structured semantic planning in large language model (LLM)-based query systems over enterprise data. It assesses their ability to translate natural language requests into governed, executable actions.

title: How Compliant is Sepsis Treatment? An Expert-Guided Neuro-symbolic Pipeline for Generating Clinical Compliance Insights
summary: This paper presents an expert-guided neuro-symbolic pipeline that utilizes large language models to generate clinical compliance insights for sepsis treatment. The pipeline aims to verify adherence to evidence-based protocols in a safety-critical setting.

title: Algorithm Design and Physician Liability
summary: This article discusses physician liability concerning AI algorithms in clinical decision-making, particularly when algorithms exhibit unequal accuracy across patient groups. It highlights a new liability rule in the US holding healthcare providers responsible in such cases.

title: Your Probabilistic JEPA Is Secretly a Hidden Markov Model: A State-Space Interpretation of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
summary: This paper provides a state-space interpretation of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning (JEPA), demonstrating that a probabilistic JEPA can be understood as a Hidden Markov Model. It shows that PIB-VJEPA shares the same computational roles as an HMM.

title: Reward Machines for Signal Temporal Logic
summary: This paper introduces "Reward Machines for Signal Temporal Logic" as a formal method for specifying real-time properties of real-valued observations and synthesizing controllers. It provides a quantitative robustness score for monitoring satisfaction.

title: A Calibrated Test of Internal Action Maps: State Signals Without Global Affine Closure
summary: This research presents a calibrated test for internal action maps, examining whether hidden state signals can support reusable action maps even without global affine closure. It organizes tests using an evidence lattice and validates a geometric branch.

title: Ontology-Grounded Project Memory for Coding Agents
summary: This paper introduces MOOSEDev, a system that provides coding agents with ontology-grounded project memory to manage and track changes in software development. This addresses the challenge of keeping historical context for agent-generated code.

title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel as LLM Agents Act and Observe
summary: This paper introduces "Second Thought," a paradigm enabling large language model (LLM) agents to reason in parallel while acting and observing. It addresses the limitation of traditional ReAct agents whose reasoning is frozen during action and observation phases.

title: Learning to Assemble Novel Structures with Unfamiliar Parts under Semantic Constraints
summary: This paper describes a neurosymbolic architecture that enables an agent to learn and assemble novel structures using unfamiliar parts under semantic constraints. The architecture leverages embodied conversations and task demonstrations.

title: Coverage Aware Active Evaluation for Failure Discovery with Paired Systems
summary: This research proposes a new method, "Coverage Aware Active Evaluation," to efficiently discover failures in autonomous systems with limited testing budgets, using proxies like simulators.

title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation
summary: This research questions the robustness of circuit-level mechanistic interpretability as evidence for AI system decisions, particularly in satisfying requirements like those in the EU AI Act.

title: Simulation-Aware In-Context Policy Improvement for LLM-Aided Analog Layout Refinement
summary: This paper introduces a method called "Simulation-Aware In-Context Policy Improvement" that uses LLMs to refine analog integrated circuit (IC) layout designs, reducing the need for manual expert tuning.

title: FLARE MCMC: Fidelity-based Layer-Adaptive REcursive proposals for MCMC
summary: This research presents FLARE MCMC, a new technique designed to accelerate Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods for statistical inference in complex models, addressing issues of slow mixing rates and high computational cost.

title: From Passive Delegates to Strategic Negotiators: Reinforcing Social Reasoning in Small Language Models with SocialRL
summary: This research enhances small language models with "SocialRL" to transform them from passive delegates into strategic negotiators, enabling AI agents to handle tasks involving conflicting goals.

title: SDO: Subspace Deconflicting Operator for Multi-Adapter Composition
summary: This paper introduces SDO (Subspace Deconflicting Operator), a method to address identity mixing and attribute leakage when composing multiple adapters within diffusion models for multi-character generation.

title: Joint Optimization of Memory and Computing Frequency for Energy-Efficient DNN Inference
summary: This paper investigates the joint optimization of memory and computing frequency for energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference on mobile devices, addressing latency and energy consumption issues.

title: MemoryLake on MemoryArena: A Matched Study of Agent Memory Backends
summary: This study uses MemoryArena to compare various agent memory backends, including MemoryLake and Mem0, evaluating their effectiveness in supporting interdependent, multi-session task completion.

title: When Personal Memory Has No Single Answer: Evaluating LLM Agents under Irreducible Conflict
summary: This research explores the challenges of evaluating LLM agents when their personal memories contain irreducible conflicts across sessions, highlighting issues arising from context-dependent preferences and evolving behavior.

title: Never the Number: Structural Abstention for AI Systems Whose Answers Are Consumed as Fact
summary: This paper addresses the critical problem of LLM text-to-SQL systems generating fluent but factually incorrect answers, proposing "Structural Abstention" as a method for these AI systems to indicate uncertainty rather than hallucinate.

title: AI Research Preference Models
summary: This research discusses AI research agents (AIRA) that can propose and evaluate machine learning experiments, identifying high evaluation cost as a significant barrier to progress on frontier tasks.

title: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: This paper introduces HELIX, a concept for "model-harness co-evolution" to achieve recursive self-improvement in interactive AI agents by jointly developing the model and its runtime environment for context, tools, and control flow.

title: Implementing Computational Law in Wolfram Language for the Governance of Artificial Intelligence
summary: This paper presents an implementation of computational law in Wolfram Language to govern AI systems by defining their obligations and permissions, and checking for compliance without requiring full inspection of their reasoning.

title: Nanbeige4.2-3B on Apple Silicon: Fixing Deployment Bugs and Decreasing Looped Transformer Memory Overhead
summary: This work identifies and fixes deployment bugs and decreases memory overhead for the Nanbeige4.2-3B agentic model, a Looped Transformer evaluated on Apple Silicon (MPS).

title: Simulation-Driven Vehicular Traffic Data Augmentation: Extending Sensor Coverage Through Virtual Sensing
summary: This research proposes "Simulation-Driven Vehicular Traffic Data Augmentation" to extend sensor coverage in urban traffic management, improving machine learning model generalization despite limited real-world data.

title: Residual Dominance as a Structural Account of Last-Item Reliance in Causal Self-Attention Recommenders
summary: This research explores "Residual Dominance" as a structural explanation for why transformer-based sequential recommenders often over-rely on the most recent interaction at inference time.

title: Agent-Orchestration in Autonomous Chip Design
summary: This paper explores the application of agent-orchestration and tool-using agents for autonomous chip design, aiming to integrate AI effectively into this complex industry.

title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
summary: This paper investigates the nature of "Agent Skills" for enhancing LLM agents, analyzing why they are effective and identifying limitations in current evaluation methodologies.

title: Benchmarking data-driven material models on the classic Treloar dataset
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking various data-driven material models using the classic Treloar dataset to compare their performance in learning and predicting material behavior.

title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining
summary: This research paper explores challenges in scaling high-quality domain data for large language model pretraining, focusing on managing training-token budgets as model sizes increase.

title: Mandato: Protocol-Level Enforcement of Digitally Signed Mandates on AI Agent Actions with Cryptographically Chained Audit Trails
summary: This paper introduces Mandato, a protocol for enforcing digitally signed mandates on AI agent actions using cryptographically chained audit trails, addressing authorization challenges in tool-calling protocols like MCP.

title: A Pathway to General-Purpose Scientific AI: Multimodal Comprehension of Scientific Images
summary: This research explores multimodal AI systems' ability to comprehend scientific images and tables, aiming for general-purpose scientific AI, and references the ALD/E-ImageMiner benchmark and ICDAR 2026 competition.

title: Regime-Conditional Verification: Correctness Estimation for Adapting and Monitoring Safety Classifiers
summary: This paper presents Regime-Conditional Verification (RCV), a method for estimating the correctness and adapting safety classifiers deployed with large language models to address policy misalignment and performance degradation.

title: Retrieval Grounding Latent Reasoning for Dense Retrieval
summary: This research introduces a method for dense retrieval that incorporates latent reasoning into text representations, aiming to improve relevance for reasoning-intensive retrieval tasks by enhancing embedding models.

title: A Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning Framework for Structured Drift Diagnosis and Recovery in Autonomous LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces a graph-based reinforcement learning framework designed to diagnose and recover from runtime behavioral drift in autonomous LLM agents, which can lead to unintended side effects in real-world workflows.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Production Scheduling in an Industry-Based Coating Scenario Using the Digital Model Playground
summary: This research applies reinforcement learning methods to production scheduling in an industrial coating scenario, using a digital model playground to address challenges like sequence-dependent setup times and stochastic disturbances.

title: QuaSAR: Quantization Compensation via Stable Activation-Aware Rank Truncation
summary: This paper introduces QuaSAR, a post-training quantization method that uses stable activation-aware rank truncation and residual compensation to restore model accuracy while constraining additional model storage overhead.

title: Towards Efficient Multimodal and Multilingual Opinion Extraction for STI: A QLoRA-Based Fine-Tuning Approach
summary: This research explores an efficient QLoRA-based fine-tuning approach for large language models to perform multimodal and multilingual opinion extraction for Science and Technology Intelligence, addressing challenges in noise filtering.

title: Removing Temporal Note Redundancy Improves Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Medicine
summary: This research demonstrates that removing temporal note redundancy enhances multimodal reinforcement learning for medical applications, specifically in optimizing mechanical ventilation settings.

title: BiasTrace: Linking Reasoning Behaviours to Biased Outputs in LLMs
summary: This paper introduces BiasTrace, a method designed to link reasoning behaviors within large language models to their biased outputs, aiming to improve the understanding of mechanisms that produce inaccurate and discriminatory inferences.

title: Can Language Models Understand mmWave Data? Benchmarking Large Language Models for mmWave Radar-Based Human Understanding
summary: This research benchmarks large language models for their ability to understand mmWave radar data, exploring their potential as universal reasoning engines for mmWave radar-based human understanding.

title: FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online Moe Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction
summary: This paper introduces FreeBalance, a method for pre-routing online load balancing for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, designed to reduce latency in distributed inference by predicting residual workloads.

title: APTER: Adaptive Post-Training with Expert-Grounded Rubrics
summary: This paper presents APTER (Adaptive Post-Training with Expert-Grounded Rubrics), a method designed to improve large language models' ability to satisfy domain constraints, include critical evidence, and provide complete reasoning in professional applications.

title: Don't Claim Benchmark-Oriented Optimization Improves General Coding Capability -- Diverse Evaluation Is Required
summary: This article critiques the practice of claiming general coding capability improvements based solely on optimization for a small set of coding benchmarks, advocating for more diverse evaluation methods.

title: Training-Free Knowledge Transfer Across Model Scales through Activation-Guided Pruning
summary: This research introduces a training-free method for knowledge transfer across different model scales using activation-guided pruning, enabling a smaller recipient language model to leverage capabilities from a larger donor model despite architectural mismatch.

title: From BERT to Frontier Agents: Eight Years of Language-Model Progress, the Collapse of the Capability-Cost Curve, and the Rise of Task-Targeted Models
summary: This article provides an eight-year overview of language model progress from BERT to frontier agents, analyzing the collapse of the capability-cost curve and the rise of task-targeted models, noting a sharp drop in costs.

title: EEG-PRISM: Physiologically-Grounded Interpretability of Predictions by EEG Foundation Models
summary: This research introduces EEG-PRISM, a method for physiologically-grounded interpretability of predictions from EEG foundation models, addressing the need for universal explainable AI techniques in EEG analysis.

title: SAGE: Surrogate-gradient Adaptation via Attention-Guided Entropy for Spiking Transformers
summary: This paper introduces SAGE, a method for surrogate-gradient adaptation via attention-guided entropy, designed to improve the training of energy-efficient spiking neural networks and spiking transformers.

title: Capacity-Dependent Effects of Data Selection for Reasoning
summary: This research investigates the capacity-dependent effects of data selection in reasoning supervised fine-tuning, suggesting that responses closer to a student's distribution can lead to more effective training.

title: The Integer Alibi: Localizing Cross-Kernel Divergence in INT8-Quantized LLM Inference
summary: This research investigates discrepancies in INT8-quantized LLM inference by swapping GPU kernels (CUTLASS vs Triton) while keeping other factors constant. It aims to localize divergences caused by different kernel implementations.

title: CutClean: Neural Network Pruning for Privacy-Preserving Inference
summary: This paper introduces "CutClean," a neural network pruning technique designed to achieve privacy-preserving inference. It addresses privacy leakage concerns in high-stakes AI applications even when traditional dataset biases are absent.

title: PPAPlace: Differentiable Cross-Stage Objectives for Chip Placement Optimization
summary: This research presents PPAPlace, a method for chip placement optimization using differentiable cross-stage objectives to improve post-route performance, power, and area. It addresses the limitations of traditional methods that primarily optimize half-perimeter wirelength.

title: Recent Advances in Deep Learning-Based Drug-Target Binding Affinity Prediction
summary: This paper reviews recent advancements in deep learning-based methods for predicting drug-target binding affinity. It highlights the importance of this computational approach in drug discovery despite ongoing challenges in accuracy.

title: Dynamic Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing with Online Requests: Event-Driven Transformer--DRL and Rolling-Horizon Benchmarking
summary: This paper introduces an event-driven learning and benchmarking framework using Transformer-DRL for the Dynamic Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem. It trains Masked MLP and Transformer policies for progressively revealed requests and evolving vehicle states.

title: Stochastic Control Policies for Robust Molecular Transition Path Sampling
summary: This research explores stochastic control policies to enhance robust molecular transition path sampling, a method essential for understanding biomolecular mechanisms. It highlights the increasing role of machine learning in improving beyond traditional molecular dynamics sampling.

title: HI-MeshGraphNets: Efficient and Accurate Mesh-based Physics Learning with Hierarchical Multi-scale Graph Neural Networks
summary: This paper presents HI-MeshGraphNets, a new hierarchical multi-scale Graph Neural Network for efficient and accurate mesh-based physics learning. It offers a promising alternative to traditional numerical solvers by leveraging GNNs for simulating physical systems.

title: Federated Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework, Empirical Analysis, and Future Directions
summary: This paper proposes "Federated Prompt Learning," a unified framework addressing challenges in LLM training and deployment such as high computational costs, data centralization, and privacy concerns. It offers a decentralized approach to leverage LLMs effectively.

title: Geometric Filtering of LLM-Generated Samples for Few-Shot Text Classification
summary: This paper introduces a geometric filtering framework to improve the quality of LLM-generated synthetic training data for few-shot text classification. It filters samples based on their position in the embedding space to ensure they fall into correct class regions.

title: Fashion Outfit Generation via Unified Sequential Composition Models
summary: This research addresses the challenge of fashion outfit generation by proposing unified sequential composition models. It aims to synthesize stylistically coherent outfits from large item libraries despite the complex nature of aesthetic compatibility.

title: MedMix: Specialization-Consistent Federated Sparse MoEs under Modality Heterogeneity
summary: This paper introduces MedMix, a framework for specialization-consistent federated sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoEs) designed for multimodal medical AI. It addresses the challenges of modality heterogeneity across clients and individual samples.

title: CForce: Boosting Parallel Decoding for dLLMs via Consistency Forcing
summary: This paper introduces CForce, a technique that boosts parallel decoding for diffusion large language models (dLLMs) by applying consistency forcing. It aims to mitigate unreliable predictions and error propagation during aggressive parallelism in early denoising stages.

title: Post-training Quantization for Hybrid Iterative Generative Models
summary: This research investigates Post-training Quantization (PTQ) for Hybrid Iterative Generative Models, which combine autoregressive and diffusion paradigms. The goal is to reduce the substantial computational overhead incurred by their iterative inference.

title: Probabilistic indirect models for undrained shear strength: addressing significant data missing and variability with advanced imputation and machine learning techniques
summary: This study develops probabilistic indirect models for undrained shear strength (su) in geotechnical design, leveraging advanced imputation and machine learning techniques. It addresses significant data missingness and variability using the CLAY/10/7490 global database.

title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction
summary: This paper presents QUASAR, a method that lowers the loss floor of Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) for large language model inference using Loss-Aware Reconstruction. It aims to preserve model quality as inference shifts to lower precision.

title: Identifiability and Order-Dimension Limits of In-Context Learning on Partial Orders
summary: This theoretical paper develops a framework for in-context learning on partial orders, analyzing its identifiability and order-dimension limits. It investigates how finite prompts determine queried comparisons given transitivity, antisymmetry, and incomparability.

title: Adversarial Learning of Classifier-Free Guidance Schedules
summary: This research explores adversarial learning to optimize classifier-free guidance (CFG) schedules for text-to-image diffusion models. It aims to address the suboptimal nature of static CFG, which can introduce artifacts and limit image fidelity.

title: Model-agnostic Retrieval-Augmented Extended Forecasting for time series
summary: This paper introduces a model-agnostic retrieval-augmented extended forecasting method for time series, leveraging pretrained foundation models and RAG. It addresses the challenge of achieving optimal performance with short historical data in domain-specific applications.

title: When Denoising Hurts: Rethinking the Terminal Step of Diffusion Time Series Forecasters -- Extended Version
summary: This research challenges the assumption of uniformly beneficial iterative sampling in diffusion time series forecasters by analyzing how forecast quality evolves during reverse diffusion. It finds that denoising can sometimes negatively impact performance.

title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models
summary: This paper identifies and analyzes "forecast collapse," an unexpected phenomenon where predictions from time-series foundation models become nearly flat and show poor stock ranking. This occurs when forecasting hourly returns for equities.

title: Learning to Run Power Networks: Effective AlphaZero-inspired Topological Control
summary: This research applies Reinforcement Learning, inspired by AlphaZero, to autonomously control and stabilize power grids by reconfiguring their topology, addressing challenges from volatile renewable energy sources.

title: From Fixed Grids to Moving Particles:A Transferable Latent Operator for Fluid Dynamics
summary: This paper explores a transferable latent operator for fluid dynamics, focusing on Lagrangian modeling which characterizes particle transport and complements Eulerian descriptions, often using neural operators.

title: Overcoming Shortcut Learning in Graph Neural Networks through Active Explanation Guidance
summary: This research introduces XIGL, an architecture-agnostic method, to overcome shortcut learning in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) by guiding them away from non-causal correlations, thereby improving their reliability in out-of-distribution tasks.

title: Smart routes: a system for development and comparison of algorithms for solving vehicle routing problems with realistic constraints
summary: This paper proposes a system for developing and comparing algorithms to solve vehicle routing problems with realistic constraints, addressing the increasing relevance of route optimization due to global urban population growth.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning solution for pickup and delivery routing problems with time window and capacity constraints
summary: This research presents a Deep Reinforcement Learning solution for optimizing vehicle routes in pickup and delivery problems, considering time window and capacity constraints, which is crucial for efficient logistics in growing urban areas.

title: Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network for Traffic Flow Prediction
summary: This paper introduces a Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network designed for traffic flow prediction, leveraging deep spatiotemporal models, graph convolutions, and attention mechanisms to capture complex dependencies.

title: Revisiting Energy-based Tabular Anomaly Detection: Energy and Reconstruction are Complementary
summary: This research re-examines energy-based tabular anomaly detection, comparing it with classical and modern methods, and suggests that energy and reconstruction approaches are complementary in approximating inlier distributions.

title: KV Cache Compression Through the Lens of Transform Coding
summary: This paper explores KV cache compression using transform coding to address the memory bottleneck in long-context inference for large language models, improving efficiency by optimizing storage of past token information.

title: MINT: A Universal Zero-Shot Predictor for Transaction Data
summary: MINT introduces a universal zero-shot predictor for transaction data, utilizing Payments Foundation Models to generate contextual embeddings from sequential financial transactions, aiding tasks like fraud prevention and credit risk assessment for banks.

title: Training Fair Tabular Foundation Models
summary: This research investigates the fairness properties of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs), which are increasingly used in high-stakes decision-making, exploring how to train them to ensure equitable outcomes.

title: Connected Subspace Clustering: Hardness, a Scalable Heuristic, and an Application to Sea Level Geodesy
summary: This paper introduces Connected Subspace Clustering, discussing its computational hardness, proposing a scalable heuristic, and demonstrating its application to sea level geodesy for grouping measurements with physical constraints.

title: AutoSchema: Live Schema Grounding for Agentic Text-to-Sparql over Heterogeneous Knowledge Graphs
summary: AutoSchema provides live schema grounding for agentic Text-to-Sparql systems, enabling language model agents to query heterogeneous life science knowledge graphs effectively by utilizing curated Metadata Interoperability Exchange files.

title: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Model Merging
summary: This research applies Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization to the process of model merging, which combines trained AI models directly in weight space, to efficiently select merge parameters despite expensive evaluations and conflicting source capabilities.

title: Convex losses and their applications to SVM, SVR, and Shallow Neural Networks
summary: This paper proposes multiple new convex loss functions for SVM, SVR, and Shallow Neural Networks, specifically for binary classification tasks, and explores their practical applications in primal SVM formulations and neural networks.

title: Detecting Contaminated Code-Generation Prompt Batches via Influence Functions
summary: This research proposes using Influence Functions to detect contaminated code-generation prompt batches that elicit insecure implementations from Large Language Models, aiming to enhance LLM security against novel attacks.

title: Non-Parametric Spatiotemporal Trajectory Prediction via State-Conditioned Transition Sampling
summary: This paper presents a training-free, non-parametric method for multi-modal trajectory prediction that leverages state-conditioned transition sampling from a historical transition table, achieving accuracy comparable to larger transformer models without GPU or learned parameters.

title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty of Delay Detection in Business Processes
summary: This research investigates the challenges of early delay detection in business processes, focusing on understanding the "long tail" of cases and using Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) with historical event logs to predict remaining case times.

title: Catching the Imposter: Self-Supervised Learning of Physical Coherence with Cross-Entity Feature Permutations
summary: This paper introduces "imposter," a novel discriminative pretext task for Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) that leverages cross-entity feature permutations to learn physical coherence in scientific data by identifying "imposter" feature subsets.

title: Boosting Data Augmentation with Stochastic Weight Averaging
summary: This research explores boosting data augmentation, a method for incorporating symmetries into neural networks, by combining it with Stochastic Weight Averaging to improve modern deep learning solutions.

title: Does a Language Server Save Tokens for Coding Agents? A Measurement Methodology and Preliminary Study
summary: This study investigates whether using a Language Server Protocol (LSP) for semantic retrieval saves tokens for coding agents compared to lexical retrieval, providing a measurement methodology and preliminary findings on agent context management.

title: Think in Latent, Explain in Language: Self-Explainable Latent Reasoning
summary: This paper explores latent reasoning as an alternative to Chain-of-Thought, aiming to improve computational efficiency by compressing reasoning into embeddings, while also addressing the challenge of explainability in this opaque latent space.

title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Inflation-Aware Routing for Agentic LLM Systems
summary: This research analyzes 'token inflation' in agentic LLM systems, where repeated retries consume extra tokens, leading to a gap between per-token pricing and actual workflow costs.

title: BCMT: Blockwise Causal Memory Transformer
summary: Introducing BCMT (Blockwise Causal Memory Transformer), a new architecture for long-context language modeling that addresses the quadratic complexity of self-attention by decoupling local and global attention.

title: Jais 2: A Family of Arabic-Centric Open Large Language Models
summary: Jais 2 is a new family of open large language models developed to advance Arabic-centric language modeling, showing strong performance across Arabic and culturally relevant benchmarks.

title: IterCOMP: Reasoning-aware Adaptive Prompt Compression for Multi-hop Question Answering
summary: IterCOMP is a new method for reasoning-aware adaptive prompt compression designed for multi-hop question answering, aiming to improve efficiency and accuracy in retrieval-augmented generation systems by managing lengthy and noisy contexts.

title: Measuring Fairness in Large Audio Language Models via Semantic-Aware Bias Estimation
summary: This study focuses on measuring fairness in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) for tasks like speech recognition and audio question answering, proposing a semantic-aware bias estimation method to address fairness across demographic subgroups.

title: GRPO Beyond English: A Large-Scale Study of GRPO in Non-English and Multilingual Settings
summary: This large-scale empirical study investigates Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a technique used in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), to improve the reasoning capabilities of pretrained language models in non-English and multilingual settings.

title: CLAIR-Fin: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Claim-Level Verification and Adaptive Debate in Cross-Modal Financial QA
summary: CLAIR-Fin is an adversarial multi-agent framework designed for claim-level verification and adaptive debate in cross-modal financial question answering, aiming to defend against hallucination in retrieval-augmented pipelines.

title: TeachMateGPT: A Multi-Agent Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Pedagogical Assessment Generation from Science Curriculum Materials
summary: TeachMateGPT is a multi-agent, knowledge-grounded framework for automatically generating pedagogical assessment items from science curriculum materials, addressing limitations of existing retrieval-augmented generation systems.

title: StreamHear: Domain-Adapted Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Streaming Speech Recognition
summary: StreamHear is a semi-supervised pipeline that improves streaming automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance on domain-shifted audio by fine-tuning a pretrained student model through domain-adapted pseudo-labeling.

title: BM25-Augmented Many-Shot Translation for Low-Resource North-Eastern Indian Languages
summary: This paper describes a retrieval-augmented many-shot translation pipeline, using BM25, to translate between English and eleven low-resource North-Eastern Indian languages for a shared task.

title: GALA: Generation-Aware Cross-Modal Alignment for Text-to-Time-Series Synthesis
summary: GALA (Generation-Aware Cross-Modal Alignment) is a new method for text-to-time-series synthesis, aiming to create more expressive and controllable time series generation from natural language descriptions.

title: Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive: Reasoning Behaviors in Thinking Models
summary: This research investigates the relationship between observed reasoning behaviors in AI models and their actual predictive power, exploring whether reasoning-oriented training genuinely amplifies behaviors tied to correct answers or merely makes traces appear more deliberative.

title: When Lexical Change Misleads: Rethinking Dynamic Topic Model Evaluation with Traditional and LLM-Based Metrics
summary: This study re-evaluates dynamic topic models, demonstrating how traditional coherence metrics can be misleading when vocabulary changes, and proposes rethinking evaluation with both traditional and LLM-based metrics.

title: ASSERT: A Measurement Pipeline for GenAI Audits
summary: ASSERT is presented as a measurement pipeline for auditing generative AI (GenAI) systems, designed to quantify compliance with policies, compare system behaviors, track regressions, and inform deployment decisions.

title: Bootstrapping Niche Multilingual Code Translation via Reinforcement Learning with Execution-Based Verifiable Supervision
summary: This paper details a method for bootstrapping niche multilingual code translation using reinforcement learning with execution-based verifiable supervision, aimed at preserving executable behavior across various programming languages.

title: Scaling Creative Writing Beyond Story-Centric Data with Attribute-Guided Genre Expansion
summary: This work introduces an attribute-guided genre expansion framework to scale creative writing capabilities of large language models (LLMs) beyond story-centric data, enabling them to adhere to diverse creative formats.

title: Batch-wise Adaptive Pruning: Periodic Neuron Activation-Aware Weight Pruning for Language Reasoning Model
summary: This paper proposes Batch-wise Adaptive Pruning, a periodic neuron activation-aware weight pruning method designed to reduce computational costs and improve throughput for Large Reasoning Models during batched inference.

title: S2Dialog: Multimodal Dialogue Retrieval with Semantic and Acoustic-Style Modeling
summary: S2Dialog is a new method for multimodal dialogue retrieval that combines semantic and acoustic-style modeling to find similar dialogues, crucial for tasks like emotion recognition.

title: HERMES: a multi-agent framework for structured knowledge extraction from ultra-long documents in geoscience
summary: HERMES is a scalable multi-agent framework designed for structured knowledge extraction from ultra-long, complex documents in geoscience, addressing the challenge of accessing information from legacy literature.

title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge
summary: This challenge evaluates speaker diarization, recognition, and conversational speech understanding tasks over multilingual conversations, serving as a benchmark for speech language models.

title: How Much Do Legal RAG Systems Still Hallucinate?
summary: This paper conducts a fine-grained analysis of hallucination behavior in eight legal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems to understand the extent of this challenge in the legal domain.

title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning
summary: Researchers propose AdaPop, an adaptive popularity method for LLM unlearning that adjusts gradient pressure based on training-data frequency, addressing the challenge of removing deeply memorized popular facts.

title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SimpleOPD, a tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation method designed to transfer long-context reasoning capabilities from stronger teacher models to shorter-context student models.

title: Envs-FORGE: Frontier-Optimized Reward-Grounded Environment Synthesis for Agent RL
summary: This work introduces Envs-FORGE, a method for synthesizing frontier-optimized, reward-grounded training environments tailored for reinforcement learning with terminal agents, improving difficulty and reward reliability.

title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations
summary: This paper investigates the intrinsic dimensionality of language model representations to determine whether complexity differences reflect properties of language itself or data construction artifacts.

title: A Survey of Large Models in Sports
summary: This survey provides an overview of the applications and advancements of large models, particularly multimodal large language models (MLLMs), within the sports industry.

title: Information Satisfaction: A Reader-Centered Axis for Summarization Evaluation
summary: This paper proposes 'Information Satisfaction' as a new reader-centered metric for summarization evaluation, aiming to measure the utility of a summary to an individual user beyond general quality.

title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model
summary: This paper presents a method for frozen language models to both answer and abstain from reasoning tasks in a single forward pass, addressing issues of under-used evidence and confabulation when input is insufficient.

title: Reading Between The Lines: Modeling and Evaluating Behavioral Realism in Legal Simulation
summary: This work introduces WitnessSim, an AI-driven deposition simulator with controllable legal personas, along with an evaluation framework to assess behavioral realism in legal training simulations.

title: Do AI chatbots find what experts would? Effects of model, user role, and sample size on study retrieval for medical questions
summary: This study evaluates whether AI chatbots retrieve medical studies similar to what experts would, analyzing the quality of retrieved studies and factors influencing their selection for clinical questions.

title: VoiceChat-TTS: A Low-Latency Continuous Speech Synthesis Model for Interactive Agents
summary: VoiceChat-TTS is presented as a new low-latency, continuous speech synthesis model designed for interactive agents, enabling real-time adaptability and user barge-in capabilities for spoken dialogue.

title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems
summary: This paper explores the concept of 'Agentic Transaction' to propose ACID-compliant principles for LLM agent systems, enhancing their reliability for autonomous tasks, tool use, and multi-step workflows.

title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement
summary: MathForm is introduced as a method for scaling mathematical autoformalization, leveraging knowledge retrieval and verification-guided refinement to translate natural language into machine-verifiable formal languages.

title: Grounding Without Corrective Control: Truth-Tracking Profiles for Large Language Models
summary: This paper discusses the implications of grounding in large language models, specifically focusing on the absence of corrective control and its effects on truth-tracking and answerability of model outputs.

title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in Vision Language Models
summary: This research investigates 'color bias' in Vision Language Models (VLMs), studying how these models interpret text rendered as images and the potential impact on industrial decision-making systems.

title: AnchorBench: A Multi-Pathway Benchmark for the Anchoring Effect in LLMs
summary: AnchorBench is introduced as a new multi-pathway benchmark specifically designed to measure and analyze the anchoring effect, a cognitive bias, in large language models.

title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation
summary: This paper proposes a 'Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark' for evaluating large language models used as judges in principle-based regulatory contexts, focusing on accuracy, transparency, consistency, and explainability.

title: Wrong but Useful: Trajectory Value Beyond Answer Correctness in Multi-Agent Messages
summary: This paper explores the concept of 'trajectory value' in multi-agent reasoning systems, arguing that even incorrect messages can contain useful information beyond mere answer correctness for task completion.

title: LLMs Don't Pay for the Jump
summary: The article discusses the theoretical limitations of Large Language Models, arguing they cannot perform abductive reasoning like Einstein's 'Jump' due to lacking embodied simulation. It posits that LLMs are limited to induction and deduction, sparking a debate on their inherent capabilities.

title: Multiphase-Diff: Diffusion-Based Generative Modeling for High-Contrast Multiphase Physical Systems with Sharp Interfaces
summary: 'Multiphase-Diff' is introduced as a new diffusion-based generative modeling technique designed to handle high-contrast multiphase physical systems with sharp interfaces. It addresses challenges related to singular gradient terms and extreme contrast in physical simulations.

title: PROVE: Training-Free Prompt Recovery using Verifiable Evidence
summary: 'PROVE' is presented as a training-free method for recovering natural-language prompts from images generated by text-to-image models. This development raises concerns for copyright protection and content ownership of AI-generated content.

title: MedPlex: Deep Vision-Language Co-Adaptation for Clinically Grounded Medical Segmentation
summary: 'MedPlex' is proposed as a method for deep vision-language co-adaptation aimed at clinically grounded medical image segmentation. It addresses the limitations of vision-only approaches by integrating textual knowledge into the segmentation process.

title: Limitations of Synthetic Data Generation in Specialized Data-Scarce Domains
summary: The article investigates the limitations of using synthetic image generation, particularly from diffusion-based models, to alleviate data scarcity in specialized vision tasks. It highlights that while promising in general benchmarks, its effectiveness in sparse, high-variance real-world domains is unconfirmed.

title: CAST: Closed-form Analytic Semantic Transfer for Zero-Shot Classifier Extension
summary: 'CAST' (Closed-form Analytic Semantic Transfer) is introduced as a method for Zero-Shot Classifier Extension, enabling large pre-trained models to adapt to novel categories without requiring examples from the target distribution. It addresses the challenge of data unavailability in many domains for model adaptation.

title: ChartProbe: A Diagnostic Study on Visual Reasoning through Perception, Grounding, and Simple Reasoning
summary: 'ChartProbe' is a diagnostic study investigating the unreliability of vision-language models (VLMs) when answering chart questions requiring visual quantity reasoning. It aims to determine if the difficulty stems from reasoning deficits or simpler foundational skills.

title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatially Independent Multispectral Land Classification
summary: The article explores the application of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for spatially independent multispectral land classification using satellite imagery. This method aims to improve land management, environmental monitoring, and urban planning.

title: Doomed to Re-Annotate, Forever: The ImageNet Story
summary: The paper highlights persistent quality issues with the ImageNet-1k dataset and its noisy labels, despite its widespread use as a benchmark for visual recognition. It details a comprehensive effort to address these long-standing data annotation problems.

title: XSA-MAD: Cross-modal Semantic Alignment for Morphing Attack Detection
summary: 'XSA-MAD' is proposed as a CLIP-based multimodal framework that uses cross-modal semantic alignment to improve morphing attack detection in face recognition systems. It aims to overcome the generalization issues of existing image-based methods that rely only on visual cues.

title: Attention Capture Is Not Detection: A Two-Stage Account of How Humans Miss Localized AI Image Edits
summary: This study investigates how humans detect localized AI image edits, arguing that current approaches to curb disinformation treat detectability incorrectly. Through an eye-tracking study, it reveals a two-stage process in how humans miss such edits.

title: Consensus-gated Multi-Agent Neural Architecture Search for Seismic Fault Segmentation
summary: A 'Consensus-gated Multi-Agent Neural Architecture Search' method is proposed for optimizing neural network architectures for seismic fault segmentation. This approach addresses the challenge of training under tight labeled data budgets common in geophysical applications.

title: OpenBelief-Nav: Evidence-Preserving Object Memory for Open-Vocabulary Language-Guided Navigation
summary: 'OpenBelief-Nav' introduces an evidence-preserving object memory system designed for open-vocabulary language-guided navigation in 3D scene graphs. It aims to prevent the loss of task-relevant hypotheses by avoiding premature commitment to single object features or labels.

title: RGBX-Next: Towards Realistic Generative Rendering from G-Buffers
summary: 'RGBX-Next' explores using generative models, specifically diffusion models, as learned renderers to achieve more realistic and controllable generative rendering from G-Buffers. This approach aims to enhance the precision of generated output compared to traditional 3D rendering.

title: CMCNet: Aligning Ultrasound Image Embeddings with Textual TI-RADS Representations for Fine-Grained Thyroid Classification
summary: 'CMCNet' is presented as a deep learning approach that aligns ultrasound image embeddings with textual TI-RADS representations for fine-grained thyroid nodule classification. It aims to improve diagnosis by integrating standardized clinical frameworks into AI models.

title: Fast Implicit Neural Light Field Representation via Geometric Decomposition and Multi-Resolution Low-Rank Features
summary: The paper introduces a method for fast implicit neural light field representation using geometric decomposition and multi-resolution low-rank features. This approach aims to address the challenges of efficiently reconstructing high-dimensional light fields.

title: PPOM: Marginalizing Patch-Grid Phase for CLIP-Based Generalizable Vision-Language Prompt Tuning
summary: 'PPOM' proposes a method for marginalizing patch-grid phase in CLIP-based prompt tuning to improve generalizability in vision-language models. It addresses the sensitivity of predictions to spatial sampling and patch tokenization.

title: Rethinking Auxiliary Modalities in Multimodal Zero-shot Anomaly Detection: From Semantic Fusion to Conditional Modulation
summary: This paper rethinks the role of auxiliary modalities in multimodal zero-shot anomaly detection, advocating for a shift from semantic fusion to conditional modulation. It addresses the limitations of RGB-only observations in detecting certain types of anomalies.

title: ProFocus: Interpreting Affective Experience in Artistic Images with Progressive Visual Focusing
summary: 'ProFocus' is introduced as a method for interpreting the affective experience evoked by artistic images using progressive visual focusing. This approach aims to better understand the emotional responses triggered by visual art.

title: FIRM: Fine-Grained Intra-Token Representation of Masks for Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation
summary: 'FIRM' proposes a method for fine-grained intra-token representation of masks specifically for remote sensing reasoning segmentation using multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It aims to improve precise pixel-level masking for small targets and thin structures.

title: MedClaw: Heuristic Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Surgical Video Reasoning
summary: MedClaw introduces a heuristic agent harness designed for long-horizon surgical video reasoning, enabling understanding of complex procedures by grounding questions in visual evidence across time.

title: Content Based Video Narration of Gameplay with Vision Language Models
summary: This item presents a content-based video narration system that uses vision-language models (VLM) and text-to-speech to generate spoken, esports-style commentary for arbitrary gameplay recordings.

title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models
summary: ForgeWM describes a progressive causal training method for action-conditioned video world models, aiming for low-latency causal generation and reliable responses to interactive controls in video synthesis.

title: SSP: An Event-Matched Syn2Sim2Phy Cross-Domain Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Driving VLA Models
summary: SSP proposes an event-matched cross-domain evaluation framework (Syn2Sim2Phy) for autonomous driving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, addressing performance gaps caused by varied data sources.

title: E-S2Feat:Semantic-Guided Spiking Local Feature Detection and Description for Event Cameras
summary: E-S2Feat introduces a semantic-guided spiking local feature detection and description method for event cameras, aiming for robust feature learning despite sparsity and noise for resource-constrained platforms.

title: Beyond Text Conditioning: A Systematic Study of MLLM-DiT Fusion for Video Generation
summary: This study explores MLLM-DiT fusion architectures to enhance video generation, particularly for high-level semantic planning, building on advancements in Diffusion Transformers and multimodal models.

title: Source-Agnostic Image Translation Based on Latent Aware Adaptive Masking
summary: This work proposes a source-agnostic image translation framework that dynamically refines a binary mask during the reverse diffusion process using latent-aware adaptive masking, improving pretrained diffusion models.

title: Discovery and Spatial Characterisation of Multiple Shortcut Groups for Auditing Vision Model Bias
summary: This research focuses on discovering and spatially characterizing shortcut groups to audit bias in vision models, addressing how models trained on spurious correlations may fail to generalize.

title: Voxel-based 3D Facies Segmentation from Seismic Data: A Comparative Study
summary: This item presents a comparative study on voxel-based 3D facies segmentation from seismic data, a significant challenge in geophysics that requires robust methods for identifying geological formations.

title: InstructVVT: Instruction-Driven Video Virtual Try-On without Auxiliary Spatial Priors
summary: InstructVVT introduces an instruction-driven video virtual try-on method that precisely replaces clothing in videos while preserving spatial and temporal dynamics, without relying on auxiliary spatial priors.

title: CoDS: Robust Collaborative Perception via Expert-driven Detection and BEV Segmentation
summary: CoDS proposes a system for robust collaborative perception that uses expert-driven detection and BEV segmentation, addressing challenges like multi-source noise and communication delays in multi-agent information exchange.

title: SPARGen: Unifying Spatial Perception and Reasoning through Native Multimodal Generation
summary: SPARGen introduces a framework that unifies spatial perception and reasoning through native multimodal generation, allowing AI to recover geometric structure and understand spatial relations from visual observations.

title: PISA: A Pseudo-Individual Source-Domain Feature Adaptation Framework for Test-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
summary: PISA is a pseudo-individual source-domain feature adaptation framework for test-time open-vocabulary object detection, designed to mitigate performance degradation in pre-trained models due to image-domain shifts.

title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
summary: This item investigates self-supervised visual on-policy distillation, exploring how informative teacher-student asymmetry can be generated for improved model training without privileged supervision.

title: SCVIB: Editable State-Conditioned Visual Instance Binding forMulti-Turn Personalized Localization
summary: SCVIB introduces editable state-conditioned visual instance binding, a multi-turn localization setting where AI systems bind and localize objects based on support-defined instances and protocol-defined state events.

title: Concept Guidance: Precise, Training-Free Latent Control for Text-to-Image Generation
summary: Concept Guidance introduces a precise, training-free latent control method for text-to-image generation, addressing the limitations of diffusion models in continuous, concept-specific guidance and reliability.

title: LightTeaNet: A Weakly Supervised Lightweight CNN for Multi-Label Tea Leaf Disease Detection and Localization
summary: LightTeaNet proposes a weakly supervised lightweight CNN for multi-label tea leaf disease detection and localization, offering an efficient method to combat crop diseases affecting tea production.

title: RankT2I: A Submodular Framework for Discovering Interpretable and Diverse Semantics in Text-to-Image Models
summary: RankT2I presents a submodular framework for discovering interpretable and diverse semantics in text-to-image models, aiming to help users understand and control the image generation and editing capabilities of these models.

title: Zero-Shot Skeleton-Based Action Anticipation
summary: This item describes research into zero-shot skeleton-based action anticipation, a method that enables AI systems and robots to predict human or humanoid actions from partial observations without prior examples.

title: On the Robustness of Temporal Vision-Language Models for Surgical Endoscopy Videos
summary: This research investigates the robustness of temporal vision-language models (TVLMs) for surgical endoscopy videos, analyzing their performance under clinically realistic acquisition artifacts such as haze and motion blur.

title: Learning to Forecast Crop Growth from Earth Observation Data
summary: This research investigates using Earth observation data and meteorological drivers to forecast crop growth and future canopy development for agricultural management.

title: MAGneT-3D: Monocular and Domain-Generalizable Temporal 3D Detection
summary: This research introduces MAGneT-3D, a method for monocular temporal 3D object detection that aims to be more domain-generalizable by addressing issues in query-based detectors.

title: Spatial Message Passing in Language Space for Pathology Image Interpretation
summary: This research proposes a spatial message passing method in language space to improve multimodal large language models' interpretation of gigapixel pathology images, addressing visual context limits.

title: Intelligent Detection of Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Metrics Based on 2D Floor Plans
summary: This research developed a neural network-based model for intelligent detection and extraction of Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) metrics from 2D floor plans to aid in efficient design.

title: TRIAGE: Risk-Controlled Pseudo-Label Admission for Annotation-Efficient Semi-Supervised Retinal OCT Classification
summary: This research introduces TRIAGE, a method using risk-controlled pseudo-label admission for annotation-efficient semi-supervised classification of retinal Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images.

title: Weakly Supervised Polar Low Segmentation in Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery
summary: This research explores weakly supervised deep learning methods for polar low segmentation in Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, addressing the challenge of limited pixel-level training masks.

title: GBU-Palm: A Multimodal Video Dataset and Benchmark for Palm Presentation Attack Detection
summary: This paper introduces GBU-Palm, a new large-scale multimodal video dataset and benchmark specifically designed for systematically evaluating Palm Presentation Attack Detection systems.

title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination
summary: This research conducts a systematic evaluation of detectors and generators to assess defense mechanisms against AI-generated video attacks that fabricate real-world crisis events, exploring misinformation risks.

title: IRGNN: Efficient Invariant Radar Graph Neural Network for Radar Point Cloud Object Detection
summary: This paper introduces IRGNN, an efficient invariant Radar Graph Neural Network, for robust radar point cloud object detection, aiming to improve perception in autonomous driving under adverse weather.

title: Adjacency-Based Spectral Proxy Control of Mobile Communication Agents
summary: This research proposes an adjacency-based spectral proxy control method for repositioning controllable communication agents within a heterogeneous mobile-agent network in real-time.

title: hint$^2$: Hierarchical World Models for Inference-Time Temporal Logic Guidance
summary: This research introduces hint$^2$, a framework using hierarchical world models and Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) to enable robots to execute complex, runtime-specified instructions with temporal structure and safety constraints.

title: Graph-MambaNav: Spatial-Temporal Graph Mamba Leveraging Object-Relation Knowledge for Object-Goal Navigation
summary: This paper introduces Graph-MambaNav, a method leveraging spatial-temporal graph Mamba and object-relation knowledge to enable agents to perform efficient object-goal navigation in unseen environments.

title: Knowledge-Data-Dual-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Control in Mixed Traffic
summary: This research proposes a knowledge-data-dual-driven reinforcement learning approach to enhance decision-making and control for autonomous vehicles operating in complex mixed-traffic environments.

title: Ontology-Grounded World Models for Failure Diagnosis and Closed-Loop Repair in Physical AI Systems
summary: This paper presents Onto-EV-WM, an ontology-grounded world model framework for failure diagnosis and closed-loop repair mechanisms in physical AI systems.

title: Communication in modular robotic motor control: Bilateral controllers under realistic constraints
summary: This research investigates communication in modular robotic motor control, focusing on bilateral controllers to achieve accurate movement and robust postural stabilization in musculoskeletal systems under realistic constraints.

title: BICPO-VLA: Behavior-Identified Continuation Preference Optimization for Smooth Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control
summary: This paper introduces BICPO-VLA, a method for behavior-identified continuation preference optimization to achieve smooth asynchronous Vision-Language-Action control in robotic systems.

title: AdvDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Joint-Aligned Actions and Adversarial Learning
summary: This research presents AdvDex, a method for learning dexterous manipulation from human demonstrations via joint-aligned actions and adversarial learning to scale embodied intelligence in robots.

title: Evolve Vision-Language-Action Model into an Agent with On-the-fly Tool-use
summary: This paper proposes ART (Agentic Robot with Tool-use), a tool-injection framework that integrates end-to-end Visual-Language-Action models with on-the-fly agentic tool-use to enhance robotic capabilities.

title: FlatLab: A Unified Methodology Framework and Simulation-Based Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation of Flat Objects
summary: This paper introduces FlatLab, a unified methodology framework and simulation-based benchmark designed to address the challenges of robotic manipulation of flat objects.

title: AgilePE: Autonomous UAV Pursuit-Evasion via Self-Play Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research presents AgilePE, a self-play reinforcement learning approach for achieving autonomous pursuit-evasion capabilities in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).

title: OccPlanner: Goal-Aware Occupancy-Conditioned Diffusion Planner for Pixel-Goal Navigation
summary: OccPlanner is a goal-aware occupancy-conditioned diffusion planner designed for pixel-goal navigation, enabling 3D goal grounding and collision-free continuous planning for agents.

title: MMUSV-Sim: A Perception-Oriented Simulation and Data-Generation Platform for Multi-USV Cooperative Perception
summary: MMUSV-Sim is a perception-oriented simulation and data-generation platform for developing multi-unmanned surface vehicle (USV) cooperative perception systems at scale.

title: Accelerating Large-scale Bundle Adjustment for LiDAR Mapping via Parallel Computing
summary: This paper proposes the first fully parallel computing framework to accelerate LiDAR bundle adjustment, improving large-scale point cloud map construction with adaptive local scheduling, sub-state sharing, and point-to-plane optimization.

title: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5: A Toolkit for Robot Process Assessment
summary: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5 is a toolkit for fine-grained robot process assessment, converting rollout videos into dense progress curves and deriving multiple detailed metrics to evaluate embodied models beyond binary success rates.

title: CORAL: Curriculum-Optimized Reward Adaptation for LiDAR-Based Goal-Directed Urban Driving
summary: CORAL presents a curriculum-optimized reward adaptation strategy for reinforcement learning in LiDAR-based, goal-directed urban driving, addressing the challenge of acquiring multiple competing behaviors for autonomous vehicles.

title: Reflex: Enabling Fast and Predictive Vision-Language-Action Models for Reaction-Critical Manipulation
summary: ReflexBench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for reaction-critical robotic manipulation, addressing the gap in assessment for dynamic interaction scenarios.

title: Control-Informed Constraint Adaptation in Minimum-Time Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Racing
summary: This paper proposes control-informed constraint adaptation in minimum-time trajectory planning for autonomous racecars, ensuring safety and performance by accounting for execution errors at the limits of vehicle dynamics.

title: THRIVE: Therapeutic Humanoid Robot In Virtual Environment
summary: THRIVE (Therapeutic Humanoid Robot In Virtual Environment) is an at-home rehabilitation platform integrating VR games, real-time motion-tracking, and a socially interactive robot therapist for upper-body rehabilitation.

title: Expected Free Energy-based Informative Path Planning for Robotic Mars Exploration
summary: This paper presents an Expected Free Energy-based informative path planning method for autonomous robots exploring unknown environments, exemplified by robotic Mars exploration for efficient information gathering.

title: Ensuring Safe Physical AI in Urban Mobility via Hazard-Informed Synthesized Envelopes
summary: A unified framework is presented to ensure safe physical AI in urban mobility for heterogeneous robotic systems by bridging hazard analysis with runtime enforcement using hazard-informed synthesized envelopes.

title: Edge Case Detection in Automated Driving: Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: This paper surveys methods, challenges, and future directions for edge case detection in automated driving, crucial for enhancing the reliability and safety of automated vehicles in real-world conditions.

title: LLM-Advisor: An LLM Advisor for Cost-efficient Path Planning across Multiple Terrains
summary: LLM-Advisor is proposed as an external verification system that leverages a Large Language Model to provide cost-efficient path refinement across multiple terrains, addressing limitations of predefined route spaces.

title: Estimating Dynamic Soft Continuum Robot States From Boundaries
summary: This research addresses the challenging problem of state estimation for soft continuum robots, focusing on inferring their infinite-dimensional states from boundary observations.

title: MorphIt: Flexible Spherical Approximation of Robot Morphology for Representation-driven Adaptation
summary: MorphIt introduces a method for flexible spherical approximation of robot morphology, enabling representation-driven adaptation to meet the diverse demands of various robotic tasks.

title: Effective Game-Theoretic Motion Planning via Nested Search
summary: This paper presents effective game-theoretic motion planning via nested search, enabling individual robots to reason about interactions with other agents for safe and effective real-world deployment.

title: Genie Sim 3.0 : A High-Fidelity Comprehensive Simulation Platform for Humanoid Robot
summary: Genie Sim 3.0 is a high-fidelity comprehensive simulation platform designed for humanoid robots, facilitating the development of robust robot learning models and providing diverse training data.

title: AtomBridge: Agentic VLA Inference Plugin for Long-Horizon Tasks in Scientific Experiments
summary: AtomBridge is an agentic Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference plugin designed to enable robotic laboratories to execute long-horizon tasks for autonomous scientific discovery.

title: LatentAM: Real-Time, Large-Scale Latent Gaussian Attention Mapping via Online Dictionary Learning
summary: LatentAM is introduced as a real-time, large-scale latent Gaussian attention mapping framework that builds scalable latent feature maps from RGB-D observations for open-vocabulary robotic perception.

title: CoViLLM: An Adaptive Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly Framework Using Large Language Models
summary: CoViLLM presents an Adaptive Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly Framework that utilizes Large Language Models to improve the flexibility and adaptability of manufacturing robots for customized products.

title: Versatile Exoskeleton Control Supports Elderly Joint Energetics During Hip-Intensive Tasks
summary: Research explores versatile exoskeleton control to support elderly joint energetics during hip-intensive tasks, addressing age-related mobility decline.

title: Learning-Guided Sparsification of Dynamic Graphs in Robotic Exploration
summary: A hybrid transformer-based framework using Proximal Policy Optimization is presented for learning-guided sparsification of dynamic graphs in robotic exploration, improving performance by reducing redundant information.

title: From Reach to Insert: Tactile-Augmented Precision Assembly under Sub-Millimeter Tolerances
summary: This paper proposes a tactile-augmented two-stage method combining Imitation Learning to achieve high-precision assembly under sub-millimeter tolerances, addressing challenges of jamming and excessive interaction forces.

title: Sampling-Based Coordination-Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Robot Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work introduces a sampling-based multi-objective multi-robot reinforcement learning approach to optimize competing objectives and maintain coordinated behavior in distributed robot systems.

title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation Using Contact Wrench Guidance From Human Demonstration
summary: CHORD, a framework for long-horizon manipulation, enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation by using contact wrench guidance derived from human demonstrations, addressing challenges in transferring human skills.

title: A Change of Frame Makes Balance Observable: Distillation-Free Humanoid Single-Leg Stance
summary: Research presents a method for achieving distillation-free humanoid single-leg stance, demonstrating improved balance performance compared to existing state-of-the-art general policies on a new benchmark.

title: WAM-Diff2: Hierarchical AR-to-Diffusion Distillation for Highly Efficient Autonomous Driving VLA
summary: WAM-Diff2 introduces hierarchical AR-to-diffusion distillation for highly efficient Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in autonomous driving, addressing computational latency and exposure bias.

title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots
summary: PFM-HR introduces a reusable Pose Flow Matching prior to improve reinforcement learning for physics-based humanoid tracking, addressing limitations of existing motion and pose priors.

title: HierDAMap: Towards Universal Domain Adaptive BEV Mapping via Hierarchical Perspective Priors
summary: HierDAMap presents a method for universal domain adaptive Bird's-Eye View (BEV) mapping through hierarchical perspective priors, aiming for robust visual perception in autonomous driving across various real-world conditions.

title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud
summary: PhyAI presents a framework for real-time physical AI, focusing on scalable rollouts in the cloud and efficient inference at the edge via GPU serving and onboard deployment.

title: AI opäť posunula hranice možného. Podarilo sa jej navrhnúť vírusy, ktoré fungujú aj mimo počítača
summary: AI has successfully designed functional viruses intended to combat bacteria, pushing boundaries for new treatment methods but also raising new questions.

summary: AI video start-up Higgsfield has been valued at $5.4 billion after receiving backing from Goldman Sachs and Intel.

summary: Anthropic is facing backlash from Claude subscribers regarding its new AI watermark feature.

summary: DeepSeek, a major AI player, has launched "Harness v0.1", a new product aimed at boosting the AI sector and the domestic chip industry.

summary: The head of the Czech cryptocurrency wallet company Trezor stated they experienced their second-best year but still had layoffs, clarifying they do not attribute this to AI.

summary: Alibaba's Qwen AI model has achieved 3 billion downloads, surpassing Meta and Google in the open AI space.

summary: Experts suggest focusing on broader AI infrastructure investments as the market matures.

summary: Matyáš Zetek, a Czech expert from McKinsey, advises young people to understand how AI will change work and professions, noting the upcoming robotization of the Czech manufacturing economy.
