title: DeepTCM1.0: A Multi-Expert AI Agent for Deciphering Mechanisms of Chinese Herbal Formulae Based on General Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces DeepTCM1.0, a multi-expert AI agent designed to decipher the mechanisms of Chinese herbal formulae by integrating general large language models with traditional Chinese medicine theory.

title: StocksTalk: A Voice-Enabled Conversational Agent for Structured Query Generation over Web Data
summary: StocksTalk is a voice-enabled conversational agent that transforms spoken financial screening requests into executable and validated structured queries over real-world market data.

title: Different Facets of Verbalised Overconfidence: an Interpretability Study
summary: This interpretability study examines overconfidence in large language models, analyzing how models like Qwen3-4B express uncertainty across different logical reasoning scenarios.

title: Institutional Prestige as Geographic Bias in Large Language Models: Evidence from Three Factorial Experiments with Bootstrap Confidence Intervals
summary: This research investigates whether large language models exhibit geographic bias and systematically discriminate in candidate evaluations based on applicant ethnicity, institutional prestige, and location.

title: Same Facts, Different Updates: Inference Setup Shapes LLM Behavior in Medical Allocation
summary: This research explores how inference setup can shape large language model behavior in sensitive decision-making processes, such as medical allocation, leading to unexpected outcomes.

title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings
summary: This paper presents Brain2Qwerty v2, a model that enables accurate decoding of natural sentences from non-invasive brain recordings, aiming to restore communication for individuals with speech loss.

title: Temporal Multi-Signal Fusion for Token-Level Hallucination Detection
summary: This paper proposes a new method for token-level hallucination detection in generative models, treating hallucination as a temporally extended span using multi-signal fusion and sequence labeling.

title: You Are What You Prompt: Prompt Quality, Domain Shift, and Uncertainty in Agrifood Vision-Language Models
summary: This study analyzes the impact of prompt quality, domain shift, and uncertainty on the performance of agrifood vision-language models, and explores the behavior of Zero-shot Prompt Ensembling.

title: Alignment Is All You Need: Instruction-Free Training for General Audio-Language Models
summary: This paper proposes an instruction-free training approach for building general audio-language models, simplifying the typical multi-stage pipeline for multimodal large language models.

title: Language Models for Portuguese: A Systematic Mapping Study
summary: This systematic mapping study reviews the development and current landscape of language models specifically designed for the Portuguese language.

title: The Deontic Gap: Large Language Models and the Modal Language of Obligation
summary: This research examines whether large language models accurately reproduce human patterns of deontic modal usage, focusing on how they handle language of obligation like 'must' and 'should'.

title: When Do LLMs Actually Help? Evaluating LLMs as Data Quality Annotators
summary: This study evaluates the effectiveness and consistency of large language models when used as automated data quality annotators for tasks such as entity matching and brand mislabeling in e-commerce.

title: Are LLMs Safe Beyond Text: Do Emojis Expose Gaps in Safety Evaluation
summary: This work investigates whether emoji-augmented prompts expose gaps in the safety evaluations of large language models, which predominantly rely on text-based adversarial inputs.

title: Efficient INT8 Inference of Small NLP Models on Server CPUs with PyTorch Native Stack
summary: This paper discusses efficient INT8 inference for small NLP models, like BERT-family encoders, on server CPUs using the PyTorch native stack to optimize latency, throughput, and cost.

title: Figurative and Cultural Knowledge in LLMs: Investigating Cross-Domain Transfer through Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper investigates how large language models (LLMs) acquire and transfer figurative and cultural knowledge through fine-tuning, studying its impact on understanding and cultural immersion.

title: Tangut Word Segmentation under Extreme Resource Scarcity: Integrating Traditional Lexicons and Unlabeled Text
summary: This study presents a systematic approach to Tangut word segmentation, an extinct low-resource language, by integrating traditional lexicons with unlabeled text to address the lack of explicit word boundaries.

title: Pedagogical AI in Mental Health: A Tri-Stream Fine-Tuned LLM Framework for Automated Clinical Supervision and Risk Triage
summary: Researchers propose a tri-stream fine-tuned LLM framework, based on Mistral-7B-instruct, for automated clinical supervision and risk triage in mental health to address the critical shortage of senior oversight.

title: OmniAlign: A Unified Multilingual Aligner for Word and Sentence Alignment
summary: OmniAlign is introduced as a unified multilingual aligner capable of performing both word and sentence alignment, addressing the limitations of existing tools that typically specialize in a single granularity.

title: WhiteMatter: All-to-All Cross-Layer Connections via KV Mixing
summary: WhiteMatter proposes a new Transformer architectural component called KV Mixing, enabling all-to-all cross-layer connections where shallow layers can attend to deeper past-token representations during autoregressive decoding.

title: MissDiag: Diagnostic Evaluation of Incomplete-Knowledge Robustness in KGQA and KG-RAG
summary: MissDiag is a diagnostic evaluation method introduced to assess the robustness of Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) and KG-RAG systems against incomplete knowledge graphs, which are common in real-world scenarios.

title: DART-SD: Diamond-topology Aware Retrieval and Tuning for Self-Distillation of Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents
summary: DART-SD is a new method focused on improving multi-turn tool-calling capabilities for autonomous agents by using 'diamond-topology aware retrieval and tuning' for self-distillation, moving beyond full-length trajectory imitation.

title: Shared Circuits for Shared Grammar: Tracing Subject-Verb Agreement Across Languages
summary: This research investigates whether multilingual large language models share internal mechanisms for grammatical operations, specifically tracing subject-verb agreement across different languages to understand cross-lingual generalization.

title: Beyond LLM-Based Reasoning: Lightweight GNNs for Agent Failure Attribution
summary: This paper proposes using lightweight Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for 'Agent Failure Attribution' to diagnose complex failure modes in LLM-based multi-agent systems, identifying faulty agents and their actions.

title: Compress and Forget: bitsandbytes Quantization Amplifies Proactive Interference in LLMs
summary: Research shows that post-training quantization (PTQ) in LLMs amplifies 'proactive interference,' a documented failure mode where retrieval of repeatedly overwritten values degrades, mirroring human working memory issues.

title: From Storage to Access: Verifiable Activation of Parametric Knowledge in LLMs via Explicit Priming and Implicit Reasoning
summary: This paper explores methods, including explicit priming and implicit reasoning, to reliably recall and verify factual knowledge encoded within large language models' parameters, aiming to address bottlenecks in factual question answering.

title: TranslatePsy-AfriSLM: High-Quality Data Scaling For Low-Resource Machine Translation
summary: TranslatePsy-AfriSLM addresses the digital divide by focusing on high-quality data scaling for low-resource machine translation in African languages, aiming to improve the performance of open-source LLMs.

title: X2Streaming-TTS: Causal Token-Level Text-to-Speech from Streaming Text with Speech-State Inheritance
summary: X2Streaming-TTS is a new token-level text-to-speech system designed for low-latency spoken dialogue by generating speech from streaming text with speech-state inheritance, ensuring perceptual continuity.

title: Learning What to Fail On: Failure-Mode Contextual Bandits for Adversarial Data Curation
summary: This work introduces a novel framework utilizing 'failure-mode contextual bandits' for adversarial data curation, aiming to improve robustness in natural language understanding by learning what types of failures to target.

title: Aslema at NADI 2026: Augmentation through Fewshot for SLU
summary: Aslema, a system for the NADI 2026 Shared Task 5, evaluates different LLMs in zero-shot and fine-tuned settings for intent recognition and slot filling, demonstrating that fine-tuning consistently outperforms zero-shot inference.

title: MemFuse: Multi-Source Memory Fusion from Fragmented Observations
summary: MemFuse is a novel memory system for agents that performs multi-source memory fusion from fragmented observations across applications and devices, addressing limitations of existing single-source memory systems.

title: Execution-grounded evaluation reveals hidden failures in language-model calculations for environmental science
summary: AtmosCoder-Bench is an execution-grounded benchmark introduced to evaluate large language model calculations in environmental science, making the computational process visible to reveal hidden failures beyond final answers.

title: Gradient Mirage: Trainable yet Label-Unidentifiable Gradients in Large Language Model Split Learning
summary: This research investigates gradient matching attacks (GMAs) in LLM split learning, analyzing the assumption of gradient-objective consistency and its implications for privacy when the server attempts to recover private training labels.

title: Readable, Faithful, Used: Three Dissociable Properties of Demographic Identity in a Language Model
summary: This paper examines how demographic identity is represented in language models, exploring the readability, faithfulness, and usage of inter-group differences when LLMs simulate survey respondents, addressing issues of bias and representation.

title: Decomposing Wrong-Consensus Agreement in LLM Self-Consistency: A GPT-4.1 Case Study
summary: This paper analyzes 'wrong-consensus agreement' in LLM self-consistency, explaining why majority voting sometimes fails and introducing a 'pluralistic agreement index Gamma' to quantitatively account for this phenomenon.

title: Do Large Language Models Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas?
summary: This paper analyzes AI hallucinations, which are considered an engineering flaw, and explores their philosophical significance in relation to machine consciousness. It contributes to the broader debate on AI behavior and its implications.

title: Identifying Implicit Premises for Logical Reconstruction of Argument Graphs
summary: This research focuses on natural language processing methods to identify implicit premises (enthymemes) for the logical reconstruction of argument graphs from natural language text. It addresses challenges in accurately parsing and understanding argumentative structures.

title: Understanding Multilingual Medical ASR Adaptation Through Layer-Wise Analysis
summary: This research investigates the adaptation of multilingual medical automatic speech recognition (MedASR) models by analyzing their layer-wise behavior. It aims to improve performance in specialized terminology and limited data scenarios.

title: Assessing Quality of Experience in Natural Language Generation of German Text
summary: This paper addresses the critical need for reliable evaluation of Natural Language Generation (NLG) in German text, highlighting the shortcomings of traditional automatic metrics in capturing the quality of experience. It focuses on improving assessment methods for generated content.

title: SMTrap: Cost-Effective DoS Attacks Against Large Reasoning Models via SMT Conflict Guidance
summary: This paper proposes SMTrap, a novel and cost-effective method called "search amplification" for conducting Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks against large reasoning models. It aims to reduce the expense of synthesizing attack queries.

title: Human-Centric Intelligence in the Era of Foundation Models: A Survey
summary: This survey paper examines the evolution of human-centric intelligence in the era of foundation models, discussing its integration and potential for progress. It reviews recent advancements in this interdisciplinary field.

title: LumiTokens: 3D Relighting via Token-Space Lighting Transformation
summary: This paper introduces LumiTokens, a novel method for 3D relighting that utilizes token-space lighting transformation, aiming to improve efficiency over existing recomputation-heavy approaches. It leverages latent scene representations for multi-view image encoding.

title: XRF-to-Optical Field-of-View Localization with Vision Language Models
summary: This research applies Vision Language Models (VLMs) to localize the field-of-view between X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and optical microscopy images. It aims to improve the registration of complementary measurements from different imaging modalities.

title: FedCoRe: Target-Adaptive Completion for Missing Modalities in Healthcare Federated Learning
summary: This paper introduces FedCoRe (Federated Cross-Modal Representation), a target-adaptive method for completing missing modalities in healthcare federated learning. It addresses the challenge of varying data availability across different hospital sites in multimodal models.

title: A Configurable Privacy-Preserving MRI Processing Workflow Using Deep Learning-Based Brain Extraction and Adaptive Anatomical Preservation
summary: This research presents a configurable, privacy-preserving MRI processing workflow that uses deep learning for brain extraction and adaptive anatomical preservation. It aims to address privacy concerns related to facial and cranial information in structural MRI volumes.

title: Reproducible Multimodal Affordance Prediction
summary: This paper highlights the difficulties in evaluating and comparing multimodal affordance prediction methods due to heterogeneous problem formulations and inconsistent dataset annotations. It emphasizes the need for improved reproducibility in this area.

title: From Inference to Adaptation: A Unified Optimal Transport View of Vision Language Model
summary: This paper proposes a unified optimal transport framework for Vision Language Models (VLMs), aiming to improve their adaptation to real-world distribution shifts during inference. It addresses the sensitivity of VLMs to changes in data distribution.

title: TTSD-FAR: Test-Time Self-Distillation with Fisher-Anchored Restoration for Missing-Modality Emotion Recognition in LVLMs
summary: This research introduces TTSD-FAR, a method employing test-time self-distillation with Fisher-anchored restoration for missing-modality emotion recognition in large video-language models. It aims to improve performance in real-world scenarios where multimodal data may be incomplete.

title: What Does Attention Transfer Transfer? Attention Structure and Robustness in Vision Transformers
summary: This paper investigates the impact of attention transfer on the robustness and internal attention structure of Vision Transformers (ViTs). It examines how copying pretrained teacher's attention maps affects accuracy under distribution shifts.

title: COSTA: A Cluster-Centric Paradigm for Annotation-Free Open-Set Semantic Segmentation of Aerial Point Clouds with Domain Shifts
summary: This paper proposes COSTA, a cluster-centric paradigm for annotation-free open-set semantic segmentation of aerial point clouds, designed to address generalization issues and domain shifts. It focuses on adapting pre-trained models efficiently to unlabeled target-domain data.

title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
summary: This paper introduces a method for training-free sparse attention to accelerate video transformers, particularly for video generation and world models. It addresses challenges in implementing executable sparse operators despite row-wise attention concentration.

title: DyG$^2$T: Modeling Object Dynamics with 3D Gaussian Temporal-Spatial Particle Graph Transformer
summary: This paper presents DyG$^2$T, a 3D Gaussian Temporal-Spatial Particle Graph Transformer for modeling object dynamics from limited visual observations. It aims to improve accurate motion trajectory prediction in embodied interaction scenarios.

title: OptiModNet: A UNet-Transformer Hybrid with Grouped-Query and Channel Attention for Optic Disc and Cup Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes OptiModNet, a UNet-Transformer hybrid model incorporating grouped-query and channel attention, for precise optic disc and cup segmentation. It aims to achieve high performance with low computational requirements for glaucoma detection.

title: Prior-Conditioned Gaussian Discriminants for Generalizable AI-generated Image Detection
summary: This research investigates Prior-Conditioned Gaussian Discriminants for generalizable AI-generated image detection. It aims to improve the reliability of detectors against synthetic images, particularly under shifts in generator, prompt/style, and source domains.

title: StateTrace: An Object-Centric Framework for Hidden-State Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Long Videos
summary: This paper introduces StateTrace, an object-centric framework designed to improve hidden-state spatiotemporal reasoning in long videos. It addresses the challenge of inferring object states when target objects become invisible in existing video-language models.

title: Zero-Shot SAM2 Segmentation and Vision Transformer-Based Recognition of Elamite Cuneiform Symbols from Degraded Tablet Images
summary: This paper presents an AI system using Zero-Shot SAM2 segmentation and Vision Transformers to recognize ancient Elamite cuneiform symbols from degraded tablet images. It addresses challenges like varying illumination and surface erosion in historical artifact analysis.

title: PATE-Forensics: Perception-as-Tool for Explainable Deepfake Forensics with General-Purpose MLLMs
summary: PATE-Forensics introduces a 'Perception-as-Tool' paradigm for explainable deepfake forensics, decoupling detection, localization, and explanation. It leverages agent-style tool use with general-purpose MLLMs to enhance forensic analysis.

title: MR-IQA-2: Faithful Image Quality Reflection via Fine-Grained Credit Assignment
summary: This paper introduces MR-IQA-2, a method that uses fine-grained credit assignment to improve the faithfulness of multimodal large language models in image quality assessment. It addresses how MLLMs assign reasoning to their quality ratings.

title: OmniHandwritingOCR: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal LLMs in Handwritten OCR Scenarios
summary: OmniHandwritingOCR is presented as a diagnostic benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of multimodal large language models in handwritten optical character recognition (OCR) scenarios. It highlights limitations of existing benchmarks which focus on printed text.

title: FD-CanKD: Frequency-Decoupled Cross-Attention Distillation as a Refinement Prior for Compact Object Detectors
summary: FD-CanKD proposes a frequency-decoupled cross-attention distillation method as a refinement prior for compact object detectors. This technique aims to bridge the accuracy gap between small and large models in resource-constrained visual perception.

title: Teach a Molmo2Fish: Towards interactive fish tracking with natural language guidance
summary: This research explores interactive fish tracking using natural language guidance, aiming to integrate computer vision models into ecological workflows. It addresses the challenges of multi-object tracking in large ecological datasets.

title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation
summary: VA-Judger proposes a reward modeling approach that leverages human preference feedback to post-train joint video-audio generation models. This method aims to improve the quality of generated content by integrating nuanced human evaluations.

title: SPARC: Slice-to-volume Pipeline for Automated Reconstruction of gated 3D+time fetal Cardiac MRI
summary: SPARC introduces a slice-to-volume pipeline for the automated reconstruction of gated 3D+time fetal cardiac MRI. This method provides valuable diagnostic information for assessing cardiac function in complex congenital heart disease.

title: PALATE: Personalized Aesthetic Learning through Adaptive Taste Evolution for Multi-User Portrait Retouching
summary: PALATE presents a method for personalized aesthetic learning through adaptive taste evolution for multi-user portrait retouching. It aims to generate subjective yet professionally valid results by adapting to individual user preferences.

title: PCQA-R1: Advancing Generalized 3D Point Cloud Quality Assessment with Reinforcement Learning
summary: PCQA-R1 advances generalized 3D point cloud quality assessment by employing reinforcement learning within large multimodal models. This research explores no-reference PCQA, an active topic for optimizing the visual experience of point clouds.

title: When Safety Overrides Vision: Exploring Dynamics between Vision Influence and Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research explores the dynamics between vision influence and safety alignment in vision-language models, observing how safety constraints can override accurate visual reasoning. It investigates the trade-offs in VLM behavior when balancing safety and factual responses.

title: SAM2Dual: Training-Free, Dual Memory for Long-Term Video Object Segmentation
summary: SAM2Dual proposes a training-free, dual memory system to address error accumulation and drift in long-term video object segmentation (VOS). It enhances SAM2's performance by improving its memory mechanism for extended sequences.

title: Clinically Structured Surrogate Rewards for Post-SFT Medical Image Captioning
summary: This paper introduces clinically structured surrogate rewards for post-supervised fine-tuning (SFT) medical image captioning, optimizing for clinical accuracy. The method uses sequence-level policy optimization to ensure concise and clinically meaningful descriptions.

title: Dynamic SpectraFormer for Ultra-High-Definition Underwater Image Enhancement
summary: Dynamic SpectraFormer is presented as a specific AI model designed for ultra-high-definition underwater image enhancement. It aims to correct color distortion, haze, and poor visibility caused by light absorption in water.

title: Teeth2Point: A Two-Stage Dental CBCT ROI-to-Point Segmentation Framework
summary: Teeth2Point introduces a two-stage dental CBCT ROI-to-point segmentation framework designed for accurate tooth labeling, particularly for missing or malpositioned teeth. It leverages deep learning architectures to improve dental practice.

title: Vision-Language Models for Egocentric Video: From Hand-Object Interaction to Embodied AI
summary: This paper explores the application of Vision-Language Models to egocentric video, focusing on hand-object interaction and its implications for embodied AI. It highlights the growing importance of this perspective for wearable intelligence and human-robot interaction.

title: DynCur-Geo: Dynamic Curiosity Reward Shaping for Multimodal Active Geo-Localization
summary: DynCur-Geo proposes dynamic curiosity reward shaping for multimodal active geo-localization, enabling low-altitude UAVs to search for targets. This method addresses challenges like restricted views and sparse feedback in time-sensitive applications.

title: FRAGMENT: Factorized Graph Representations for Document Generation and Editing via Entity-Aware Transformations
summary: FRAGMENT introduces factorized graph representations and entity-aware transformations for structured document generation and editing. This method aims to better capture the interplay between spatial layout, textual content, and logical structure.

title: DocClaw: A Unified Agentic System for Intelligent Document Processing
summary: DocClaw presents a unified agentic system for intelligent document processing, encompassing tasks like OCR, document question answering, and key information extraction. This system aims to perceive and acquire knowledge from document content efficiently.

title: Composed Historical Image Retrieval by Modeling Temporal Representations
summary: This research proposes a method for composed historical image retrieval by modeling temporal representations within neural embedding spaces. It aims to improve retrieval performance by incorporating the linear progression of time.

title: Impact of Iterative Fine-Tuning on Transcription Accuracy in Complex Historical Sanskrit Manuscripts
summary: This research investigates the impact of iterative fine-tuning on improving transcription accuracy for digitizing complex historical Sanskrit manuscripts. It aims to make these texts more accessible for scholarly study.

title: A Critical Synthesis of Uncertainty Quantification and Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation
summary: This paper synthesizes uncertainty quantification methods for foundation models in semantic segmentation, addressing challenges like interpretability and overconfidence that are critical for safety-critical applications.

title: CamWorldQA: Perceptual Quality Assessment of Camera-Controlled World Video Generation
summary: This introduces CamWorldQA, a new method for perceptually assessing the quality of camera-controlled world video generation models, as existing video quality assessment methods are insufficient.

title: EgoHRV: Continuous Heart Rate Variability Estimation from Egocentric Systems for Autonomic Response and Skill Assessment
summary: This research proposes EgoHRV, a method for continuously estimating heart rate variability from egocentric vision systems to assess human autonomic responses like stress and engagement.

title: The Impact of CutMix on Reliability and Robustness in Semantic Segmentation
summary: This paper empirically studies the impact of the CutMix data augmentation strategy on the reliability and robustness of semantic segmentation models, particularly for safety-critical applications like autonomous driving.

title: A Few Cases Are All You Need: An Empirical Study of Annotation-Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning of MedSAM3
summary: This empirical study investigates the effectiveness of annotation-efficient LoRA fine-tuning of MedSAM3 for medical image segmentation, demonstrating strong performance with minimal labeled data.

title: CL4D: Contrastive Language-4D Pretraining for Vision-Language Reasoning in Dynamic Scenes
summary: This paper introduces CL4D, a contrastive language-4D pretraining framework designed to enhance vision-language reasoning capabilities for embodied AI agents operating in dynamic physical environments.

title: SED-FOD: Scattering-Aware Expert Decomposition for Few-Shot Cross-Sensor SAR Object Detection
summary: This research proposes SED-FOD, a scattering-aware expert decomposition method for improving few-shot cross-sensor object detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery by addressing data variations.

title: MIFR: A Modality-Invariant and Fair Representation Framework for Skin Disease Classification
summary: This paper introduces MIFR, a modality-invariant and fair representation framework designed for skin disease classification, aiming to improve diagnosis across different modalities and skin tones.

title: EfficientSync: Real-Time Lip Synchronization via Deformation-Based Reference Texture Mixing
summary: This paper introduces EfficientSync, a novel method for real-time audio-driven lip synchronization that uses deformation-based reference texture mixing for efficient and accurate mouth region manipulation.

title: EVADE: Evidence-Verified Agentic Diagnosis with Escape
summary: This paper introduces EVADE, an agentic system designed for medical diagnosis that incorporates evidence verification and an "escape" mechanism to improve reliability and calibrate trust in its responses.

title: RVLoss: Runoff Vote Loss for Self-Supervised LiDAR Scene Flow Estimation
summary: This research introduces RVLoss (Runoff Vote Loss), a novel loss function for self-supervised LiDAR scene flow estimation that addresses limitations of traditional nearest-neighbor approaches.

title: Revisiting the "Push-T" Robot Manipulation Task with Agentic Robotics
summary: This paper revisits the "Push-T" robot manipulation task by applying concepts from Agentic Robotics, utilizing large language models to approach the problem.

title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Whole-Body Control with Environment Interaction
summary: This research introduces GigaBrain-WBC-0.5, a behavior world model designed for robust whole-body control of humanoids, enabling them to interact effectively with complex environments.

title: GAPL: Grounded Action-effect Policy Learning for LLM-Based Trajectory Planning
summary: This paper proposes GAPL, a framework for Grounded Action-effect Policy Learning that enhances LLM-based trajectory planning for autonomous driving by mitigating hallucinations and improving environmental grounding.

title: GuideFetch: A Task Coordination Framework for Concurrent Navigation and Object Retrieval in Assistive Robot Dogs
summary: This paper introduces GuideFetch, a task coordination framework enabling assistive robot dogs to concurrently perform navigation and object retrieval for users.

title: The Embodiment Gap in Robot Foundation Models
summary: This paper discusses the "embodiment gap" in Robot Foundation Models and vision-language-action policies, highlighting the challenges in achieving generalization and practical deployment on physical robots.

title: HarvestPoint-ACT: Explicit Target Selection and Harvest-Point Conditioning for Robotic Fruit Harvesting under Occlusion
summary: This paper introduces HarvestPoint-ACT, a method for robotic fruit harvesting that explicitly improves target selection and harvest-point conditioning, enabling more robust grasping under occlusion.

title: Backward Layout Search for Sequence-Constrained Robotic Assembly
summary: This research focuses on robotic assembly layout planning, proposing a backward search method to determine part poses and ensure collision-free execution of assembly sequences.

title: DevGRU: Depth-guided Visual Navigation using a Collision-aware Recurrent Model
summary: This research presents DevGRU, a depth-guided visual navigation model designed to help robots avoid collisions in complex indoor environments. It aims to improve robot navigation, particularly in structured layouts and narrow passages.

title: LabDex: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Dexterous Manipulation in Laboratories
summary: LabDex is introduced as a hierarchical benchmark for evaluating robots' dexterous manipulation capabilities in laboratory settings. It aims to assess how well robots can handle diverse labware and execute complex experimental procedures.

title: Progressive Experience Fusion for Multi-Task World Model Control in Endovascular Navigation
summary: This study investigates Progressive Experience Fusion (PEF) to train a multi-task controller for autonomous endovascular navigation in robotic systems. The goal is to support the delivery of mechanical thrombectomy across varying vascular anatomies.

title: Orienteering Problem with Uncertain Time-Varying Rewards: Framework and Benchmark for Everyday Service Robotics
summary: This work introduces the orienteering problem with uncertain time-varying rewards (OP-UTVR), a novel variant for service robotics applications. It presents a framework and benchmark to address scenarios where rewards change dynamically.

title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
summary: SoftVTBench is presented as a deformation-aware visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for evaluating deformable-object manipulation by robots. It addresses the need for assessing interaction quality beyond mere task success, considering factors like slip and compression.

title: Dream2Reward: Transition-Alignment Reward Models from Positive Demonstrations for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Dream2Reward introduces a method for generating transition-alignment reward models from positive demonstrations to improve robotic manipulation learning. This approach aims to provide informative rewards even when robot behavior deviates from successful trajectories.

title: Beyond Placement and Articulation: Usage-Driven Code Scenes for Embodied Interaction
summary: This research explores "usage-driven code scenes" for embodied AI and robotic manipulation, moving beyond simple visual construction. It focuses on creating editable and extensible environments for simulation-based policy learning.

title: RoboEdit: Turning Human Manipulation Videos into Scalable Robot Experience
summary: RoboEdit is a human-to-robot video editing suite designed to transform human manipulation videos into physically plausible robot experiences. This tool aims to make abundant human demonstration data usable for robot training, which is typically costly to collect directly.

title: Autonomous Agricultural Tractor: Integrated Weed Detection and LiDAR Navigation for Precision Paddy Farming
summary: This research focuses on an autonomous agricultural tractor integrating weed detection and LiDAR navigation for precision paddy farming. It addresses challenges like robust navigation under canopy and real-time visual discrimination of weeds for site-specific management.

title: LT-Mem: Volatility-Aware Spatio-Temporal Memory for Lifelong Scene Understanding
summary: LT-Mem introduces a volatility-aware spatio-temporal memory system designed for lifelong scene understanding in robots. It enables persistent object-level understanding across repeated revisits to evolving environments, maintaining consistent cross-session object identity.

title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models
summary: DA-WAM focuses on creating decision-aligned future latents for driving world models to enhance autonomous driving. The goal is to ensure that future predictions are not just accurate but also directly informative for decision-making in evolving road scenarios.

title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning
summary: ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework introduced for achieving sim-to-real transferable dexterity in high degree-of-freedom robots. It enables robots to solve long-horizon tasks using raw visuo-tactile perception.

title: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Local Geometry for Bimanual Grasping from Partial Views
summary: PartialBiGrasp focuses on inferring hidden local geometry to enable bimanual robotic grasping from partial views. This research addresses the challenge of manipulating large, geometrically complex objects with dual-arm robots.

title: Multimodal Rapport Estimation in Real-World HRI
summary: This research investigates multimodal rapport estimation in real-world Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) to evaluate interaction quality. The goal is to use these estimations to improve robot dialogue strategies and enable autonomous behavior adaptation.

title: Engineering Psychological Safety in Autonomous Vehicles: A Systems-Theoretic Framework for Psychological Safety in Autonomous Vehicles and its Validation in Real-World Scenarios
summary: This work proposes a systems-theoretic framework for engineering psychological safety in autonomous vehicles (AVs) and validates it in real-world scenarios. It addresses psychological barriers like trust and perceived safety that limit societal acceptability of AVs.

title: Personalized Autonomous Driving via Optimal Control with Clearance Constraints from Questionnaires
summary: This research proposes a planning framework for personalized autonomous driving that incorporates user preferences for safe clearance from surrounding vehicles. It aims to enhance user comfort by explicitly considering individual desired separation distances.

title: Communications-Aware NMPC for Multi-Rotor Aerial Relay Networks Under Jamming Interference
summary: This research focuses on communications-aware Non-linear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) for multi-rotor aerial relay networks operating under jamming interference. It addresses the challenge of maintaining connectivity and optimizing motion for drones in critical missions.

title: Lexicographic Minimum-Violation Motion Planning using Signal Temporal Logic
summary: This work presents a lexicographic minimum-violation motion planning approach using Signal Temporal Logic for autonomous vehicles. It addresses scenarios where not all specifications can be met simultaneously, aiming to minimize specification violations.

title: Mask2Real-WM: Segmentation Masks as a Sim-to-Real Bridge for Controllable Dexterous World Models
summary: Introduces Mask2Real-WM, a two-stage action-conditioned world model designed to bridge simulation to real-world applications for controllable dexterous robotic manipulation. It allows robots to predict action consequences and aids in policy evaluation and planning.

title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
summary: Describes the development of a system for the semi-humanoid robot NICO to imitate human arm gestures, aiming to improve human-robot interaction.

title: Multimodal Adaptive Control for Safe Robotic Craniotomy Under Partial Observability
summary: Presents a multimodal adaptive control system for safe autonomous robotic craniotomy, designed to regulate tool-tissue interactions under partial observability to prevent damage and maintain surgical efficiency.

title: Neurosymbolic Embodied Agents
summary: Introduces a neurosymbolic embodied agent designed to factor long-horizon household tasks, aiming to address the executability issues of plans generated by language and vision-language models.

title: Breaking Planner Integrity Boundary: Enviroment State-Text Injection Attack on LLM-Driven Embodied Agents
summary: Describes an "Environment State-Text Injection Attack" that targets LLM-driven embodied agents by manipulating their planner-visible state representations, highlighting a critical security boundary.

title: It used to be our imperfect bodies that made us insecure. With AI, it’s our minds as well
summary: A philosophical reflection on how AI's advancements are shifting human insecurities from physical imperfections to mental capabilities, noting a societal trend of humans increasingly imitating technology.

title: Just How Useful Are Human-Looking Robots? Very, Unitree Robotics Investors Hope - The Daily Upside

summary: This research focuses on developing an automatic named entity recognition (NER) system to systematically identify and extract mentions of bioinformatics software and databases from scientific literature, addressing the current challenges in cataloging these resources.

title: Asymmetric Attention Heads: Structured Head-Wise Context Allocation for Transformer Attention
summary: This paper proposes a new method called "Asymmetric Attention Heads" for transformer attention, which enables structured, head-wise context allocation to improve how different attention heads process varying contextual information.

title: Hallucination as a Feature, not a Defect: Evaluating a multi-agent architecture to transform speculative language-model outputs into testable scientific hypotheses
summary: This research evaluates a multi-agent architecture designed to transform speculative language model "hallucinations" into testable scientific hypotheses, exploring how to leverage combinatorial creativity rather than solely suppressing it for factual retrieval.

title: Compliance, Capability, and Conflict: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs under System Messages
summary: This paper addresses the lack of evaluation for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) adherence to system messages by proposing a new benchmarking approach to assess their compliance and capabilities in multimodal contexts.

title: When Irrelevant Text Matters: Affine Margin Shifts in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper investigates the impact of task-irrelevant auxiliary textual context on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during visually grounded tasks, exploring how such context influences model behavior through "affine margin shifts."

title: Represented but Ignored: A Causal Account of Prosodic Underuse in Audio-Language Models
summary: This research provides a causal analysis of "prosodic underuse" in audio-language models, explaining why these models often fail to fully leverage the linguistic and emotional information conveyed by speech prosody.

title: NepOOC-M: Bilingual Nepali-English Benchmark and Comparative Analysis of Multimodal Architectures for OOC Detection
summary: This paper introduces NepOOC-M, a new bilingual Nepali-English benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal architectures for detecting out-of-context misinformation, where authentic images are paired with misleading captions.

title: Time-Series Retrieval for Grounding Multimodal Language Models in Remaining Useful Life
summary: This research explores the use of time-series retrieval methods to ground Multimodal Language Models (MLLMs) for domain-specific maintenance and prognostics tasks, particularly focusing on predicting remaining useful life (RUL).

title: Can Conversational AI loosen Us-Versus-Them Boundaries? The Effects of Common, Dual, and Separate Identity Framings on Pro-Immigrant Intergroup Helping
summary: This preregistered experiment investigates whether conversational AI can reduce intergroup tensions and promote pro-immigrant helping behavior by studying the effects of common, dual, and separate identity framings on majority-group members.

title: A Speech Corpus for Mizo Automatic Speech Recognition: Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 Fine-Tuning with Morphology-Aware Evaluation
summary: This study reports on the development of an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system for Mizo, a low-resource language, through the creation of a dedicated speech corpus and fine-tuning of Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 multilingual models.

title: Linguistic Holonomy and Statistical Watermarks: Inner Geometry of Meaning-Preserving Transformations
summary: This paper explores the theoretical properties of statistical watermarks for language models, focusing on how meaning-preserving transformations can erode them by altering text form while maintaining content.

title: Are LLMs becoming similarly creative? Evidence from three years of models
summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming similarly creative over time by examining their performance on open-ended tasks, where creativity, originality, and diversity are crucial, contrasting with tasks with verifiable answers.

title: Hear2Act: Benchmarking When Prosody Should Change What an Assistant Does
summary: This paper introduces a new benchmarking approach to evaluate how AI assistants should interpret and respond to prosodic cues in task-oriented dialogue, considering perception, response appropriateness, and task outcomes.

title: Automated Summarization of Financial News Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: An Early Empirical Study (Fall 2023)
summary: This empirical study explores the use of Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for automated summarization of financial news to aid stock market analysts and investors.

title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a unified generative framework for integrating machine-native symbols into pretrained Large Language Models, enabling them to process structured information beyond natural language tokens.

title: Generating Diverse Personas for User Simulators to Test Interview Dialogue Systems
summary: This paper introduces a method for generating diverse user personas for simulators to efficiently test interview dialogue systems, reducing the labor and cost associated with human-based evaluation.

title: Reliable Financial Named Entity Recognition under Domain Shift
summary: This study investigates reliable financial Named Entity Recognition under domain shift, focusing on confidence estimation methods to ensure safe automation when AI systems encounter varying input distributions.

title: Remember, Verify, or Ask? Cross-Family Evaluation of Memory Commitment in LLM Agents
summary: This research evaluates memory commitment in LLM agents, exploring how interaction-derived information should be handled – whether persisted, used contextually, re-verified, or clarified with the user, to avoid distorting future behavior.

title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
summary: This paper presents a method for efficiently estimating uncertainty dynamics in LLM text generation by analyzing the distribution of reasoning chains using resampling-based analyses.

title: Mitigating Identity Essentialism in LLM Agents with Longitudinal Life Trajectories
summary: This research proposes using longitudinal life trajectories to mitigate identity essentialism in LLM agents, enhancing their ability to capture human-like diversity in social simulations.

title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces ReCache, a framework designed for efficient key-value (KV) cache reuse and compression in tool-augmented LLM agents, optimizing the handling of recurring tool and skill schemas.

title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
summary: This work systematically evaluates the asymmetric harms of Large Language Model (LLM) compression, revealing behavioral shifts often masked by standard aggregate metrics like perplexity and accuracy.

title: Projector Is All You Train
summary: This research investigates whether fine-tuning the language model backbone of a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is necessary when adapting it to new modalities, suggesting that focusing on the projector might suffice.

title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
summary: This paper introduces Thinkingbox, a sandbox and benchmark designed to evaluate the reliability and performance of AI agents in complex stateful business workflows beyond simple task completion.

title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization
summary: This paper introduces PersonalBench, a new benchmark designed to measure the authorship gap in LLM personalization by evaluating how closely a model's output matches a target author's writing style.

title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
summary: This paper introduces FlashPrefill V2, a block-sparse prefill attention mechanism designed to optimize long-context serving for Large Language Models by mitigating the quadratic complexity bottleneck during the prefilling phase.

title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
summary: This research introduces SWE-bench Science, an evaluation framework designed to assess the capability of coding agents in resolving engineering tasks specifically within scientific contexts.

title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment
summary: This paper introduces LoRA-GA$^2$, an enhanced Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning method that utilizes multi-step gradient adaptive alignment to further reduce the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning for large models.

title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels
summary: This research focuses on optimizing LLM evaluation pipelines by developing strategies for stopping and routing LLM judge panels, determining which judges to use for specific examples and tasks.

title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
summary: This paper introduces a knowledge-guided agentic framework designed to mitigate patient-context ambiguity in health queries, enabling healthcare chatbots to provide more appropriate responses to underspecified patient requests.

title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
summary: This research explores how periodic subject changes influence novelty, surprise, and connection in base language models by analyzing a cognitively inspired generation loop.

title: Learning how to Forget: Fine-tuning for Long-Context Sparse Attention
summary: This paper introduces a new fine-tuning method for transformer language models that enables long-context sparse attention, optimizing key-value (KV) cache selection and compression for more efficient inference.

title: Dynamic Gated Cross-Modal Fusion with Sarcastic-aware Contrastive Regularization for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
summary: This research proposes a dynamic gated cross-modal fusion method with sarcastic-aware contrastive regularization to improve multimodal sarcasm detection, addressing challenges with instance-dependent inconsistencies. The method aims to better identify ironic intent from multimodal content.

title: Natural Language Code Retrieval for 1C:Enterprise: An Open Benchmark and Efficient Bi-Encoder
summary: This paper introduces an open benchmark and an efficient bi-encoder for natural language code retrieval within the 1C:Enterprise ecosystem, which previously lacked open datasets and specialized models. It aims to address the challenges of Russian syntax and domain-specific terminology in this task.

title: Robust Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis via Iterative Proxy Correction
summary: This research proposes an iterative proxy correction method for robust incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis, aiming to mitigate the issues caused by missing or corrupted multimodal inputs. The approach addresses the weakening of cross-modal complementarity and misleading information in such scenarios.

title: HealMed: Multilingual Evaluation of Large Language Models in Medicine
summary: HealMed is presented as an expert-reviewed benchmark for the multilingual evaluation of large language models in medicine, featuring 1,000 examples across nine languages and three task formats. It was developed over two years to assess LLM performance in a medical context.

title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking
summary: This research audits cross-lingual fairness in language model watermarking, highlighting how current evaluation methods, primarily focused on English text, fail to adequately assess performance in multilingual deployments. It discusses the impact of evaluation-design choices on determining conclusive results for such schemes.

title: SABET-QA: Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
summary: SABET-QA is introduced as a framework for Question Answering over Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGQA) that iteratively refines reasoning states across multiple hops. It aims to address the limitations of existing embedding-based methods that struggle with multi-step queries.

title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models
summary: OenoBench is introduced as a wine-domain knowledge benchmark of 3,266 multiple-choice questions across six pillars and four difficulty tiers for evaluating Large Language Models. The corpus is built from 38,104 atomic, source-anchored facts.

title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models arbitrate between conflicting evidence from textual summaries, numerical observations, and external tool outputs when making decisions. A controlled synthesis setup is introduced to study this evidence arbitration process.

title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
summary: FormalTCS is presented as an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models on frontier, end-to-end Theoretical Computer Science research, addressing the gap between existing benchmarks and realistic research settings. It aims to assess LLMs' potential in automated TCS research.

title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
summary: Task-CoEvolve proposes a novel approach for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) agent harness optimization through adaptive validation task selection. This method iteratively rewrites harness code based on validation performance to achieve substantial performance gains.

title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
summary: This research introduces "Inject, Align, Recover," a staged post-training method for retrieval-free document knowledge internalization in Large Language Models. It aims to convert a fixed corpus into usable parametric knowledge, allowing LLMs to answer questions about it without explicit retrieval at inference time.

title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
summary: G-CARL proposes a Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning approach for patient-oriented medical report interpretation, addressing the need for both evidence-grounded medical factuality and context-dependent patient communication. It aims to improve personalized interpretation of medical reports.

title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
summary: ConceptGuard introduces a benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive unlearning in Large Language Models, which assesses their ability to selectively remove harmful or sensitive knowledge. It addresses limitations of existing methods that rely on disjoint forget and retain sets.

title: HARP: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion for Query-Based CVE Prioritization
summary: HARP proposes a Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion method for query-based CVE prioritization, addressing the challenge that vulnerability prioritization is inherently preference-dependent. It aims to provide flexible ranking unlike existing fixed-criterion methods.

title: Measuring What a Specification Determines: A Formal Semantic-Block Model and an Execution-Judged Benchmark
summary: This work introduces a formal semantic-block model for specifications and an execution-judged benchmark to evaluate specification quality independently of model capability. It represents a specification as a structure of semantic blocks, dependency relations, and rules.

title: Does Listening Matter? Backchanneling and Nodding in AI Clone
summary: This research investigates whether integrating multimodal listening behaviors, such as verbal backchannels and head nodding, can enhance the presence and authenticity of AI clones. It explores how these behaviors, typically absent, could improve human-like interaction.

title: PEA-DPO: Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization for MLLMs Alignment
summary: PEA-DPO introduces a Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization method for aligning Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with human preferences. It aims to address a key limitation in multimodal preference optimization identified through representational analysis.

title: StreamSoccer: Event-Driven Memory for Streaming Soccer Commentary
summary: StreamSoccer proposes an event-driven memory system for streaming soccer commentary, designed to causally update its state as video arrives and organize growing history into semantic units. It allows for recalling information under bounded computation and memory constraints.

title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
summary: TempJail introduces a novel temporal jailbreak attack against Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) that leverages subtitle scheduling. This research explores video-based jailbreaks, a relatively unexplored area compared to text and image-based attacks.

title: Clustering and Token Denoising for Faster and More Robust VLMs
summary: This research proposes clustering and token denoising techniques to make Visual-Language Models (VLMs) faster and more robust, particularly addressing the computational burden of processing visual tokens. The goal is to facilitate edge deployment of models like LLaVA.

title: SceneGTMM: A Conformal Mapping-based Scene-Aware Transferable GNN-Transformer Dual-Graph Interaction Framework for Map Matching
summary: This paper introduces SceneGTMM, a GNN-Transformer framework for map matching that addresses challenges in noise robustness, cross-regional transfer, and interpretability using a conformal mapping-based approach.

title: Does Marginal Coverage Guarantee Class-Conditional Safety for Zero-Shot VLMs Under Shift?
summary: This research audits whether marginal coverage guarantees class-conditional safety for zero-shot Vision-Language Models (VLMs) under deployment shift, evaluating techniques like split-conformal prediction for models like CLIP.

title: CAViAR: A Causal Video Dataset for Fine-Grained Accident Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios
summary: This paper introduces CAViAR, a new causal video dataset designed to facilitate fine-grained accident reasoning in real-world scenarios, aiming to improve autonomous driving systems' ability to interpret traffic accidents.

title: Beyond Recognition: Compact Multi-Domain Arabic Manuscript HTR with Candidate-Selection Analysis and Evidence-Preserving Review
summary: This research presents Phoenix, a compact multi-domain system for historical Arabic manuscript transcription that goes beyond simple recognition to preserve uncertain readings and distinguish visual evidence from linguistic plausibility.

title: HiRA-CAM: Preserving Fine-Grained Spatial Relevance in Gradient-Based Visual Explanations
summary: This paper introduces HiRA-CAM, a method designed to improve the interpretability of deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks, by preserving fine-grained spatial relevance in gradient-based visual explanations.

title: VideoRun2D Demo: Markerless Body Tracking for Biomechanical Analysis of Running
summary: This demo showcases VideoRun2D, a markerless body tracking system for biomechanical analysis of running, utilizing advancements in deep learning for human pose estimation with applications in sports analysis.

title: A Plug-in Interpretation of Conditioning in Score-Based Diffusion Models
summary: This research proposes a novel plug-in conditioning mechanism for score-based diffusion models, using multi-speed joint diffusion to enforce conditioning at inference time via a correction term.

title: CVSD-Reg: Cross-Modal Visual Semantic Prior Distillation for Robust LiDAR Registration
summary: This paper proposes CVSD-Reg, a new method for robust global LiDAR registration that uses cross-modal visual semantic prior distillation to overcome the sensitivity of existing learning-based methods to variations in point cloud characteristics.

title: Where Grounding Accuracy Lives on the IoU Curve: Label-Free Inference-Time Boundary Refinement
summary: This research investigates label-free inference-time boundary refinement for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), exploring how a frozen model can use its own predictions to improve the precision of bounding boxes without needing target annotations.

title: Stream4D: 4D-Consistency for Streaming Autoregressive Diffusion Video Models
summary: This paper introduces Stream4D, a method to improve 4D-consistency in streaming autoregressive diffusion video models, addressing issues like geometric drift and unnatural motion in long-horizon video generation.

title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces Block3D, a method for efficient text-to-3D generation that uses block-wise diffusion to achieve high geometric fidelity at a lower inference cost.

title: VGI-BENCH: Probing Visual Intelligence in Video Generation Models
summary: This paper introduces VGI-BENCH, a new benchmark designed to reliably evaluate the visual intelligence and zero-shot visual reasoning capabilities of video generation models.

title: TextRefine: Improving Textual Fidelity, Spatial Placement, and Glyph Rendering for Text Editing in Product Posters
summary: This paper proposes TextRefine, a method aimed at improving text editing in product posters by enhancing textual fidelity, spatial placement, and glyph rendering, addressing limitations of general-purpose image editing models.

title: When Guidance Goes Off-Scale: Recalibrating Diffusion Transformers under Analog Compute-in-Memory Nonidealities
summary: This research investigates recalibrating Diffusion Transformers to function effectively with analog compute-in-memory (CIM), aiming to reduce memory traffic and energy costs by addressing non-idealities inherent in CIM hardware.

title: PL-NBA: A Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset Supporting Multiple Visual Understanding Tasks
summary: This paper introduces PL-NBA, a new possession-level universal basketball video dataset designed to support multiple visual understanding tasks and address limitations of existing datasets in preserving temporal continuity of game events.

title: MUST-PET: MUltimodal Self-supervised learning across Tracers for whole-body PET/CT-based lesion segmentation
summary: This research introduces MUST-PET, a multimodal self-supervised learning method across tracers for whole-body PET/CT-based lesion segmentation, addressing generalization limitations due to scarce annotations in cancer applications.

title: Scaffolding Minds: Optimizing Latent Visual Target Representations for Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a two-stage training paradigm for optimizing latent visual target representations to enhance multimodal reasoning, involving encoding helper images into latent tokens and refining them with reward feedback.

title: RIPE++: Reinforced Keypoint Learning from Positive Pairs Only
summary: This paper introduces RIPE++, a method for reinforced keypoint learning that utilizes only positive pairs, addressing challenges in sparse keypoint extraction and matching for geometric computer vision tasks.

title: Robust Cross-Modal Foundation Model Perception for Underwater Robots under Degraded Visual Conditions
summary: This research explores robust cross-modal foundation model perception for underwater robots, aiming to improve their ability to operate in degraded visual conditions by integrating information from various sensors like sonar.

title: Scale-Separated Conditioning for Style-Encoder-Free Diffusion Stylization
summary: This paper proposes Scale-Separated Conditioning, a method for style-encoder-free diffusion stylization that aims to separate target geometry from transferable appearance in reference-based stylization.

title: Learning to Beat: Phenotype-Guided Latent Flow with Regional Motion Priors for Biventricular Motion Synthesis
summary: Focuses on synthesizing full-cycle 3D+t biventricular motion from end-diastolic anatomy using a phenotype-guided latent flow for cardiac function analysis.

title: Question-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Multimodal Visual Question Answering
summary: Develops a question-guided evidence acquisition method to improve multimodal LLMs' reliability in reading documents for Visual Question Answering.

title: Gallileo-4D: Frozen Backbone Ensemble for Dynamic 4D Reconstruction
summary: Describes an entry to the PhysAI Dynamic 4D Reconstruction Challenge, which placed third on the leaderboard using a frozen backbone ensemble.

title: Towards Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning via Enhanced Vision-Language Alignment
summary: Explores enhanced vision-language alignment for medical image captioning to achieve clinically faithful descriptions and improve diagnostic workflows.

title: A 360-Degree Vision Dataset for Learning Yaw Control on GPS-Denied Micro-UAVs in Disaster-Response-Relevant Environments
summary: Presents a data-driven approach using 360-degree vision for learning yaw control on micro-drones in GPS-denied indoor disaster-response environments.

title: DIFFCZSL: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning Regularized by Diffusion Representations
summary: Introduces DIFFCZSL, a method for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning that uses diffusion representations to regularize the recognition of unseen attribute-object compositions.

title: Unified and Efficient Point-Line Local Features
summary: Proposes a unified and efficient method for point-line local features to improve multi-view computer vision pipelines for matching and pose estimation.

title: AvatarDynamizer: From Static to Dynamic Human Avatars via Generative Dynamic Textures
summary: Presents AvatarDynamizer, a method that generates dynamic human avatars from static inputs using generative dynamic textures to achieve perceptual realism.

title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging
summary: Applies flow matching techniques for 3D curvilinear structure segmentation in medical imaging, addressing challenges like complex topology and weak contrast.

title: Open-Vocabulary 3D Object Detection with Co-Distillation Discovery and Dual Guidance Robust Training
summary: Proposes a new method for open-vocabulary 3D object detection using co-distillation discovery and dual guidance robust training to detect unseen objects in 3D scenes.

title: From Street View Imagery to Street Quality Indicators: Vision Language Inference for the Suburban 15-minute City
summary: Applies vision-language inference to Street View imagery to derive street quality indicators for urban planning, particularly for the 15-minute city concept.

title: V-REX: Efficient Specialist VLM Training for Veterinary X-Rays
summary: Introduces V-REX, an efficient specialist Vision-Language Model training approach for veterinary X-Rays, challenging assumptions about fine-tuning large foundation models.

title: HandMvNet: Real-Time 3D Hand Pose Estimation Using Multi-View Cross-Attention Fusion
summary: Presents HandMvNet, a real-time method for 3D hand pose and shape estimation from multi-view camera images using cross-attention fusion.

title: BeyondMasks: Evaluating Causal and Physical Consistency in Video Object Removal
summary: Proposes new evaluation protocols for video object removal, focusing on causal and physical consistency beyond traditional masked region fidelity in generative video models.

title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation
summary: Introduces ArmorOCR, a method using observation-transferred self-distillation to enhance large multimodal models' robustness against adversarial visual text for OCR.

title: ID-VTG: Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding
summary: Presents ID-VTG, a method for Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding that addresses challenges in distinguishing visually similar events with natural language queries.

title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training
summary: Investigates feature evolution and migration in Vision Transformers during training by visualizing changes across network depth and training time.

title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: Introduces DPC-Net, a Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration designed to handle diverse image degradations within a unified model.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study
summary: Develops and validates an AI-powered tool for workflow analysis in minimally invasive colorectal surgeries using video-based assessment to improve outcomes.

title: G3Ego: Gaze-Guided Graphs for Egocentric Action Understanding
summary: Proposes G3Ego, a graph-based framework using gaze-guided graphs for egocentric action understanding, focusing on hand-object interactions in first-person videos.

title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces RoMAN-Flow, a method using autoregressive normalizing flows for offline reinforcement learning to improve robot policies in robotic manipulation tasks.

title: Unwarping the Lens: A Physics-Grounded Approach to Video Glasses Removal
summary: This research presents a physics-grounded approach to remove eyeglasses from video, addressing complex refractive distortions and reflections using large-scale generative priors.

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes a prompt-conditioned channel attention method for hierarchical feature modulation, aiming to improve anatomically plausible segmentation despite low contrast and ambiguous boundaries.

title: Ultra-High-Definition Restoration Transformers with Correlation Matching Transformation
summary: This work introduces UHDformer++, a general Transformer-based framework designed for Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) image restoration tasks, operating across high and low-resolution learning spaces.

title: APPROVE: Visual End-User-in-the-Loop Robot Programming with LLMs
summary: The APPROVE system enables non-experts to program robots using Large Language Models (LLMs) and visual feedback, simplifying the creation of robot programs from natural language.

title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
summary: This research explores how spatially distributed tactile feedback can improve robotic teleoperation, bringing it closer to human dexterity for controlling remote robots.

title: Learning the Right Abstraction: Neural Reduced Dynamics for Complex Robot Control
summary: This work advocates for using neural reduced dynamics in less accurate but faster simulations to facilitate large-scale reinforcement learning for complex robot control in embodied AI.

title: SCAPE: Scenario-Conditioned Simulation-Augmented Policy Evaluation
summary: SCAPE is presented as a method for scenario-conditioned simulation-augmented policy evaluation, aiming to reliably assess robot-learning policies by bridging the sim-to-real gap.

title: Hybrid Feedback Sampling for Sample-Efficient Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper proposes Hybrid Feedback Sampling to improve the sample efficiency of Model Predictive Control (MPC) for real-world robotic systems, particularly for high-dimensional and unstable dynamics.

title: When Automata Meet Streams: Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning
summary: This research introduces Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning, integrating symbolic planning with continuous parameters for executing long-horizon robot tasks.

title: Fine-Tuning VLAs with Self-Demonstrated Generative Control for Multi-Task Manipulation
summary: This study addresses fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for multi-task robot manipulation, mitigating performance drops caused by hardware mismatches through self-demonstrated generative control.

title: LF-GICP: Parameter-Free Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR Odometry via a Voxel-Normal Localizability Field
summary: LF-GICP is a parameter-free LiDAR odometry method designed to handle geometrically degenerate environments like tunnels, improving localizability by using a voxel-normal localizability field.

title: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Surface Vehicles using Turning Circle-based Control Barrier Functions
summary: This paper presents a guide path-free multimodal trajectory planning framework for autonomous surface vehicles operating in dynamic environments, integrating Model Predictive Control with control barrier functions.

title: OrthoSkillVLA: Continual Skill Learning via Gradient-Informed Skill Subspace Adaptation
summary: OrthoSkillVLA enables continual skill learning for robot learning using Vision-Language-Action models, adapting skill subspaces to prevent catastrophic forgetting when learning diverse tasks.

title: The Verification Gap in Networked Physical AI: A Post-Semantic Communication Framework
summary: This paper introduces the 'verification gap' in networked Physical AI, where AI proposals may lack justification for physical action, and proposes a Post-Semantic Communication Framework to address it.

title: What Matters for Latent Actions in Robot Learning
summary: This research investigates the role of Latent Action Models (LAMs) in robot learning, utilizing latent actions as compact representations derived from large-scale unlabeled videos.

title: World-Model-Grounded LLM Planning for AUV and ASV Navigation Near Offshore Wind Farms
summary: This work explores using a world model to ground LLM planning for Autonomous Underwater (AUV) and Surface Vehicles (ASV) navigation near offshore wind farms, giving LLMs a sense of physics.

title: GOAG: Generative and Object-Agnostic Grasp Planner for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
summary: GOAG is a generative and object-agnostic grasp planner introduced for dexterous robotic manipulation, designed to generalize grasping capabilities to new and unknown objects.

title: CoToGrasp: Contact-Topology-Conditioned Dexterous Grasp Synthesis via Canonical Workspace Learning
summary: CoToGrasp proposes a method for contact-topology-conditioned dexterous grasp synthesis, focusing on generating grasps that support specific functional tasks rather than just physical stability.

title: MILD: Tractable Terrain Modeling for Learning Improved Bipedal Locomotion on Deformable Surfaces
summary: MILD offers a tractable terrain modeling approach to improve bipedal robot locomotion on deformable surfaces, overcoming limitations of current simulators in capturing complex terrain properties.

title: PVRA: A Pointwise Key-point Voting Framework for Robotic Assembly
summary: Introduces PVRA, a computer vision framework that enables robots to perform autonomous manipulation for progressive assembly tasks by perceiving objects and their key-points.

title: Learning Highly Dynamic Skills Transition for Quadruped Jumping Through Constrained Space
summary: Proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning pipeline that allows quadrupedal robots to perform dynamic jumping and locomotion through confined spaces, mimicking animal behavior.

title: Evidence-Gated Task and Motion Planning with Vision-Language Models
summary: Discusses a method for robots to execute long-horizon manipulation tasks from natural language instructions, reasoning about task structure and feasibility even under partial observability using Vision-Language Models.

title: Towards Professional Tennis Styles for Humanoid Robots with Adaptive Motion Planning and Tracking
summary: Presents AdaPT, an Adaptive Motion Planning and Tracking framework, to enable humanoid robots to achieve professional tennis motion styles while maintaining strong task performance.

title: Planning-Oriented End-to-End Autonomous Driving: Architectures, Evaluation, and Emerging Paradigms
summary: A survey reviewing the evolution of end-to-end autonomous driving systems from simple camera-to-control regression to planning-oriented approaches with structured representations and realistic evaluation.

title: Video2DoorTraversal: Push Door Traversal via Simulated Door Twins
summary: Introduces Video2DoorTraversal, a framework for wheel-legged mobile manipulators to learn door opening and traversal from a single RGB video using a real-to-sim-to-real approach.

title: Multi-Tool Robotics Enables In-Situ Sample Manipulation for Time-Resolved Synchrotron Measurements
summary: Describes how multi-tool robotics can enable in-situ sample manipulation during X-ray experiments at synchrotron beamlines, overcoming radiation safety protocols and allowing for continuous data acquisition.

title: Wave-Based Bilateral Teleoperation between Nonlinear Manipulators with Direct Contact Force Feedback
summary: Explores wave-based bilateral teleoperation for nonlinear, multi-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulators, focusing on direct contact force feedback despite constant communication delays.

title: DiffDef: A Diffusion Model for Generating Multimodal Goal Shapes From Demonstrations for Deformable Object Manipulation
summary: Introduces DiffDef, a diffusion model designed to generate multimodal goal shapes from demonstrations, facilitating the manipulation of deformable objects through shape servoing.

title: SUM-AgriVLN: Spatial Understanding Memory for Agricultural Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Presents SUM-AgriVLN, a method incorporating Spatial Understanding Memory, to enhance agricultural robots' ability in Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) for autonomous tasks.

title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach for UAV Path Planning in Dynamic Environments
